Taking down Hogger requires venture into deeply hostile gnoll territory, and his ferocity has earned him a reputation as the deadliest threat facing novice adventurers in Elwynn.

quest:179.text: Dwarven Outfitters. Dwarven Outfitters is an introductory survival task in Coldridge Valley offered by Sten Stoutarm. In exchange for culling local wolves and gathering their tough meat for winter rations, fresh recruits are rewarded with sturdy gloves to ward off frostbite in Dun Morogh's biting cold. The high mountain pass of Coldridge Valley is brutally cold, and unprepared travelers quickly learn that standard kit is no match for the elements. Standing outside Anvilmar, Sten Stoutarm offers a straightforward frontier bargain to new recruits: venture into the snowy drifts, hunt down the prowling wolves, and bring back cuts of tough meat to help supply the outpost. In return, he provides proper cold-weather gloves to ensure young adventurers keep all ten fingers. While wolves represent a perpetual hazard to dwarven scouts and fledgling gnomes training in the valley, they are also a vital resource. Their meat sustains the garrison stationed at Anvilmar, and culling their numbers keeps the paths between the local encampments somewhat safer. Stoutarm's arrangement serves a double purpose—testing a recruit's ability to handle the local wildlife while stockpiling food for the bitter nights ahead.

quest:18.text: Brotherhood of Thieves. Brotherhood of Thieves is an early task assigned by Deputy Willem outside Northshire Abbey. It directs young Alliance recruits across the eastern river to push back an encroaching band of brigands known as the Defias Brotherhood. Collecting the thieves' signature red burlap bandanas provides Stormwind authorities their first tangible evidence of the group's organized presence in the valley. Northshire Valley has long been considered a safe haven within Elwynn Forest, protected by Stormwind guards and dedicated to training new recruits and Clerics of the Holy Light. Recently, however, discipline around the perimeter has frayed. Vagrants and thieves have crossed the eastern river, lurking near the woods and setting up small camps right under the abbey's nose. Deputy Willem, tasked with maintaining local order, recognizes that the local guard cannot spare the manpower to police every corner of the valley without volunteer aid. What sets these outlaws apart from common highwaymen is their coordination and uniform attire. They call themselves the Defias Brotherhood, marking their allegiance with distinctive red burlap bandanas tied over their faces. By ordering recruits to hunt these brigands and retrieve their masks, Deputy Willem aims to curb their bold advance while taking inventory of just how deeply the Defias have infiltrated the heartland of the kingdom.

quest:1818.text: Speak with Dillinger. Speak with Dillinger is a Horde military directive issued in Brill. Austil de Mon, the warrior trainer at the Gallows' End Tavern, dispatches able-bodied fighters to Deathguard Dillinger at the west end of the village to take on a hazardous combat mission in service of Lady Sylvanas. Within the Gallows' End Tavern in Brill, the warrior trainer Austil de Mon keeps a watchful eye out for promising combatants willing to serve the Dark Lady. When the Deathguards require capable hands, de Mon directs unproven adventurers out of the tavern and into the field. Deathguard Dillinger, who oversees security on the western edges of Brill, has requested someone with martial competence for an urgent task. Brill sits squarely on the front line of Tirisfal Glades, where the Forsaken must constantly prove their martial dominance against hostile threats. Dillinger's post near the village graveyard puts him in prime position to manage local incursions. For the young warrior, reporting to Dillinger is more than a simple errand: it is a formal test of combat prowess and political loyalty to the newly forged Forsaken nation.

quest:1819.text: Ulag the Cleaver. Ulag the Cleaver is a rite of passage for young Forsaken warriors in Tirisfal Glades. Deathguard Dillinger tasks you with releasing and executing an enslaved Scourge warrior bound inside a northern mausoleum, testing your martial resolve and earning the respect of the Deathguard. When the Scourge swept across Lordaeron, the Forsaken managed to capture a peculiar undead warrior who named himself Ulag the Cleaver. While Ulag possessed a conscious, lucid mind, his spirit remained inextricably dominated by the psychic thrall of the Lich King. Seeking to understand how the Scourge binds free will, the Forsaken kept him restrained under a magical seal beneath a mausoleum north of Brill, hoping to break the entity's spiritual chains. All efforts to sever Ulag from the Lich King's mental grip ended in failure. Recognizing that true freedom could only come through destruction, Deathguard Dillinger repurposed the captive as a trial of combat for rising Forsaken warriors. By disturbing the skull stone trigger outside the crypt, a warrior breaks the protective wards, releases Ulag from his imprisonment, and grants him release at the edge of an axe.

quest:182.text: The Troll Cave. Assigned by the mountaineer Grelin Whitebeard, this mission dispatches adventurers to cull young Frostmane trolls gathering in the southern caves of Coldridge Valley. With the Ironforge Senate preoccupied by an escalating trogg crisis, lone scouts and willing recruits must handle border skirmishes before the trolls establish a permanent foothold. While Ironforge's regular forces are consumed with repelling rock-jawed trogg incursions across the snowfields, the southern approaches cannot be left unguarded. Grelin Whitebeard and his brother Senir were deployed by the mountain authorities to assess whether the native ice trolls posed an immediate danger to the heartland. Perched on a bluff overlooking the frozen valley, Grelin maintains a solitary watch on their movements. Grelin's reconnaissance revealed that the local Frostmane clan had begun settling in a deep cave along the southern ridgeline of Coldridge Valley. Believing full military mobilization would be an unnecessary waste of dwarven manpower, the scout favored hiring capable local volunteers to cull the aggressive whelps. Thinning their young fighters serves to disrupt their encampment before the Frostmane can mount coordinated raids against nearby dwarven homesteads.

quest:1820.text: Speak with Coleman. Speak with Coleman is a transitional task in Tirisfal Glades offered to champions who have proven their worth against the Scourge. Deathguard Dillinger directs capable warriors from the town square to the local tavern to assist Coleman Farthing with personal and factional vendettas. After assisting in the containment of severe local threats—such as laying to rest dangerous Scourge remnants like Ulag the Cleaver—adventurers earn the personal trust of Deathguard Dillinger. As one of the sentinels watching the roads into Brill, Dillinger judges who is capable of handling more than routine perimeter patrols and points capable fighters toward citizens in need of specialized service. Not every conflict in Tirisfal Glades is fought on high command orders from the Undercity. Across the ruined kingdom of Lordaeron, surviving undead carry deep grudges tied to the lands, families, and fortunes they left behind. Coleman Farthing bides his time within the Gallow's End Tavern, seeking an instrument of vengeance to strike back at the threats lingering near former settlements like the Agamand Mills.

quest:1821.text: Agamand Heirlooms. Coleman Farthing tasks adventurers with plundering the Agamand Family Crypt at the northern end of Agamand Mills. Driven by bitter resentment over his mortal demise, he seeks to strip his former masters of their ancestral weapons and erase their final remnants of dignity. Before the Third War devastated Lordaeron, Coleman Farthing served the wealthy and influential Agamand family at their expansive mills in Tirisfal Glades. Whatever occurred during the fall of their estate, Farthing blames his former lords entirely for his death. Now raised into undeath among the Forsaken, he views the Agamands' downfall with spiteful satisfaction, rejoicing that the once-proud dynasty has been reduced to mindless minions enslaved to the Lich King. To completely extinguish what remains of the family's prestige, Farthing sends adventurers into the Agamand Family Crypt nestled beneath the northern bluffs of the mills. Within its haunted stone halls, the restive dead wander alongside lingering Scourge. Farthing demands the extraction of four storied relics—the Agamand family sword, axe, dagger, and mace—ensuring their bloodline's legacy is stripped of every remaining shred of honor.

quest:183.text: The Boar Hunter. The Boar Hunter is an early errand given by the dwarf hunter Talin Keeneye in Coldridge Valley. A surge in the local crag boar population has made the woods overly dangerous, and young recruits are tasked with culling the aggressive beasts so seasoned hunters can track in peace. Coldridge Valley is typically a quiet, protected training ground for young mountaineers and scholars of Ironforge. However, the wildlife often grows restless and overabundant in the harsh winter climate. Talin Keeneye, a veteran hunter stationed outside Anvilmar, notices that the aggressive small crag boars have multiplied so rapidly that they pose a genuine threat to anyone wandering the snow-covered trails. Hunting is a cornerstone of dwarven life, providing meat, hide, and essential fieldcraft practice. Yet when game becomes a nuisance that attacks on sight, culling is required to restore balance. By trimming the crag boar numbers across the valley slopes, young adventurers prove their combat readiness while giving local hunters room to pursue their sport without getting overwhelmed.

quest:184.text: Furlbrow's Deed. Furlbrow's Deed is a stolen land grant carried by Defias thieves in Elwynn Forest. Returning the document to the displaced Farmer Furlbrow near the Westfall border offers the fleeing couple their only hope of one day reclaiming their stolen homestead. While clashing with Defias bandits across Elwynn Forest, travelers often recover a crumpled land deed signed by Theodore and Verna Furlbrow. On the back of the parchment, crude handwriting reveals the bandits' scheme: having strong-armed the elderly farmer off his property, they smuggled the document across the river into Elwynn to use as a template for forging deeds to other seized land. The scrawl also notes that the Furlbrows were seen stranded by the road just over the border, immobilized by a broken wagon. The Furlbrows' loss is emblematic of the tragedy engulfing Westfall. With the Stormwind army absent and the realm's resources strained, the Defias Brotherhood has driven dozens of families from their ancestral soil, using force and legal manipulation to consolidate their hold on the kingdom's breadbasket. Though Theodore and Verna are abandoning their farm for their own safety, retaining their lawful deed preserves their single claim against the rogue uprising should order ever be restored to the province.

quest:1858.text: The Shattered Hand. This rogue trial serves as the final initiation into the ranks of the Shattered Hand within Orgrimmar. Therzok tasks aspiring rogues with unlocking a recovered satchel by lifting the key from an unwitting accomplice. Having retrieved Tazan's locked satchel, aspiring rogues find the prize useless without its key. Rather than forcing the complex lock by brute strength, the Shattered Hand insists on genuine craft. Therzok points his initiates toward Gamon, an easily distracted tauren drunkard who frequents Orgrimmar's tavern and previously assisted Tazan, making him an ideal mark for quiet thievery. Relieving Gamon of the key without alerting the entire tavern allows an initiate to unlock the satchel and secure Tazan's logbook. Bringing these stolen contents back to Therzok in the Cleft of Shadow satisfies the guild's rigorous standards. With the job done cleanly, the candidate is formally inducted as a recognized operative of the Shattered Hand.

quest:1859.text: Therzok. Therzok is a summons delivered to promising Horde rogues operating near the Valley of Trials and Sen'jin Village. The rogue trainer Kaplak spots your knack for violence and stealth, quietly directing you into the cavernous Cleft of Shadow to meet an operative of the Shattered Hand. Not all servants of the new Horde fight in plain daylight under the banner of Thrall's honor. When young rogues begin making a name for themselves in Durotar, Kaplak pulls them aside with hushed words. Word of an agent who combines physical lethality with a willingness to skirt the rules of open warfare travels fast to the ears of the underground guild in Orgrimmar. Kaplak sends the initiate deep beneath the red stone cliffs of Orgrimmar into the Cleft of Shadow. Away from the watchful eyes of the city grunts, Therzok waits in the gloom. The meeting serves as an induction point, bringing lone cutpurses and ambushers into the structured fold of the Shattered Hand, the covert network functioning as the Horde's daggers in the dark.

quest:1860.text: Speak with Jennea. Speak with Jennea is an introductory summoning summons directed at novice Alliance mages who have advanced beyond basic training in Elwynn Forest. Dispatched by the trainer Zaldimar Wefhellt in Goldshire, initiates are directed to report directly to Jennea Cannon in the Wizard's Sanctum within Stormwind City. Once an apprentice mage shows sufficient mastery of elementary spells in Goldshire, Zaldimar Wefhellt recognizes that field training under local tutors has run its course. Rather than lingering indefinitely in Elwynn's hamlets, promising spellcasters are directed into Stormwind City itself. At the heart of the Mage Quarter looms the Wizard's Sanctum, a sprawling sanctuary of arcane research and instruction where the realm's senior practitioners coordinate broader magical matters across the kingdom. Zaldimar emphasizes that reporting to Stormwind is far more than a routine scholastic promotion; a specific task has arisen that directly impacts the security of Elwynn Forest and Stormwind alike. Upon arrival, the apprentice reports to Jennea Cannon, an established mage who oversees vital local assignments. While Jennea remains measured and cautious about divulging grand secrets to a freshly arrived apprentice, reporting to her marks the start of direct service to the wizarding order.

quest:1861.text: Mirror Lake. Mirror Lake is an introductory investigative quest for novice Alliance mages studying in the Mage Quarter of Stormwind. Tasked by Jennea Cannon, apprentices venture just southwest of the city gates to sample the waterfall waters of Mirror Lake for residual magical contamination. Azeroth has suffered catastrophic mystic conflicts over the recent decades, from the opening of the Dark Portal to the Third War and the battle at Mount Hyjal. These violent shocks tore ancient arcane currents from their once-stable channels. In the Wizard's Sanctum of Stormwind, magi like Jennea Cannon monitor these shifts closely, fearing that dislodged flows of arcane power might bleed into the surrounding wilderness and corrupt local ecosystems. Mirror Lake lies nestled beneath the cliffs just southwest of the Stormwind gates, serving as a primary natural reservoir fed by mountain falls. Because the surrounding countryside depends on these waters, Jennea sends novice mages equipped with a glass flask directly to the base of the waterfall. Collecting fresh spray allows the Sanctum to conduct delicate scrying and reagent tests to confirm whether wild magic has begun seeping into the public water supply.

quest:1879.text: Speak with Bink. "Speak with Bink" is an Alliance summons directing novice mages from Dun Morogh to the capital city of Ironforge. Dispatched by Magis Sparkmantle, the call sends promising spellcasters to assist Bink, an arcane researcher working out of the Hall of Mysteries. Novice mages training in the cold crags of Dun Morogh eventually catch the eye of Magis Sparkmantle. Recognizing when an apprentice has outgrown the rudimentary exercises around Kharanos, Sparkmantle passes along word from his colleague, Bink. The request is specific and uncompromising: Bink requires an arcane specialist and refuses to trust the matter to anyone who cannot wield magic. The assignment carries young mages into Ironforge's Mystic Ward, where scholars, priests, and arcanists convene beneath the soaring stone vaults of the Hall of Mysteries. Here Bink conducts her studies, evaluating arriving apprentices with sharp-eyed scrutiny. In her view, raw potential is merely a beginning; an undisciplined spellcaster quickly becomes a hazard rather than an asset in arcane matters.

quest:1881.text: Speak with Anastasia. Speak with Anastasia is an introductory summons directing promising Forsaken mages to Anastasia Hartwell in the Undercity. Dispatched by mage trainer Cain Firesong, the young caster is called to the Magic Quarter to undertake critical work for the magi of the Forsaken. This brief summons sets the stage for investigations out into the blighted lands of Tirisfal Glades. As nascent spellcasters hone their early talents under the guidance of Cain Firesong in Brill, they are soon directed into the capital. The mages of the Forsaken maintain a dedicated enclave within the Magic Quarter of the Undercity, organizing both arcane scholarship and strategic defensive efforts across Lordaeron. Cain Firesong acts as an evaluator, filtering out mere novices and sending those who demonstrate genuine talent directly to senior practitioners who require capable field hands. Anastasia Hartwell stands among the prominent mage instructors within the Undercity. Rather than leaving promising students to study trivial incantations in safety, she wastes little time pressing them into service for the Forsaken's territorial and practical interests. Answering her summons is both a rite of passage for arcane practitioners and an induction into the shadowy, pragmatic magical pursuits that define the post-Scourge undead.

quest:1882.text: The Balnir Farmstead. "The Balnir Farmstead" is an early rite of passage for young Forsaken mages, directed by Anastasia Hartwell in the Undercity's Mage Quarter. Initiates are sent to eastern Tirisfal Glades to gather snapdragons from an abandoned farmstead sitting dangerously close to the border of the Plaguelands. The floral samples serve as barometers for the encroaching magical corruption spreading from the Scourge-blighted east. While the Royal Apothecary Society frequently studies the effects of necromancy and decay, the mages of the Forsaken maintain their own watchful eye on the borderlands. Anastasia Hartwell tasks novice spellcasters with travelling to the Balnir Farmstead in eastern Tirisfal Glades. Snapdragons native to the farm's gardens are naturally sensitive to shifting magical currents, absorbing ambient energies from the soil and atmosphere. By examining these blooms, arcane scholars in the Undercity can measure whether the corruptive contagion of the Lich King's domain has seeped past the bulwark into Tirisfal proper. The Balnir Farmstead sits near the fringes of the glades, uncomfortably near the blight-scarred wilderness of the Western Plaguelands. The Forsaken recognize that the Lich King's plague is an unruly and destructive power that actively rots the land itself. Although the Forsaken harness their own dark arts, uncontained Scourge corruption threatens their territorial borders and security. Anastasia intends to pass the gathered snapdragons along to the apothecaries, uniting arcane observation with alchemical investigation to defend Lordaeron's reclaimed heartland.

quest:1885.text: Mennet Carkad. Mennet Carkad is an introductory rogue quest in the Undercity that brings promising operatives into the fold of the Deathstalkers. Directed by Marion Call, aspiring assassins are summoned to report directly to Mennet Carkad deep within the Rogues' Quarter. Within the dark corridors of the Undercity, word travels quietly among the Forsaken's covert operatives. When a scout or assassin catches the eye of the higher leadership, an invitation is issued. Marion Call passes down word that Mennet Carkad, a prominent figure among the rogue handlers, has taken personal notice. Given the lethal reputation of the Forsaken intelligence apparatus, ignoring such a directive is not considered a viable option. Mennet Carkad waits in the shadowy alcoves of the Rogues' Quarter, watching over recruits and evaluating their readiness. Those who heed his call are not simply joining an ordinary guild of thieves; they are being tested for entry into the Deathstalkers, the dreaded espionage and assassination arm of the Forsaken. Swift obedience is merely the first baseline test for anyone seeking to serve the Dark Lady from the shadows.

quest:1886.text: The Deathstalkers. This task marks the trial for initiates seeking entry into the Deathstalkers, the covert and lethal arm answering to Lord Varimathras in the Undercity. Assigned by Mennet Carkad in the Rogues' Quarter, the mission demands ruthless initiative to intercept a traveling messenger. Completing it opens the door to deeper clandestine schemes within the Forsaken realm. The Deathstalkers do not admit just anyone into their ranks. Operating directly under dreadlord Varimathras, this secretive order acts as both the secret police and elite assassination corps of the Forsaken. To earn their notice, a hopeful agent must demonstrate cunning, discretion, and an unhesitating willingness to eliminate targets. In the shadowy corners of the Rogues' Quarter, handler Mennet Carkad sets an initiation trial designed to weed out the weak or overscrupulous.

quest:1898.text: The Deathstalkers. This covert assignment sends an undercover operative into the Undercity's shadowy underbelly to interrogate an unwitting conspirator. Acting under orders handed down from Lord Varimathras, you pose as an expected messenger to uncover treason within the Forsaken's own capital. The Deathstalkers do not merely eliminate external threats to the Forsaken; they maintain a ruthless vigil over their own citizens. Acting on suspicions harbored by Lord Varimathras, Deathstalker Mennet Carkad sets an infiltration plan in motion. Armed with a forged or acquired letter of introduction belonging to Astor Hadren, you are tasked with slipping past the suspicions of a local merchant named Andron Gant.

quest:1899.text: The Deathstalkers. This errand continues the Deathstalkers' deception of the informant Andron Gant in the Undercity. Still believing you are the messenger he was expecting, Gant hands over a ledger meant for his secret contacts, and the operative delivers it instead to Mennet Carkad in the Rogues' Quarter. The exchange marks the transition from simple inquiries to deeper, more covert operations on behalf of the Forsaken state. The Deathstalkers do not rely solely on brute force or shadow magic; their operations depend heavily on mundane ledgers, recorded names, and meticulous surveillance. Andron Gant, operating out of the Undercity, hands over a personal ledger crammed with intelligence, believing it bound for the mysterious employers he secretly serves. Taken in by the operative's disguise, Gant even asks that the same courier be sent in the future, never suspecting that his ledger is headed straight to the Deathstalkers.

quest:1961.text: Gathering Materials. Gathering Materials is a rite of passage for aspiring Horde mages training in the Undercity. Assigned by Anastasia Hartwell, the task sends apprentices into Silverpine Forest to claim arcane gems from the wizards of Dalaran, assembling the components needed to weave their first true mage's robes. Within the arcane cloisters of the Magic Quarter, novice mages must prove their mastery over more than just raw incantations. To earn their first true robes—a formal mantle marking their station and personal worth—initiates are directed by Anastasia Hartwell to harvest the raw components required for enchanted weave: a bolt of simple linen and a set of potent Dalaran mana gems. The mana gems cannot simply be purchased or manifested; they must be torn from Dalaran mages stationed across Silverpine Forest, particularly near Ambermill. Anastasia Hartwell remarks with cold detachment that while Dalaran's arcane philosophies mirror their own, sentimental hesitation has no place in the Undercity. In the eyes of the Forsaken, if those living wizards lack the strength to defend their relics, they forfeit both their treasures and their lives. Once gathered, the cloth and gems are delivered to Josef Gregorian, a tailor residing in the Magic Quarter. While Gregorian readily admits he lacks the magical talent to gauge the pristine quality of Dalaran's enchanted stones, he possesses the rare artisan skill needed to weave their raw power directly into the fabric of the robes.

quest:1963.text: The Shattered Hand. This rogue trial, issued by Therzok in the Cleft of Shadow, tests initiates seeking entry into the secretive Shattered Hand guild. To prove their deadly efficiency, aspiring rogues are tasked with hunting down the troll smuggler Tazan and seizing his locked satchel. Beneath the bustling streets of Orgrimmar lies the subterranean gloom of the Cleft of Shadow. Here operates the Shattered Hand, a clandestine order of assassins and thieves rooted in old orcish traditions. While Warchief Thrall preaches honor, diplomacy, and caution in ruling the nascent Horde, the leadership of the Shattered Hand believes such hesitation weakens their people. They seek to reclaim martial supremacy through covert violence, using knives and poison where battlefield charges might fail.

quest:1978.text: The Deathstalkers. This errand marks the formal induction of a capable operative into the ranks of the Deathstalkers, the Forsaken order of assassins and spies. Tasked with delivering Andron's Ledger directly to the dreadlord Varimathras, the courier brings proof of the Syndicate's covert activities to the highest tier of Undercity leadership. After unearthing incriminating records from Andron Gant, Mennet Carkad officially welcomes the operative into the Deathstalkers. The organization serves as Lady Sylvanas's eyes, ears, and daggers throughout Lordaeron, relying on intelligence networks, ruthless efficiency, and stealth to eliminate threats before they surface. Gaining formal recognition within the order is a major milestone for any aspiring rogue or scout in the Undercity. Because of the sensitive nature of the intelligence, the ledger is delivered directly to Varimathras in the Royal Quarter of the Undercity. The nathrezim commander oversees Forsaken tactical intelligence under Sylvanas Windrunner. Pleased with the Deathstalkers' initiative, Varimathras welcomes the operative's demonstrated capability, noting that his intelligence division can always make use of someone who delivers results.

quest:21.text: Skirmish at Echo Ridge. Skirmish at Echo Ridge is a direct military operation ordered by Marshal McBride to cleanse the Echo Ridge Mine of kobold laborers. Following initial reconnaissance, this strike aims to prevent the subterranean infestation from establishing a permanent foothold in Northshire Valley. After early scouting confirmed that kobolds had overrun the Echo Ridge Mine, Marshal McBride wasted no time organizing an active counterattack. Left undisturbed, subterranean vermin rapidly fortify their tunnels, stockpile stolen resources, and multiply beyond control. To protect the vital agricultural and spiritual retreat of Northshire Valley, the local garrison relies on recruits to engage the kobold laborers directly and thin their ranks before they entrench themselves further. The necessity of employing newly enlisted recruits for a direct frontal assault reflects the strained state of the Stormwind Army. With frontline garrisons stretched thin across the southern borders and rumors of rising unrest throughout Elwynn, local officers like McBride must muster whatever willing hands they can find. The successful skirmish at Echo Ridge demonstrates the recruit's reliability, earning them formal respect and readying them for more critical missions elsewhere in the kingdom.

quest:2118.text: Plagued Lands. Plagued Lands is an Alliance quest offered by Tharnariun Treetender in Darkshore. Driven to remedy the spreading corruption afflicting the native wildlife, Tharnariun tasks adventurers with trapping a rabid thistle bear alive using an enchanted relic to attempt a cure. A sinister affliction creeps through Darkshore's woods, twisting its beasts into maddened, aggressive shadows of their former selves. The native thistle bears have suffered the worst of this madness, succumbing to a rabid frenzy that threatens both passing travelers and the fragile ecological harmony of the coast. Where night elf sentinels often respond with steel, the druids seek to understand and heal the root cause. Refusing to slaughter the corrupted beasts without trying to save them, Tharnariun Treetender fashioned a specialized trap known as Tharnariun's Hope. Adventurers place the device on the forest floor, using its soothing light to temporarily calm a raging thistle bear's mind. Once pacified, the creature meekly follows the traveler back to Tharnariun's outpost for study.

quest:2160.text: Supplies to Tannok. Supplies to Tannok is an errand entrusted to fledgling adventurers departing Coldridge Valley through the dangerous mountain pass into greater Dun Morogh. The gnome tinkerer Hands Springsprocket sends a crate of needed provisions to Tannok Frosthammer at the Thunderbrew Distillery inn in Kharanos, bypassing the trogg-infested trails that have severed routine trade. Coldridge Valley is traditionally the proving ground and sanctuary for young Ironforge dwarves and exiled Gnomeregan survivors, but recent events have strained its connection to the rest of Dun Morogh. Trogg incursions have overrun Coldridge Pass, leaving the mountain defile perilous to cross. Mountaineers are spread thin guarding settlements and defensive perimeters, delaying scheduled supply escorts for days on end. Hands Springsprocket, a gnome waiting by the mouth of Coldridge Pass, found himself saddled with a crate of vital inn supplies meant for Kharanos without any safe way to deliver it personally. Recognizing that hearty adventurers are already preparing to brave the perilous pass, he enlists outward-bound travelers to carry the cargo to Tannok Frosthammer, the assistant at the bustling Thunderbrew inn. Reaching Kharanos marks an adventurer's entry into the broader world of Dun Morogh. Tannok Frosthammer eagerly receives the delivery, noting that word from Anvilmar has been scarce ever since the troggs disrupted travel through the pass. Delivering the goods restores a fragile line of communication and trade between the two isolated dwarf communities.

quest:2161.text: A Peon's Burden. A Peon's Burden is an introductory delivery task given by Ukor, an anxious orc laborer stranded along the trail outside the Valley of Trials. After attempting to deliver provisions to new recruits who turned out not to need them, Ukor entrusts travelers with returning the heavy load safely to Razor Hill. Ukor is an earnest peon who set out from Razor Hill with good intentions, hauling a heavy pack of provisions toward the Valley of Trials. Believing the fresh recruits training in the red canyon were in dire need of rations, he braved the road only to be turned away. The taskmasters overseeing the trials deliberately keep supplies lean—as Innkeeper Grosk later notes, surviving on meager sustenance is seen as a way to forge discipline and endurance in young Horde warriors. Though he managed to make it to the pass, Ukor finds himself terrified of retracing his steps across the sun-baked soil of Durotar. The crags along the trail teem with aggressive scorpids, venomous spiders, and prowling boars. Lacking weapons, armor, or the fighting spirit expected of orcish grunts, the frightened laborer waits along the path, pleading for any passing adventurer departing the proving grounds to shoulder his burden and return it to the inn.

quest:2178.text: Easy Strider Living. Easy Strider Living is a local culinary task offered by Alanndarian Nightsong in Auberdine. She is eager to share her prized recipe for strider stew, provided an adventurer is willing to hunt down the fierce foreststriders wandering Darkshore and retrieve their meat. Auberdine might be a quiet port village, but survival along the coast requires making good use of the local wildlife. Alanndarian Nightsong has developed a secret recipe for hearty strider stew, a savory dish made from the tall, fleet-footed foreststriders that stalk the shadowy woods of Darkshore. Rather than simply handing out culinary secrets, she asks aspiring cooks and hunters to venture out and cull the birds themselves. Foreststriders are swift, sharp-beaked avian predators that roam the mist-shrouded woodlands and beaches north and south of Auberdine. While they can be temperamental and aggressive when provoked, their succulent meat makes an excellent base for a rich stew. Bringing back fresh meat satisfies Alanndarian's hungry pot and earns the hunter her cherished recipe.

quest:218.text: The Stolen Journal. The Stolen Journal is an early Alliance quest in Dun Morogh where Grelin Whitebeard tasks adventurers with entering the troll cave in Coldridge Valley to reclaim his stolen notebook. To recover it, you must defeat the formidable troll leader Grik'nir the Cold. Reclaiming the journal allows Grelin to finalize his appraisal of the troll threat within Coldridge Valley. Grelin Whitebeard has been observing the Frostmane trolls encroaching on Coldridge Valley, keeping detailed notes on their habits and sudden aggression. During the unrest, an unusually imposing troll made off with his personal journal and retreated into the depths of their den. For Grelin, the loss is not merely sentimental; the notebook contains the bulk of his reconnaissance, leaving his official assessment stalled until it is recovered from the cavern. The brute responsible for taking the journal is Grik'nir the Cold, a powerful Frostmane troll marked with distinctive body and facial paint who holds court in the heart of the valley's troll cave. Slaying Grik'nir breaks the immediate local leadership of the cave's trolls and secures Grelin's journal. With the leader dispatched, Grelin feels confident enough to report that the valley's troll situation is manageable, sending his finished findings on to his brother Senir.

quest:22.text: Goretusk Liver Pie. Goretusk Liver Pie is a culinary errand undertaken for Salma Saldean at the Saldean Farm in Westfall. With the breadbasket of the kingdom ravaged by bandits, local homesteaders rely on hunting the aggressive local boars to put a hearty meal on the table. Assisting Salma provides a rare taste of comfort and home-cooked hospitality in an otherwise bleak frontier. Westfall was once the fertile breadbasket of Stormwind, but recent years have brought hard times. With neglected infrastructure, roving outlaws, and overgrown fields, everyday life has become a grind for the few remaining settlers. At the Saldean Farm, Salma Saldean works tirelessly to maintain a sense of hearth and home despite the encroaching dangers. Preparing a traditional meat pie represents one of the few modest luxuries available to homesteaders trying to preserve their way of life. The plains of Westfall teem with goretusks, aggressive wild boars known for their tough hides and vicious tusks. While dangerous to lone farmhands, they are also a vital source of meat for families cut off from regular trade. Salma's recipe calls for careful preparation—crushed rosemary, minced garlic, chopped dill, and simmering gravy—to turn the pungent organs of these hardy beasts into a rich, savory feast.

quest:2205.text: Seek out SI: 7. Seek out SI: 7 is an introductory task handed to fledgling rogues in Elwynn Forest by Keryn Sylvius. Carrying a small package from Goldshire to Stormwind City, novice agents are introduced to Master Mathias Shaw, the leader of the crown's covert intelligence network. In the Lion's Pride Inn at Goldshire, rogue trainer Keryn Sylvius wastes little time flattering newcomers. Believing fresh initiates look more like cheese delivery hands than capable covert operatives, Sylvius nonetheless passes along an errand: carry a sealed delivery into the capital. The task acts as both a reliable courier run and a quiet vetting process for scouts entering the broader service of the realm. The destination lies deep within Old Town, the bustling and worn quarter of Stormwind City. Tucked into the southeastern corner of the district stands the command center of SI:7—Stormwind Intelligence, Section 7. Here, Master Mathias Shaw oversees the kingdom's covert operations. Receiving the package with his characteristic dry skepticism, Shaw evaluates whether the traveler possesses the grit needed for real espionage.

quest:2206.text: Snatch and Grab. Snatch and Grab is an undercover assignment given to promising rogues by Master Mathias Shaw, leader of SI:7. It tasks operatives with infiltrating Jerod's Landing to steal shipping intelligence from the Defias Brotherhood. For an aspiring operative in Stormwind, standing before Master Mathias Shaw is the true test of entry into the kingdom's covert intelligence wing. Rather than relying on simple brute force, Shaw demands proof of finesse and stealth. Taking down key figures quietly and retrieving vital papers without drawing the realm into open scandal is the core mandate of SI:7, and this mission serves as an initiate's proving ground. Jerod's Landing sits on the river in southern Elwynn, south of Goldshire and just east of the Maclure Vineyards. Though once a quiet local dock, the Defias Brotherhood seized control of the site to establish an illicit transit corridor. By ferrying smuggled arms, supplies, and contraband across the waters from Redridge down toward Westfall, the thieves bypass royal road patrols entirely. Shaw makes SI:7's standing doctrine abundantly clear before dispatching agents into the field: should the operative be captured, compromised, or slain, the Crown and its spymasters will disavow all knowledge of their existence. Recovering the Defias Dockmaster's schedule secures crucial proof of the Brotherhood's supply lines while keeping Stormwind's official involvement in the shadows.

quest:224.text: In Defense of the King's Lands. Mountaineer Cobbleflint guards the southern tower in the Valley of Kings, desperately seeking aid against the encroaching Stonesplinter troggs. With Ironforge's military stretched thin across distant fronts, the defense of Loch Modan's southern passes falls to passing Alliance volunteers. The massive dwarven monuments carved into the mountains of the Valley of Kings loom over a garrison under severe strain. Mountaineer Cobbleflint and his fellow guards stationed at the southern watchtower face an ever-growing invasion of troggs erupting from the rock. With much of King Magni Bronzebeard's regular army dispatched abroad to support Alliance commitments, the home front relies heavily on local patrols and hired blades to prevent the province from being overrun. The subterranean threat originates within Stonesplinter Valley, a craggy ravine carving into the southern peaks of Loch Modan. Troggs and their scouts have burrowed surface-ward in massive numbers, carving out fortified camps along the valley floor. Left unchecked, their scouting parties threaten the critical roads connecting Loch Modan to the southern passes, forcing the Mountaineers to wage a continuous war of attrition.

quest:2242.text: Destiny Calls. Destiny Calls is a discreet investigation assigned by Syurna to uncover the source of corruption seeping through Teldrassil's boughs. It tasks an operative with slipping past or confronting a hostile satyr named Sethir the Ancient near the Oracle Glade to recover his journal. The night elf leadership in Darnassus has watched Teldrassil's growing malady with quiet anxiety. Rather than sending armed patrols that end up dead, the rogue trainer Syurna seeks someone capable of subtle work. Sethir the Ancient, a satyr roosting out on a remote bough near the Oracle Glade, has repelled every attempt at force and diplomatic overture alike. Uncovering what he knows requires slipping into his lair and seizing his personal possessions.

quest:233.text: Coldridge Valley Mail Delivery. Coldridge Valley Mail Delivery is a simple courier task entrusted to recruits by Sten Stoutarm at Anvilmar. With mountain passes often choked with snow and troggs pressing nearby, carrying fresh correspondence out to the camps along the frozen lake keeps the valley's isolated defenders connected. Life in Coldridge Valley is secluded even in the calmest of seasons. When winter couriers successfully navigate the mountain pass with mail from the rest of Dun Morogh, the missives pile up quickly at Anvilmar. Sten Stoutarm, busy managing local supply concerns and security, relies on wandering recruits to carry these bundles down the western road rather than letting vital tidings languish in the hall. The intended recipient, Talin Keeneye, keeps watch by the frozen lake to the west, observing trogg movements and dangerous wildlife. Even out in the cold, word from Ironforge and surrounding outposts remains precious. However, mail sorting under harsh mountain conditions is rarely flawless, and letters bound for different scouts often travel together in a single bundle.

quest:234.text: Coldridge Valley Mail Delivery. This errand completes a courier run across the snowy drifts of Coldridge Valley. Passing the dispatch from mountaineer Talin Keeneye down the southeastern road ensures that Grelin Whitebeard stays connected to the dwarven capital. Even in an isolated basin like Coldridge Valley, news and formal correspondence must travel. While Anvilmar serves as the administrative heart of the valley, field scouts and sentries stationed along the trails rely on foot couriers to relay dispatches between the high passes and Ironforge. Grelin Whitebeard maintains a small camp down the road to the southeast of Talin Keeneye's post. Enduring freezing drifts and constant trogg harassment, veteran mountaineers stationed at these remote watchpoints depend on regular missives to stay informed of broader affairs across Dun Morogh and the kingdom beyond.

quest:2498.text: Return to Denalan. Return to Denalan is an Alliance quest connecting the botanists investigating corruption within Teldrassil. After studying the mossy tumors afflicting local timberlings, Rellian Greenspyre sends you back south to Lake Al'Ameth to assist Denalan with an alarming new discovery. While examining the strange mossy tumors afflicting Teldrassil's timberlings, Rellian Greenspyre receives urgent word from his colleague Denalan. Stationed beside the tranquil waters of Lake Al'Ameth, Denalan believes he has finally isolated what is causing these unnatural growths on the forest's nature spirits. Recognizing the gravity of the situation, Rellian dispatches you back south immediately to lend a hand.

quest:2499.text: Oakenscowl. Denalan asks adventurers to put an end to Oakenscowl, a powerful timberling corrupted by a massive growth. Dwelling in a cave along the southern bank of Lake Al'Ameth, the maddened creature now spreads blight across the local wildlife. Oakenscowl was once a grand leader among the timberlings, the wood spirits that tend to the lush boughs of Teldrassil. Tragically, the corruption creeping through the world tree does not discriminate between humble wildlife and ancient protectors. Driven wild by a gargantuan tumor swelling upon its bark, Oakenscowl has become a vessel of blight rather than a steward of growth. Lurking in a cavern on the southern shore of Lake Al'Ameth, Oakenscowl's toxic presence actively poisons surrounding waters and woodland beasts. Denalan, unable to face the beast alone, seeks the creature's destruction not out of malice, but to mercifully sever the source of corruption and study the bizarre, overgrown tumor plaguing the lake's spirits.

quest:2518.text: Tears of the Moon. Tears of the Moon is a solemn task assigned by Priestess A'moora in the Temple of the Moon. Once cherished by the goddess Elune, the great spider Lady Sathrah has fallen into madness, forcing the Sisterhood of Elune to seek her merciful end and retrieve her sacred spinnerets. Within the serene confines of Darnassus's Temple of the Moon, Priestess A'moora laments the tragic fate of Lady Sathrah. In earlier days, Sathrah was celebrated as a blessed creature of Elune. She wove delicate silver webs beneath the night sky, catching the evening mist that gathered upon Teldrassil's boughs. The shimmering dew her webs collected possessed miraculous healing properties, carefully gathered and preserved by the Sisterhood of Elune for their sacred ministrations.

quest:2519.text: The Temple of the Moon. The Temple of the Moon is an introductory quest in Darnassus where Sister Aquinne directs adventurers to seek out Priestess A'moora. The Sisterhood of Elune requires aid for a suffering ancient creature dwelling within the boughs of Teldrassil. It serves as the opening call to a solemn ritual of mercy. While walking among the waters and shaded groves of the Temple Gardens, travelers meet Sister Aquinne, a devoted servant of Elune. Sensing capable hands, she reaches out on behalf of her order. A venerable forest creature is suffering, and the Sisters cannot attend to the matter alone. Sister Aquinne directs candidates toward the grand Temple of the Moon just to the southeast. There, Priestess A'moora coordinates the rituals and practical duties required to address Teldrassil's troubled wildlife, preparing sympathetic allies to carry out a sorrowful task of mercy.

quest:2520.text: Sathrah's Sacrifice. Sathrah's Sacrifice is the conclusion to a somber ritual performed within the Temple of the Moon in Darnassus. Entrusted with the remains of Lady Sathrah, players offer the fallen creature's spinnerets to Elune's sacred waters to cleanse her soul of corruption and lay her spirit to rest. Following the tragic slaying of Lady Sathrah, Priestess A'moora charges initiates with a final spiritual duty. The great spider had fallen prey to the dark madness spreading across Teldrassil, warping her once-peaceful nature into mindless aggression. Rather than treating her death as a simple culling, the Priesthood of Elune seeks to redeem her fallen essence. By placing her silvery spinnerets into the central fountain of the Temple of the Moon, the consecrated waters wash away the tainting corruption, granting her release.

quest:267.text: The Trogg Threat. The Trogg Threat is an Alliance quest issued by Captain Rugelfuss at the Southern Gate of Loch Modan. With the local Ironforge Reserve called away to support Alliance battlefronts, the remaining defenders are stretched thin against the hostile trogg tribes in the hills. Adventurers are tasked with culling the troggs and returning with their stone teeth to relieve pressure on the mountain pass. The defensive line guarding the southern approach into Loch Modan is in a precarious state. The regular dwarven mountaineers and Ironforge Reserve regiments have been dispatched to reinforce broader Alliance war fronts, leaving Captain Rugelfuss and a skeleton garrison stationed at the southern guard tower. Constrained by strict orders not to abandon the gate, Rugelfuss cannot mount an active offensive into the highlands, leaving nearby settlers and travelers vulnerable to ambushes. Troggs residing in the surrounding crags pose an escalating danger to Khaz Modan. Left unchecked, their numbers swell quickly, threatening to overrun dwarven outposts. To buy time and thin the menace, Rugelfuss calls upon wandering adventurers to assault the troggs directly in their hillside warrens and present severed stone teeth as physical confirmation of the deed.

quest:282.text: Senir's Observations. Having gathered vital intelligence on local threats in Coldridge Valley, Grelin Whitebeard entrusts you with carrying his findings to his brother, Senir Whitebeard, out in Kharanos. However, leaving the sheltered valley requires passing through a tunnel recently overrun by hostile troggs, guarded by Mountaineer Thalos. Grelin Whitebeard spent considerable effort documenting the troll activity stirring around Coldridge Valley. When his journal was pilfered and subsequently recovered, it became clear that the collected intelligence was far too critical to trust to an inexperienced apprentice. Looking to bypass intermediate hands, Grelin selects a seasoned adventurer to convey his report directly to his brother, Senir Whitebeard, who conducts operations outside the valley in Kharanos. Leaving Coldridge Valley is no longer a simple trek down the main road. The eastern tunnel connecting the valley to the wider snowy plateau of Dun Morogh has been violently overrun by burrowing troggs. To prevent unwary civilians from wandering into a deathtrap, the Ironforge guard has stationed Mountaineer Thalos just outside the passage. Only travelers carrying urgent, official business are granted leave to push past the sentry post and brave the subterranean gauntlet.

quest:287.text: Frostmane Hold. Frostmane Hold is an Alliance recon mission assigned by Senir Whitebeard in Kharanos. Having tracked the hostile Frostmane trolls to their heavily guarded cavern stronghold near Iceflow Lake, Senir enlists adventurous scouts to brave the interior, eliminate their headhunters, and supply vital intel for his scouting reports. Stationed in Kharanos, mountaineer and scout Senir Whitebeard was tasked with monitoring the encroaching Frostmane troll threat across Dun Morogh. While he successfully traced the aggressive tribes back to their primary cavern dwelling southwest of Brewnall Village, the sheer volume of armed trolls gave him pause. Reluctant to step foot inside alone and falling severely behind on his official reports, Senir hires passing adventurers to venture into the icy recesses on his behalf. The stronghold sits carved into the western peaks overlooking Iceflow Lake, a freezing redoubt packed with hostile ice trolls. To fulfill Senir's mission, scouts must fight their way deep through the subterranean tunnels, cull the fierce Frostmane Headhunters stationed along the ledges, and map the interior layout. Surviving the delve provides the critical intelligence Senir requires to finalize his findings for Ironforge's military commanders.

quest:291.text: The Reports. Carry Senir Whitebeard's report on the Frostmane trolls from Kharanos to Senator Barin Redstone in Ironforge. Senir warns that the senator is sour and asks you not to mention who helped gather the information. After daring reconnaissance deep inside Frostmane Hold, Senir Whitebeard drafts an urgent report detailing the growing troll threat facing Dun Morogh. Stationed out of Kharanos, the mountaineer needs a courier to deliver these intelligence findings directly to Senator Barin Redstone in Ironforge. Eager to preserve his own reputation in the eyes of the government, Whitebeard cheerfully advises his runner not to mention who actually did the hazardous legwork out in the snowy crags.

quest:2997.text: Tome of Divinity. The Tome of Divinity is an introductory summons calling young dwarven paladins from their field duties in Dun Morogh to the mountain city of Ironforge. Dispatched by Azar Stronghammer, the initiate is directed to seek guidance from Tiza Battleforge high in the Hall of Mysteries. It marks the formal beginning of a paladin's deeper trials in service to the Holy Light. While dwarven initiates begin their training protecting the snowbound villages and roads of Dun Morogh, martial prowess alone does not make a paladin. Azar Stronghammer recognizes when a defender has grown ready for deeper spiritual instruction. Rather than continuing standard martial drills, he sends promising candidates into the heart of Ironforge to begin their true initiation under the city's revered holy elders. The summons directs the initiate to the Mystic Ward, climbing into the quiet chambers of the Hall of Mysteries. There, surrounded by sacred relics and solemn study, stands Tiza Battleforge. As one of the most respected dwarven champions of the Light, she tests incoming paladins on their readiness to embrace self-sacrifice, mercy, and the heavy moral duties of their holy calling.

quest:2998.text: Tome of Divinity. Tome of Divinity marks a vital summons for budding human paladins serving the Alliance. Dispatched by local mentors like Brother Wilhelm in Goldshire, initiates travel to Stormwind's Cathedral of Light to meet Duthorian Rall. Answering this call begins the sacred trial necessary to master the holy gift of resurrection. Novice paladins beginning their journey through Elwynn Forest spend their early days helping the locals and testing their combat prowess against wolves, Defias bandits, and kobolds. Once an initiate demonstrates both martial discipline and dedication to the Holy Light, mentors such as Brother Wilhelm deliver a personal summons. Influential paladin leaders take note of promising students, directing them to leave local chapel outposts behind and report straight to the spiritual heart of the kingdom. In the Cathedral Square of Stormwind, the Cathedral of Light serves as the supreme sanctuary for the kingdom's priesthood and the Knights of the Silver Hand. It is here that Duthorian Rall resides, overseeing the growth of those sworn to the Order. Stepping beneath the soaring vaulted ceilings, the initiate stands before high-ranking paladins to receive the formal trials of the Tome of Divinity—challenges structured to test unyielding compassion, fortitude, and sacrificial duty.

quest:2999.text: Tome of Divinity. Tome of Divinity is a rite of passage quest offered to young dwarven paladins serving in Dun Morogh. Directed by Brandur Ironhammer, the paladin trainer in Ironforge's Hall of Mysteries, an initiate is sent upstairs to speak with the respected paladin trainer Tiza Battleforge. It marks the transition from basic martial training into the deeper spiritual duties and sacred vows of the Holy Light. While novice paladins spend their early days defending Anvilmar and Kharanos from troggs and frost trolls, their duties eventually call for deeper devotion. Brandur Ironhammer, recognizing that an initiate has proven their martial discipline, advises them to take a break from their work in the snowy passes and seek guidance upstairs in his own Hall of Mysteries in Ironforge. There, senior paladins oversee the spiritual maturation of the order. Tiza Battleforge stands as one of the most revered paladins among the Ironforge dwarves. It is her responsibility to instruct initiates on the true burdens of the Light, moving past simple swordplay and hammer swings to teach compassion, justice, and self-sacrifice. Seeking her out begins the formal study of the Tome of Divinity, a sacred process aimed at granting a paladin the ability to resurrect the fallen.

quest:3000.text: Tome of Divinity. This errand directs dwarven paladins wandering abroad to return home to Ironforge to further their sacred calling. Offered by Lord Grayson Shadowbreaker in Stormwind, it points fledgling champions toward Tiza Battleforge, one of the most respected instructors in the Hall of Mysteries. Returning home marks the beginning of their formal trials with the Tome of Divinity. While dwarven paladins frequently aid the kingdom of Stormwind and venture throughout human territories, their spiritual and martial roots remain anchored in Khaz Modan. Lord Grayson Shadowbreaker, recognizing when a dwarf's training in the field has progressed enough, advises them to return to the heart of Ironforge. There, their own people oversee the profound spiritual obligations expected of a full Knight of the Silver Hand. Upon returning to the mountainous capital, the paladin is directed to the Mystic Ward. Deep within the Hall of Mysteries, atop its upper level, resides Tiza Battleforge. She serves as a venerated mentor to the younger generation of dwarven paladins, preparing them to shoulder the burden of the Holy Light through the sacred trials recorded in the Tome of Divinity.

quest:3065.text: Simple Tablet. Simple Tablet is an introductory rite of passage for fledgling warriors entering the Valley of Trials. Delivered into your hands after proving your mettle against local beasts, it directs you toward Frang, the local veteran tasked with honing raw brawn into martial discipline. After proving you can hold your own against the Mottled Boars of the valley, Gornek hands over a parchment specifically marked for you. In the harsh environment of Durotar, the Horde does not leave its fighters without guidance for long. The tablet serves as an invitation to seek out Frang, the warrior trainer stationed outside the Den. Frang takes shelter in the shade just outside the Den, watching recruits trickle in from the red scrubland. He assesses fresh recruits with a seasoned eye, ready to impart fundamentals—whether hefting a heavy axe or wielding a spear—to ensure each new soldier can defend the fragile settlements of the young Horde.

quest:308.text: Distracting Jarven. Down in the cellar of Thunderbrew Distillery, guard Jarven Thunderbrew finds himself surrounded by barrels he is forbidden to touch. Craving a taste of the family craft, he asks a passing adventurer for a mug of Thunder Ale to help sharpen his wits on duty. Jarven Thunderbrew is tasked with keeping watch over the deep stores of Thunderbrew Distillery in Kharanos. Despite being surrounded by the finest stout in Dun Morogh, he works under strict family orders not to dip into the stock while on guard. The temptation proves too much, prompting him to enlist passing travelers to fetch him a pint of potent Thunder Ale from the taps upstairs. Jarven insists that a good drink will only hone his senses and bolster his watch. Whether indulging a guard on duty is wise remains an open question, but among the hardy dwarves of Dun Morogh, few can fault a Thunderbrew for wanting a taste of his own kin's world-famous brew.

quest:3082.text: Etched Tablet. Etched Tablet is an introductory hunter quest delivered in the Valley of Trials after completing initial trials. It directs aspiring troll hunters to report to the hunter trainer Jen'shan to begin their formal training in the wilderness. After proving their early mettle against the local boars of the Den, novice hunters are intercepted by Gornek with a carved message. The stone tablet bears the mark of Jen'shan, a skilled troll huntswoman stationed nearby. Gornek passes it along as a sign that the young hunter has demonstrated sufficient grit to catch the eye of seasoned survivalists, marking the transition from basic brute survival to disciplined wilderness training. When reporting to Jen'shan, the troll trainer speaks of the deep history between orcs and trolls within the Horde. While orcs possessed renowned traditions of warriors and shamans, the Darkspear trolls brought ancient stalking, tracking, and survival skills that helped the orcs endure life on Azeroth. Jen'shan views the training of new hunters as an ongoing exchange of survival knowledge, binding the allied races closer together through shared respect for the hunt.

quest:3083.text: Encrypted Tablet. The Encrypted Tablet is a summons delivered by Gornek to aspiring rogues training within the Valley of Trials. Written in cipher, the message directs novice cutpurses to Rwag, the covert operative in the Den who oversees rogue instruction and ties to the Shattered Hand. Once an initiate proves their mettle against the local wildlife, Gornek hands over an Encrypted Tablet delivered specifically for them. Rather than plain speech, the message is locked in cipher—a test and a precaution fitting for those who practice the arts of stealth, poison, and subterfuge. It invites the recruit to descend into the Den to meet Rwag, the trainer responsible for shaping rogues, thieves, and cutpurses for the Horde. Upon decoding the instructions and entering the Den, initiates find Rwag, an agent aligned with the Shattered Hand. While he assures newly recruited rogues that the guild will not dictate their every breath, he warns that the Hand holds him accountable should an apprentice fail to perform. In a fledgling nation surrounded by foes, the Horde relies heavily on silent scouts and agile cutpurses to gather intelligence and eliminate threats from the shadows.

quest:3084.text: Rune-Inscribed Tablet. The Rune-Inscribed Tablet is a summoning missive delivered to aspiring shamans training in the Valley of Trials. Sent by Shikrik, it invites promising initiates to begin formal instruction in communing with the spirits and commanding the elemental forces of earth, fire, water, and air. After proving their early discipline in the dusty training grounds of the Valley of Trials, fledgling shamans are handed a carved stone tablet by Gornek. The runes upon it serve as an invitation from Shikrik, the local shaman trainer, signaling that the initiate is ready to look beyond simple physical combat and heed the deeper currents of the natural world. Shamanism occupies a sacred place in the revitalized Horde. As Shikrik teaches, shamans draw their power from the four elemental forces and their strength from ancestral spirits. Emulating Warchief Thrall, shamans are expected to be spiritual guides and bulwarks of wisdom for their communities, offering protection to the settlements taking root across Durotar.

quest:3085.text: Hallowed Tablet. A simple summons delivered to fledgling priests in the Valley of Trials after their initial trial of strength. The inscribed tablet directs young spiritualists to Ken'jai, the resident troll priest trainer, who introduces them to the deeper communion with the spirits. After proving their mettle against the local boars under Gornek's supervision, young priests training in the Valley of Trials receive an inscribed stone known as the Hallowed Tablet. Delivered through Gornek, the message bears the mark of Ken'jai, a Darkspear mystic positioned outside the Den who watches over newcomers called to the path of faith and spiritual magic. Unlike the Holy Light practiced by their human or dwarven counterparts across the sea, priesthood among the Horde's Darkspear trolls centers on communion with the spirits and loa. Ken'jai welcomes fledgling acolytes to Durotar by reminding them that their power stems from spiritual discipline, promising to instruct them in greater rites only as their spiritual bond matures.

quest:3086.text: Glyphic Tablet. Glyphic Tablet is an introductory class quest in the Valley of Trials directed at novice Horde mages. Dispatched via Gornek after proving one's strength, it directs young spellcasters to Mai'ah, a troll mage trainer stationed outside the Den. After proving their basic mettle against the local wildlife in the Valley of Trials, fledgling mages are presented with an inscribed tablet passed along by Gornek. The missive originates from Mai'ah, the valley's resident mage trainer, bidding the initiate to seek her out by the entrance to the Den when they are ready to pursue their formal arcane studies. When greeted, Mai'ah wastes little time on formalities, cutting straight to the sober reality of arcane power. While acknowledging that mages wield world-shaping potential, she warns that their greatest threat is neither rival warriors nor enemy races, but the unseen corrupting lure of magic itself. She counsels humility and patience, cautioning that unchecked sorcery easily tricks a practitioner into overestimating their own mastery.

quest:3087.text: Etched Parchment. Etched Parchment is an initiation quest directing young orc hunters in the Valley of Trials to their local class trainer, Jen'shan. Delivered through Gornek after an initiate's first blooding, the note opens the door to specialized wilderness training and survival skills in Durotar. After proving their basic mettle against the local mottled boars, hunters starting in the Valley of Trials receive an etched parchment handled by Gornek. The missive originates from Jen'shan, a skilled Darkspear hunter who observes new arrivals from the edges of the encampment. The note serves as an official invitation to begin formal training, acknowledging that the initiate possesses the instincts required to master the untamed beasts and harsh landscape of Durotar. Reporting to Jen'shan marks the transition from common recruit to dedicated stalker. Jen'shan disabuses newcomers of the notion that the hunter's craft is simpler than the arcane arts or ancestral shamanism. Mastering Durotar's predators, maintaining ranged weaponry, and surviving off an unforgiving land demand relentless discipline. She directs her apprentices to aid the other denizens of the valley to test their abilities before returning to her for more advanced survival techniques.

quest:3088.text: Encrypted Parchment. The Encrypted Parchment is a summons delivered to novice orc rogues who have proven their basic survival skills in the Valley of Trials. Written in cipher, it directs promising recruits into the shadowed depths of the Den to meet Rwag, an operative serving the interests of the Shattered Hand. After proving their mettle against the local wildlife, novice orcs receive an encrypted parchment passed along by Gornek. While other trainers openly recruit pupils in the clearing, the rogue instructor Rwag prefers the discreet safety of cipher and stone. The parchment directs the initiate past the sunlit camp and deep into the cavern known as the Den. Upon deciphering the note and venturing inside, the novice discovers Rwag skulking within the rock. Suspicious of the warlocks lurking even deeper in the cave, Rwag wastes no time explaining his true allegiance: he watches recruits on behalf of the Shattered Hand. While orcish society champions overt honor and glory on the battlefield, the Shattered Hand acts as the Horde's silent network of spies, cutthroats, and intelligence gatherers.

quest:3089.text: Rune-Inscribed Parchment. Rune-Inscribed Parchment is a missive delivered to fledgling Horde shamans beginning their journey in the Valley of Trials. Written by the trainer Shikrik, the parchment summons promising initiates to begin their formal tutelage in commune with the spirits and elements. After proving their basic survival skills against the local wildlife, new orc shamans are handed a rune-inscribed parchment by Gornek, the overseer of the Valley of Trials. The parchment bears mystical writing from Shikrik, the valley's resident shaman trainer, requesting an audience with the newly arrived initiate. Reporting to Shikrik marks the formal beginning of a shaman's sacred duty to the Horde. Shikrik reminds the young initiate that their calling is not merely martial; they are chosen to serve as conduits for the ancestral spirits and wielders of elemental wrath. Through Shikrik, new shamans learn to channel spiritual energies, mend wounds, and call upon the natural forces of Kalimdor.

quest:3092.text: Etched Note. The Etched Note is a formal summons directed to promising young tauren hunters in Camp Narache. Delivered on behalf of the trainer Lanka Farshot, the message calls the novice forward to begin mastering the practical and spiritual arts of the wild. While training amidst the bluffs of Red Cloud Mesa, young tauren showing an aptitude for marksmanship and tracking are passed an etched message. Handed down through Grull Hawkwind, the note carries word that Lanka Farshot has taken notice of the youth's bloodline and raw capability, urging them to formalize their study beneath his watchful eye. To the Shu'halo, a hunter is far more than a simple scout or warrior. Hunters sustain the tribes through their quarry, protect nomadic encampments, and live in close balance with the beasts of Kalimdor. By calling the novice into training, Lanka sets the groundwork for mastering weapons, understanding the creatures of Mulgore, and eventually undertaking the ancient art of taming wild companions.

quest:3094.text: Verdant Note. The Verdant Note is a formal summons delivered to promising young tauren in the Red Cloud Mesa. Entrusted by Grull Hawkwind, the message bids budding protectors of the wilds to seek out the druidic mentor Gart Mistrunner at Camp Narache. Young tauren stepping into their responsibilities on the Red Cloud Mesa are quickly singled out for their natural gifts. Grull Hawkwind passes along this missive on behalf of a messenger sent by Gart Mistrunner. The note acts as an invitation into the ancient fold of tauren druidism, calling the initiate away from basic village errands to heed the whispering balance of the plains. Upon answering the summons, Gart Mistrunner warns the fledgling druid that ancestral and natural spirits have grown restless across Mulgore. Tauren druids are tasked to act as living avatars of nature, keeping harmony with the will of the Earthmother regardless of distant rivalries. While night elves also practice druidic arts, Gart cautions that their pride blinds them to the tauren's own deep-seated bond with the natural realm.

quest:3096.text: Encrypted Scroll. The Encrypted Scroll is a discreet summons delivered to freshly awakened Forsaken rogues in Deathknell. Passed along by Shadow Priest Sarvis, the cipher directs the recruit to David Trias, a rogue mentor operating quietly out of the local inn. While newly raised Forsaken battle mindless zombies in the cemetery, the settlement's leadership takes note of those with particular inclinations toward stealth and subterfuge. Shadow Priest Sarvis passes this sealed parchment to promising scouts once their initial readiness is proven. Stamped with the discreet seal of David Trias, it serves as an early introduction to the shadowy network operating beneath the Forsaken hierarchy. David Trias watches the crossroads and inn of Deathknell, scouting prospects for future clandestine operations. Rather than seeking common thieves or reckless cutpurses, the Forsaken require disciplined covert operatives to serve the fledgling kingdom. Trias hints that capable rogues may eventually catch the eye of the Shadowstalkers, a dedicated cadre within the Forsaken who prize cunning, precision, and absolute loyalty to the Dark Lady.

quest:3097.text: Hallowed Scroll. The Hallowed Scroll is an introductory summons directed to newly awoken Forsaken priests in Deathknell. Handed over by Shadow Priest Sarvis, the missive calls the novice to Dark Cleric Duesten inside the shattered village chapel to learn how the undead wield faith after death. As newly awakened undead stagger from the graves of Deathknell, their minds are often reeling from the trauma of the plague, death, and sudden liberation from the Lich King's grip. For those who were once devout followers of the Holy Light in life, confusion runs exceptionally deep. While fledgling undead battle the mindless Scourge haunting the settlement's perimeter, Shadow Priest Sarvis intercepts incoming messages. Bearing the mark of Dark Cleric Duesten, the hallowed scroll bids newly risen priests to abandon their wandering and report to the desecrated town chapel. Upon delivering the scroll, a novice encounters the harsh theology of Forsaken priesthood. Dark Cleric Duesten pulls no punches: the Holy Light abandoned them in death, ancestral spirits are hollow tales, and planar demons have no interest in their plight. Instead, Forsaken clergy teach that sheer willpower and radical self-reliance are the only true sources of salvation. Under Duesten's tutelage, newly risen practitioners learn to channel both divine discipline and shadow, wielding power not out of devotion to distant gods, but out of absolute conviction in their own survival.

quest:3098.text: Glyphic Scroll. The Glyphic Scroll is an official summons delivered to newly awakened Forsaken mages in Deathknell. Bearing the seal of the mage trainer Isabella, the parchment directs promising practitioners of the arcane to seek her out in the desecrated village church to hone their volatile powers. When a freshly raised Forsaken demonstrates an affinity for arcane magic while culling mindless Scourge around Deathknell, they quickly catch the attention of their elders. Delivered by hand, the Glyphic Scroll is marked with the arcane sigil of Isabella, the local mage instructor. It bids the newly risen practitioner to report to her station within the ruined church, recognizing that unregulated magical aptitude poses as much danger to the Forsaken as it does to their enemies. Within the ruined chapel of Deathknell, Isabella instructs fledglings that death has not exempted them from the perils of the arcane. While mortality has stripped away their physical frailties, the volatile pull and corrupting nature of magic linger just as fiercely. For the Forsaken, pursuing arcane dominance is not merely an intellectual pursuit, but an instrument of survival and vengeance—a means to reclaim their destiny and obliterate any who challenge their fragile reclamation of Lordaeron.

quest:310.text: Bitter Rivals. Bitter Rivals is an early Alliance quest in Dun Morogh born from the fierce competition between two proud dwarven brewing families. Marleth Barleybrew sends an adventurer to infiltrate the Thunderbrew Distillery in Kharanos and tamper with their rival's stock. Few things in Khaz Modan stir passions as quickly as a pint of ale. The Barleybrews have long bristled under the shadow of the famed Thunderbrew Distillery in Kharanos. While Marleth Barleybrew begrudgingly concedes that Thunderbrew craft is respectable, she cannot stomach the notion that it is the only renowned vintage in Dun Morogh. To shake up the local palate, she devises a plan to swap a cask of Thunder Ale with her own fiery concoction, Barleybrew Scalder. Carrying out the scheme requires slipping directly beneath the noses of Kharanos patrons. Beneath the kitchen of the distillery lies the basement storeroom where aging casks await tapping. Because the Thunderbrews keep a guard posted near their most prized reserve, a would-be saboteur must find a way to lure the watchman away before secretly substituting the barrels.

quest:3103.text: Hallowed Letter. The Hallowed Letter is a formal summons given to promising young priests by Marshal McBride on behalf of Northshire Abbey's resident trainer, Priestess Anetta. It marks the start of a fledgling priest's formal mentorship in the tenets of the Holy Light amidst a troubled and vulnerable world. After proving their mettle against the kobold camps around Northshire, novitiate priests are handed a missive bearing the sacred seal of Priestess Anetta. Delivered through Marshal McBride, the letter serves as an invitation to begin serious study of the Holy Light within the abbey's quiet halls. When presented with the letter, Priestess Anetta impresses upon her new pupil the grim state of the realm. Lingering threats from the Burning Legion cast long shadows across Azeroth, while the continents struggle with fresh wounds and unrest. In her eyes, taking up the mantle of a priest is not merely an academic devotion, but an urgent moral responsibility to bring healing and solace to a suffering world.

quest:3104.text: Glyphic Letter. The Glyphic Letter is a formal summons delivered to novice human mages inside Northshire Valley by Marshal McBride. Written under the arcane seal of Khelden Bremen, the note calls promising spellcasters into Northshire Abbey to begin their formal tutelage in the arcane arts. Once an aspiring apprentice proves their capability by aiding Marshal McBride against the local vermin, the garrison commander hands them a message marked with arcane runes. The letter comes directly from Khelden Bremen, Northshire's resident mage trainer, who monitors new recruits arriving at the abbey for signs of magical discipline and talent. Northshire Abbey has historically served as a sanctuary for the Holy Light, yet the ongoing perils facing Stormwind require practitioners of every discipline. Answering the letter leads the novice upstairs to Khelden Bremen. Rather than offering easy praise, the tutor delivers a stark warning: mastering arcane power demands defiance of natural limits, inviting both profound respect and deep-seated fear from ordinary folk.

quest:3105.text: Tainted Letter. The Tainted Letter is a discreet summons delivered to novice human warlocks training in Northshire Valley. Entrusted to Marshal McBride by the secretive trainer Drusilla La Salle, the missive calls initiates away from the prying eyes of the Abbey guards to begin their formal instruction in the fel arts. While priests and paladins study openly within the sanctified halls of Northshire Abbey, practitioners of darker magic must tread carefully. Upon proving their capability against the local kobold menace, novice warlocks receive a letter passed along by Marshal McBride. Bearing the insignia of Drusilla La Salle, the missive instructs the fledgling spellcaster to report directly to her secluded post outside the abbey's main walls before pursuing any other duties. Meeting Drusilla reveals the precarious nature of walking the path of a warlock under the watchful eyes of Stormwind's guards, whom she dismisses as 'pathetic mundanes.' Drusilla offers a frank warning to her student: drawing power from the Twisting Nether and communing with demons carries an ever-present risk of corruption. While she counsels patience, prudence, and unwavering self-control to avoid falling prey to the dark energies they manipulate, she makes it clear that such caution should never extinguish one's burning ambition.

quest:3106.text: Simple Rune. Simple Rune is an introductory task given to novice dwarven warriors in Coldridge Valley. Passed along by Sten Stoutarm on behalf of the warrior trainer Thran Khorman, it directs fresh recruits inside Anvilmar to begin their martial training. As young recruits clear pests and prove their grit around Coldridge Valley, veteran scouts keep a watchful eye out for promising fighters. Sten Stoutarm delivers an inscribed stone—a simple rune—handed off to him by Thran Khorman. This summons calls martial hopefuls from the snowy valley paths into the warm forge-hall of Anvilmar to formally pledge themselves to the warrior's trade. Reporting to Thran offers an immediate glimpse into the harsh realities facing modern Dun Morogh. The veteran trainer speaks frankly about the kingdom's shifting landscape: displaced gnomes seeking refuge after catastrophic explosions destroyed Gnomeregan, fellow dwarves wielding foreign arcane arts or taking up human devotion to the Holy Light, and an ever-present menace of subterranean troggs clawing at the mountain borders. In Thran's eyes, solid martial discipline remains the bedrock required to withstand it all.

quest:3107.text: Consecrated Rune. The Consecrated Rune is an introductory summons delivered to fledgling dwarven paladins in Coldridge Valley. Passed along by Sten Stoutarm on behalf of Bromos Grummner, it marks an initiate's formal induction into the Knights of the Silver Hand.
