quest:405.text: The Prodigal Lich. Following your service in Brill against Scourge remnants and rot hide gnolls, Magistrate Sevren directs you south to the Undercity. Bethor Iceshard, a prominent archmage in the Magic Quarter, requires a capable operative for a sensitive mission regarding a wayward lich. Having proven your capability in the ruined town of Brill, Magistrate Sevren deems you worthy of higher-level Forsaken endeavors. Bethor Iceshard, a formidable mage dwelling in the Undercity's Magic Quarter, has demanded an agent tested in combat against the Scourge. Sevren hands over official orders, dispatching you beneath the ruins of Lordaeron into the subterranean corridors of the Forsaken capital. While Sevren admits ignorance of the exact specifics, he reveals that the task revolves around finding and recruiting a rogue lich. Liches are among the most lethal spellcasters raised by the Scourge, making any interaction fraught with peril. When you deliver the orders to Bethor atop his arcane sanctum, the icy mage cuts straight to business, eager to assess whether Brill's magistrate has sent someone strong enough to handle such dangerous quarry.

quest:407.text: Fields of Grief. Fields of Grief concludes Apothecary Johaan's experiment to weaponize ordinary pumpkins gathered from Solliden Farmstead. Having infused the crop with his latest alchemical concotion, Johaan dispatches you to feed the laced vegetable to a captive Scarlet Crusader languishing in Brill. Apothecary Johaan of the Royal Apothecary Society believes the Forsaken must exploit every tactical advantage to fend off the Scourge from the north and human incursions from the south. Rather than relying solely on raw blade-work or dark sorcery, the Society seeks to harness ordinary staples of the land. By tainting the pumpkins recovered from the mortal farmers of Solliden Farmstead, Johaan intends to prove that even common produce can be transformed into an instrument of death on behalf of the Dark Lady.

quest:408.text: The Family Crypt. The Family Crypt is a Horde quest tasking players with confronting the Scourge inside the Agamand Family Crypt. Commanded by Magistrate Sevren in Brill, adventurers must destroy the raised Agamand ancestors and slay the skeletal Scourge commander, Captain Dargol. While the Forsaken have carved out a fragile dominion in Tirisfal Glades, remnants of the Lich King's Scourge remain deeply entrenched in the countryside. The Agamand Mills, once a prosperous flour-producing heartland of Lordaeron, have become a dangerous Scourge stronghold. Magistrate Sevren in Brill watches this military buildup with grave concern, knowing that every inch yielded to mindless undead undermines the Forsaken's independence. The center of the local Scourge occupation is the Agamand Family Crypt, where the skeletal commander Captain Dargol has set up headquarters. Using dark necromancy, Dargol has dragged generations of Agamand family dead from their rest, twisting them into Rotting and Wailing Ancestors to swell his ranks. Sevren dispatches Forsaken agents to purge the crypt, lay the disturbed dead back to rest, and severed Dargol's head to shatter Scourge coordination in northern Tirisfal.

quest:409.text: Proving Allegiance. Proving Allegiance is the crucial trial presented by Gunther Arcanus to determine whether you truly serve the free-willed Forsaken or the Lich King. To earn the solitary necromancer's trust, you are sent to summon and destroy Lillith Nefara, a dangerous Scourge operative lurking near his island. Gunther Arcanus has isolated himself on an island in Brightwater Lake since rising into undeath, fiercely clinging to his autonomy. Though Bethor Iceshard's magical enchantments on Gunther's spellbook confirmed the emissary does not carry the foul taint of the Scourge, words and charms are not enough for the paranoid hermit. To earn his confidence, an outsider must demonstrate active hostility toward the minions of the Lich King through decisive violence.

quest:410.text: The Dormant Shade. The Dormant Shade is a dark ritual performed at Gunther's Retreat on Brightwater Lake in Tirisfal Glades. By placing a mystic candle upon an old, blood-soaked table, a traveler summons forth the Scourge agent Lillith Nefara, whose defeat proves to Gunther Arcanus that the visitor is the Lich King's foe. On the island of Gunther's Retreat in Brightwater Lake rests a battered, bloody dinner table. Far from an ordinary piece of neglected domestic furniture, it serves as the physical focus for a sinister conjuration. Stained with dried gore and abandoned to the shadows, the table acts as a makeshift ritual slab where death and dark magic linger.

quest:411.text: The Prodigal Lich Returns. The Prodigal Lich Returns marks the conclusion of the effort to recruit Gunther Arcanus into the Forsaken. Having proven your intentions and restored his grimoire, you carry an arcane communion gem back to Bethor Iceshard in the Undercity. Gunther Arcanus spent years isolated on an island in Brightwater Lake, having broken free from the Lich King's grip through sheer force of will, completely unaware that Sylvanas Windrunner had liberated Lordaeron. Bitter and suspicious of outsiders, Gunther distrusted the emissaries of the Undercity until an adventurer returned his spellbook and proved their hostility toward the Scourge. Satisfied that his visitor was not an enemy, Gunther entrusted them with a Nether Gem to establish contact with his former colleague.

quest:412.text: Operation Recombobulation. Operation Recombobulation is a bold engineering effort orchestrated by Razzle Sprysprocket in Kharanos. In response to the tragedy of Gnomeregan, Razzle and Ozzie Togglevolt seek to reverse the horrific transformation of their afflicted kin into leper gnomes using an experimental contraption known as the Recombobulator. When radiation flooded Gnomeregan to purge the trogg menace, it failed to destroy the invaders and instead warped the majority of the gnomish population into deranged, sickly leper gnomes. Refusing to accept this tragic mutation as permanent, inventor Razzle Sprysprocket has partnered with Ozzie Togglevolt to develop a technological cure: the Recombobulator. Their audacious goal is nothing less than restoring their mutated brethren back to health and sanity. Building a delicate prototype requires precise components, namely Restabilization Cogs and Gyromechanic Gears. In an ironic twist of fate, these essential parts are salvaged directly from the hostile leper gnomes wandering outside the sealed gates of Gnomeregan. By harvesting mechanical debris from their corrupted brothers and sisters, Razzle hopes to assemble the very device that will undo their shared tragedy.

quest:413.text: Shimmer Stout. Following the creation of his experimental Shimmer Stout in Brewnall Village, Rejold Barleybrew asks travelers to carry a fresh barrel out to his brother Wellart. Wellart serves as a dwarf Mountaineer stationed at the southern guard tower guarding the pass toward Loch Modan, where a cold post makes a strong drink all the more welcome. Rejold Barleybrew has perfected his new creation, Shimmer Stout, using shimmering fronds gathered from the icy crags of Dun Morogh. While the rest of the Barleybrew family dedicates their craft to the vats and kegs of Brewnall Village, Rejold's brother Wellart chose the life of a Mountaineer. Knowing the lonely conditions of guard duty on the frontier, Rejold sends a fresh barrel along with passing travelers as both a brotherly favor and a true taste test. Wellart Barleybrew is stationed at the southern guard tower flanking the South Gate Pass into Loch Modan. High atop the mountain pass, the Mountaineers endure bitter winds and occasional beast attacks while keeping watch over travelers walking the mountain road. Running low on drink and restless for excitement, Wellart finds that Shimmer Stout delivers quite a punch—so much so that it seems to brighten his vision in the dim mountain night.

quest:414.text: Stout to Kadrell. Stout to Kadrell is an Alliance delivery quest that leads travelers out of the frozen heights of Dun Morogh and into the temperate valley of Loch Modan. Entrusted with a cask of Rejold Barleybrew's newly perfected Shimmer Stout, you carry the potent brew across the territorial border to share with Mountaineer Kadrell on patrol in Thelsamar. After tasting the newly finished Shimmer Stout created by his brother Rejold, Mountaineer Barleybrew is convinced it is too good to keep entirely within Dun Morogh. Stationed at the eastern border post guarding the mountain passes, Barleybrew looks out toward his kin guarding neighboring lands. Dwarven mountaineering can be a cold, grueling assignment, and a stout heart calls for stout drink. Wanting an honest appraisal from a fellow patrolman on the line, Barleybrew sends a cask eastward with passing travelers bound for Loch Modan. The journey marks a natural rite of passage for young dwarven and gnomish adventurers who have spent their early days among the snowbound crags of Dun Morogh. Passing southeast through the South Gate Outpost and traversing the long tunnels cut through the mountain bedrock, travelers suddenly emerge into the warmer, wooded basin of Loch Modan. Patrolling along the road through the settlement of Thelsamar, Mountaineer Kadrell gladly takes a break from his vigil to tap the cask, discovering that Barleybrew's new recipe has an astonishing kick.

quest:415.text: Rejold's New Brew. Rejold's New Brew is an Alliance errand in Dun Morogh summoning an adventurer back to Brewnall Village. Having perfected a new concoction using gathered Shimmerweed, brewmaster Rejold Barleybrew wants a trusted friend to sample his latest recipe. It serves as the bridge between gathering brewing supplies and distributing his prized Shimmer Stout across the mountain realm. Word spreads quickly through Dun Morogh when a dwarven brewer strikes gold in his cellar. After securing Shimmerweed from the bitter slopes, local contacts like Tharek Blackstone or Pilot Bellowfiz urge passing adventurers to report back to Brewnall Village. Rejold Barleybrew has finished fermenting his experimental batches and is eager to share the spoils with the traveler who made it possible. Brewnall Village thrives on distinct ale craft, and Barleybrew's newest batch is no ordinary draught. Infusing local herbs into his mash produced a distinct beverage known as Shimmer Stout. Before shipping barrels off to neighboring outposts and thirsty patrons in Loch Modan, Rejold insists that the adventurer who risked life and limb for the herbs gets the honor of the inaugural sip.

quest:4161.text: Recipe of the Kaldorei. Recipe of the Kaldorei is a lesson in balance taught by Zarrin, a culinary instructor in Dolanaar. By gathering a precise number of spider legs across Teldrassil, aspiring cooks learn that sustaining oneself from nature requires restraint and respect. Behind the inn in Dolanaar, Zarrin tends a bubbling cauldron and instructs young adventurers on the traditions of his people. Long before the modern age, night elves knew themselves as the kaldorei, meaning 'children of the stars.' For Zarrin, understanding that ancestral heritage begins not on the battlefield, but in the relationship between a hunter, their food, and the surrounding boughs of Teldrassil. The core of the lesson lies in restraint. Zarrin charges his pupils with gathering small spider legs from the woodland arachnids outside Shadowglen, but specifically commands that only seven be taken—no more. In night elven culture, living in harmony with nature demands taking strictly what is necessary and returning kindness to the wild. This delicate balance must be upheld even in troubled times, a philosophy that transforms a simple spider kabob into a moral discipline.

quest:417.text: A Pilot's Revenge. Following the trail of a missing dwarven siege engine pilot leads to a frozen corpse in the wilds of Dun Morogh. Found among the remains, Hildelve's personal journal details his fatal struggle against a notorious predator known as Mangeclaw, leaving behind a dying wish for vengeance. Pilot Hildelve did not survive his time stranded in the rugged snowy crags. When travelers locate his remains, they discover his journal resting beside him. In his last penned words, Hildelve recorded a savage encounter with a massive Ice Claw bear he named Mangeclaw. Though he managed to fend off the monstrosity initially, the injuries proved severe, and the beast eventually returned to finish off the weakened pilot. Knowing his end was near, Hildelve wrote down one final plea in his journal: retribution against the monster that took his life. Returning to Pilot Hammerfoot with the journal and a claw torn from the fallen beast brings grim closure to the Ironforge Siege Brigade, honoring their lost comrade and removing a deadly menace from the mountain paths.

quest:418.text: Thelsamar Blood Sausages. In the bustling town of Thelsamar, cook Vidra Hearthstove keeps the local laborers and miners fed with a famous highland staple: blood sausages. Preparing this hearty dwarven fare requires freshly gathered ingredients from the surrounding valley of Loch Modan. Thelsamar is never short on hungry appetites. Between energetic children and weary miners returning from the Ironband Excavation, Vidra Hearthstove works tirelessly over the tavern stove. To keep the populace fed and satisfied, she relies on a local culinary tradition known across Loch Modan: savory blood sausages made from the wildlife wandering the rugged mountain pass. While traditional blood sausage relies on fresh blood, seasoned meat, and natural casings, Vidra's recipe reflects the rugged pragmatism of the dwarves. Boar intestines provide the casings, bear meat forms the dense filling, and spider ichor is added to lend a sharp, pungent bite. Though collecting venomous fluid and entrails is not for the faint of heart, the result is a regional favorite that travelers quickly learn to appreciate.

quest:419.text: The Lost Pilot. Pilot Hammerfoot fears the worst for his comrade, Mori Hildelve, who ventured into the craggy hills of Dun Morogh on foot after wrecking his siege engine. Hildelve was searching for a rare ore vital for potent blastpowder, but days have passed amidst unsettling roars echoing through the peaks. Dwarven siege engines are formidable war machines, but even iron treads struggle against the treacherous, jagged ridges of Dun Morogh. While scouring the slopes for a rare mineral deposit required to produce high-grade blastpowder, Pilot Mori Hildelve pushed his engine too far up a steep hill and busted the machine. Undeterred by the breakdown, Hildelve ordered his companion, Pilot Hammerfoot, to stay behind and guard the broken machinery while he pressed higher into the frozen wilderness on foot. Days went by with no sign of Hildelve returning to camp. In the dead of night, strange and vicious beastly growls began echoing down from the rocky crags, turning Hammerfoot's mild impatience into creeping dread. Though Hildelve had a reputation for being as tough as nails, surviving the frigid heights of Dun Morogh without mechanized armor or heavy support against prowling predators is a dangerous gamble.

quest:420.text: Senir's Observations. This errand completes a scouting line out of Coldridge Valley, carrying Grelin Whitebeard's completed report through the trogg-infested pass to his brother Senir in Kharanos. It bridges the secluded training grounds of Anvilmar with the broader troubles facing Dun Morogh. Through Senir's candid reception, travelers catch their first glimpse of political friction simmering between field scouts and the Ironforge Senate. After Grelin Whitebeard recovers his stolen journal from the Frostmane trolls, he prepares a detailed report of the valley's threats for his brother Senir. Mountaineer Thalos, stationed guarding the gate out of Coldridge Valley, entrusts passing adventurers with carrying this dispatch. Leaving the relative seclusion of the introductory vale means braving the tunnel cut through the mountain, which has recently been overrun by violent troggs ambushing all traffic. Travelers who punch through emerge onto the snowblown highways of central Dun Morogh, following the main road straight into the cozy hub of Kharanos. Senir Whitebeard, found seeking warmth over drinks at the Thunderbrew Distillery in Kharanos, greets newcomers with rough mountaineer hospitality. Reading through Grelin's findings, Senir chuckles over his brother's aggressive rhetoric. Grelin liberally invokes the name of King Magni Bronzebeard to press for urgent action, an assertive tactic Senir notes is bound to agitate the stubborn Ironforge Senate. Senir admits he has fallen behind on filing his own observations due to the bitter cold, but receiving Grelin's dispatch nudges him back into service, opening further work monitoring hostile forces across the snowfields.

quest:421.text: Prove Your Worth. Prove Your Worth is an introductory Horde quest offered by Dalar Dawnweaver at the Sepulcher in Silverpine Forest. To assist the Forsaken campaign against southern human and dwarven territories, adventurers are tasked with thinning the feral worgen prowling near the roadside. It marks the opening step in unraveling the arcane fallout wrought by Archmage Arugal. Lady Sylvanas Windrunner and her dreadlord lieutenant, Varimathras, have set their sights on securing the regions south of Tirisfal Glades, including human and dwarven enclaves. However, the path through Silverpine Forest remains fraught with danger. Instead of an open staging ground, the Forsaken find their supply lines and forward bases threatened by feral Moonrage worgen that roam the pine-choked hills. The presence of these beasts is no natural occurrence. Dalar Dawnweaver points the finger directly at Arugal, a disgraced former mage of Dalaran who unleashed otherworldly worgen upon the region during the Scourge invasion. Arugal has since claimed Shadowfang Keep, letting his feral creations overrun the forest. Before Dalar will entrust soldiers with deeper investigations into Arugal's sorcery, recruits must demonstrate their martial prowess by culling the nearest Moonrage Whitescalps.

quest:422.text: Arugal's Folly. Assigned by Dalar Dawnweaver at the Sepulcher, this quest tasks Forsaken agents with securing Arugal's earliest spellbooks from a nearby farmstead. Uncovering the magic behind the worgen curse is vital for the Forsaken to turn it against the mad mage and secure Silverpine Forest. Recovering the Remedy of Arugal marks the first step in unraveling the threat looming from Shadowfang Keep. Dalar Dawnweaver, an ambitious Forsaken mage residing in the crypts of the Sepulcher, holds no respect for Archmage Arugal. To Dawnweaver, Arugal was an unremarkable practitioner whose inclusion in the Kirin Tor was baffling and whose magical understanding seemed amateurish. However, the monstrous beasts now roaming Silverpine cannot be ignored. To break Arugal's hold on the region, Dawnweaver intends to deconstruct the spells that unleashed the worgen upon Lordaeron.

quest:423.text: Arugal's Folly. This task sends Forsaken agents to collect enchanted shackles from Moonrage worgen roaming Silverpine Forest. Dalar Dawnweaver, analyzing Arugal's notes, aims to unravel how the renegade mage artificially reinforced his unstable magic. Studying these bindings brings the Forsaken closer to dismantling the worgen threat plaguing the region. Upon inspecting Arugal's recovered research, Dalar Dawnweaver expresses utter contempt for his former peer. According to Dalar, Arugal was never fit to serve Dalaran, let alone handle high sorcery during the kingdom's direst hour. To compensate for his mediocre talent, Arugal relied on enchanted relics and hardware to bolster and bind his summoned worgen beasts. Dalar requires physical samples of these items to dissect the magical tether holding the monsters together. The cursed inhabitants of Silverpine, transformed into Moonrage worgen, wander the woods carrying physical manifestations of Arugal's binding enchantments. Moonrage Gluttons and Moonrage Darksouls stalk the regions to the north and east of the Sepulcher. Prized for the residual arcane energy woven into their metal, their heavy shackles serve as crucial specimens for Dawnweaver's counter-research against Shadowfang Keep.

quest:425.text: Ivar the Foul. Ivar the Foul is a quest in Silverpine Forest that marks the culmination of the reconnaissance mission undertaken by Deathstalkers Rane and Quinn Yorick. Trapped at the farmstead known as the Ivar Patch, Rane asks Horde travelers to eliminate the savage ghoul Ivar the Foul so Quinn can recover from his mauling and complete their report to High Executor Hadrec. Siblings Rane and Quinn Yorick were deployed by the Deathstalkers to conduct reconnaissance across Silverpine Forest on behalf of High Executor Hadrec at the Sepulcher. Their reconnaissance grinded to a sudden, violent halt when moving through a farmstead in the northern forest, where they were ambushed by the vicious ghoul known as Ivar the Foul. Though the scouts managed to escape with their unlives, Quinn was severely mauled in the confrontation. Even after receiving an alchemical remedy concocted from forest beasts, Quinn remains too frail to march. Knowing Ivar prowls the nearby barn waiting for Rane's guard to falter, Rane calls upon Horde adventurers to storm the barn, sever Ivar's head, and permanently secure the homestead.

quest:426.text: The Mills Overrun. Tasked by Deathguard Dillinger in Brill, this mission sends Forsaken soldiers to break the Scourge's foothold at the nearby Agamand Mills. Mindless undead gather among the ruined windmills, threatening to establish a forward base dangerously close to Tirisfal Glades' settlements. To halt this staging ground, recruits must shatter the ranks of skeletal soldiers and bonecasters. The Agamand Mills once anchored the agricultural heart of Tirisfal Glades, but in the wake of the Third War, their windmills overlook a far grimmer harvest. Scourge forces under the Lich King's thrall have begun massing on the grounds. If these mindless thralls successfully secure the mills, they will have an entrenched base of operations from which to push deeper into Tirisfal and strike directly at the fledgling Forsaken holdings. Deathguard Dillinger wastes little time on sentiment. Tasked with fortifying Brill and policing the territory, Dillinger orders recruits to hunt down Rattlecage and Cracked Skull Soldiers alongside Darkeye Bonecasters. By demanding notched ribs and blackened skulls as proof of their destruction, Dillinger ensures the skeletal ranks are being physically battered apart, throwing the mindless remnants back toward the Plaguelands before their offensive can truly begin.

quest:427.text: At War With The Scarlet Crusade. Executor Zygand in Brill coordinates the Forsaken campaign against the Scarlet Crusade in Tirisfal Glades. Using intelligence recovered by Executor Arren, you are dispatched to eliminate Scarlet Warriors stationed at a guard tower west of the Solliden Farmstead. This assault marks the Forsaken military's opening offensive to purge the zealous crusaders from their borders. The fledgling Forsaken state under Lady Sylvanas Windrunner faces simultaneous threats on multiple fronts. While the Deathguard keeps a wary vigil against the swelling armies of the Lich King, the fanatical mortals of the Scarlet Crusade contest Forsaken dominance over their former homeland. The Crusade considers all undead abominations to be purged with fire and blade, blind to the fact that the Forsaken have broken free of the Scourge's control. Thanks to intelligence documents secured by Executor Arren at Deathknell, Executor Zygand now knows the exact encampments and outposts held by the zealots across Tirisfal Glades. With regular Deathguard garrisons occupied by Scourge containment, independent Forsaken champions are commissioned to strike out directly. The first strike falls upon the guard tower west of Solliden Farmstead, where Scarlet Warriors muster and threaten the western approaches to Brill.

quest:428.text: Lost Deathstalkers. Lost Deathstalkers is a reconnaissance mission assigned by High Executor Hadrec at the Sepulcher. Two Forsaken scouts, Rane and Quinn Yorick, went missing weeks ago while surveying the haunted farmsteads of northern Silverpine Forest. Tracking them down reveals not only their fate, but the encroaching perils that threaten the Forsaken hold on the region. The Deathstalkers serve as the eyes, ears, and hidden daggers of Lady Sylvanas and the Forsaken. When operatives go silent, command takes notice. High Executor Hadrec deployed the scouts Rane and Quinn Yorick into northern Silverpine Forest weeks ago to monitor the abandoned farms and watch for enemy movements. Having received no courier or report since their departure, Hadrec fears the duo met a grim end at the hands of the Scourge or worse. Northern Silverpine is rife with danger, situated between the ruined estates of Lordaeron and the shadowed borders of Tirisfal Glades. Wandering undead, prowling beasts, and feral worgen make unescorted travel perilous even for seasoned rogues. Tracking the Yoricks requires searching the dilapidated northern farmsteads where their reconnaissance first began, hoping to recover whatever intelligence they gathered before danger overwhelmed them.

quest:429.text: Wild Hearts. Wild Hearts is a Horde quest in Silverpine Forest tasked by Rane Yorick. To save her brother Quinn from wounds inflicted by the ghoul Ivar the Foul, you must harvest discolored worg hearts and deliver them to Apothecary Renferrel at the Sepulcher for an alchemical remedy. Following the disastrous mission that left the Deathstalkers pinned down at a farm in northern Silverpine, Rane Yorick finds herself attending to her severely wounded brother, Quinn. The feral ghoul Ivar the Foul left Quinn mangled and failing to recover. Knowing conventional rest will not restore an undead body torn by such savagery, Rane looks to the macabre arts of the Royal Apothecary Society to stitch her brother back together. Silverpine's wolves have not escaped the dark corruption plaguing northern Lordaeron. The local worgs carry corrupted, discolored hearts that contain uniquely potent essences. While vile to ordinary eyes, the Royal Apothecaries have learned to distill these blighted organs into concoctions capable of revitalizing withered Forsaken flesh.

quest:430.text: Return to Quinn. Return to Quinn is a Horde quest in Silverpine Forest where an adventurer delivers a restorative draught concocted by Apothecary Renferrel to the wounded Deathstalker Quinn Yorick. Trapped and weakened at the Ivar Patch north of the Sepulcher, Quinn requires the draught before he can contemplate returning to duty. Following the harvesting of wild beast hearts for the Royal Apothecary Society, Apothecary Renferrel at the Sepulcher brews a restorative potion formulated to aid Quinn Yorick. Renferrel has little time for sentimentality or bedside manners, quickly handing off the mixture to return to his own clandestine alchemical research, leaving the adventurer to run the courier run back into the wilderness. Quinn Yorick hides beside his sister, Deathstalker Rane Yorick, amid the ruined farmstead known as the Ivar Patch. Severely hurt by the ghoul Ivar the Foul and unable to march through hostile territory, Quinn drinks the draught immediately upon arrival. While the concoction restores his strength enough to eventually travel, the surrounding territory remains fraught with danger, particularly under the watchful malice of the ghoul lurking nearby.

quest:431.text: Candles of Beckoning. Candles of Beckoning is a brief task centered around salvaging specialized ritual tapers discovered in Tirisfal Glades. These eerie tallow candles are steeped in dark practices and recovered from a crate on Gunther's Retreat, Gunther Arcanus's island in Brightwater Lake. The crate on Gunther's Retreat supplies the Candle of Beckoning used in his test of allegiance. Gunther asks an adventurer to take a candle to the old, bloody altar just off the island's southern coast, light it, and confront the Scourge agent Lillith Nefara. The crate holding these candles sits on Gunther's Retreat, the island in Brightwater Lake where the lich Gunther Arcanus dwells. A single candle is all that is needed for the test Gunther sets in Proving Allegiance: lit upon the old, bloody altar off the island's southern coast, it awakens the Scourge agent Lillith Nefara.

quest:432.text: Those Blasted Troggs!. Foreman Stonebrow is at his wit's end after troggs completely overran his operations at Gol'Bolar Quarry. Destructive and aggressive, the beasts have trashed his mining equipment and powder barrels, leaving him furious and demanding retaliation. Unable to fight them himself due to failing aim, he pays brave adventurers to head down into the pit and cull the brute Skullthumpers. Gol'Bolar Quarry was once a proud, productive dwarf excavation site nestled in the snowy hills of eastern Dun Morogh. That prosperity ended abruptly when subterranean troggs broke through the bedrock and swarmed the lower terraces. Instead of merely occupying the tunnels, the savages have wreaked wanton havoc, smashing scaffolding and blowing through precious barrels of blasting powder. Watching the ruin of his life's work from the safety of the ridge has pushed Foreman Stonebrow to the brink of apoplexy. Frustrated by his own aging hands and poor aim, he relies on passing wanderers and Alliance recruits to execute raw vengeance. Thinning the ranks of the burly Rockjaw Skullthumpers provides him a brief moment of relief, though nothing short of total extermination will truly satisfy his wrath.

quest:433.text: The Public Servant. Senator Mehr Stonehallow of Ironforge has traveled directly to Gol'Bolar Quarry to address the sudden trogg invasion threatening Dun Morogh's mining operations. Seeking to reclaim the site, he enlists adventurers to cut down the aggressive Rockjaw Bonesnappers so miners can return to work. It is rare to find a member of Ironforge's Senate standing in the slush and dirt of a contested mine, but Senator Mehr Stonehallow is no typical politician. Holding dual allegiance to the dwarven ruling body and the scholarly Explorers' League, Stonehallow has taken personal responsibility for organizing a response to the trogg infestation at Gol'Bolar Quarry. Rather than waiting for slow legislative measures, he directly contracts capable mercenaries and travelers to cull the invaders. Gol'Bolar Quarry was once a vital source of stone and mineral wealth for Dun Morogh, but deep excavations broke into previously sealed subterranean hollows. Primitive, savage troggs of the Rockjaw tribe flooded into the pits, wrecking delicate mining equipment and driving out civilian laborers. Stonehallow's objective is to clear out the vicious Rockjaw Bonesnappers, paving the way for Mountaineer garrisons to secure the quarry and restore iron-shoveling infrastructure.

quest:435.text: Escorting Erland. Trapped indoors by aggressive prowling predators, Deathstalker Erland requires an escort through Silverpine Forest to regroup with his partner. Assisting him safely across the wilderness delivers him directly to Deathstalker Rane Yorick. Even seasoned scouts of the Forsaken occasionally find themselves outmatched by the unforgiving ecology of Silverpine Forest. Deathstalker Erland finds himself cornered inside a dilapidated shelter, surrounded by starved wolves eager to pick at what little flesh remains on his withered frame. Alone, breaking through their pack is suicide. Erland's objective lies near the Ivar Patch, where his partner Deathstalker Rane Yorick maintains watch. The route cuts directly through predatory wolf territory. Once guided through the prowlers, Erland sprints the final stretch to reach the safety of Rane Yorick's outpost, where the scouts can consolidate their intelligence for the Undercity.

quest:437.text: The Dead Fields. The Dead Fields is an assault mission issued by High Executor Hadrec from the Sepulcher. Forsaken scouts discovered that the Rot Hide gnolls infesting an abandoned northern farmstead are led and shielded by the Scourge banshee Nightlash, whose destruction is critical to securing Silverpine Forest. North of the Sepulcher lies an abandoned farmstead known as the Dead Fields. Once ordinary farmland, the grounds are now choked by Rot Hide gnolls—pestilent, plagued scavengers that infest the Silverpine countryside. High Executor Hadrec previously sent small raiding parties to dislodge them, but every offensive stalled under unnatural magical resistance. The Rot Hides are not acting merely on feral instinct; they are reinforced by the Scourge. A banshee named Nightlash oversees the area, using dark sorcery to scatter Forsaken skirmishers whenever the gnolls face ruin. Hadrec dispatches Horde champions to cut down the gnolls until Nightlash is lured out, demanding her spectral essence as proof of her demise.

quest:445.text: Delivery to Silverpine Forest. This errand serves as a vital courier mission linking the Royal Apothecary Society's research in Brill with their ongoing efforts in Silverpine Forest. Tasked by Apothecary Johaan, you carry valuable findings to Apothecary Renferrel at the Sepulcher to aid the development of the Dark Lady's New Plague. The Royal Apothecary Society operates under the direct command of Lady Sylvanas Windrunner, tasked with concocting a New Plague capable of wiping out both the living and the Scourge. Isolated laboratories across Forsaken territory cannot work in a vacuum; survival and progress demand constant communication. In Brill, Apothecary Johaan has gathered experimental results that must be circulated to other researchers in the field without delay. Silverpine Forest represents the next frontier of Forsaken expansion and research. Based out of the Sepulcher, Apothecary Renferrel oversees biochemical testing amidst regional threats like the Moonrage worgen, rogue humans, and lingering Scourge. By receiving Johaan's notes from Tirisfal Glades, Renferrel integrates new alchemical findings into his own local experiments, further advancing the Society's grand design.

quest:447.text: A Recipe For Death. A Recipe For Death is an alchemical errand commissioned by Apothecary Renferrel at the Sepulcher in Silverpine Forest. Tasked with gathering grizzly bear hearts and arachnid blood, adventurers transport the volatile biological reagents to Master Apothecary Faranell in the Undercity to aid in formulating the Forsaken's lethal New Plague. Positioned on the front lines in Silverpine Forest, Apothecary Renferrel recognizes the grim arithmetic facing Sylvanas's people. Surrounded by the relentless legions of Arthas and enduring remnants of humanity, conventional warfare offers little hope. The Forsaken's grand ambition lies in developing a New Plague—an engineered contagion potent enough to rot both living humans and undead Scourge alike. Renferrel's field research determined that combining arachnid venom from the Skittering Dark with toxins concentrated in the hearts of native bears yields a virulent foundation. Once the harvested organs and blood are collected from the wilderness of Silverpine, they must be delivered beneath the ruins of Lordaeron into the heart of the Apothecarium. There, Master Apothecary Faranell oversees the grand design of the Royal Apothecary Society. Faranell immediately takes custody of Renferrel's samples, testing their contaminable properties to refine formulas that might one day secure Forsaken supremacy across the continent.

quest:449.text: The Deathstalkers' Report. The Deathstalkers' Report is a crucial military courier assignment delivered to High Executor Hadrec at the Sepulcher. After securing injured Deathstalkers in the northern wilds, you carry their gathered intelligence concerning unexpected Scourge activity back to Forsaken high command. This dispatch alters the Forsaken's assessment of their hold on Silverpine Forest. The Deathstalkers act as the eyes, ears, and daggers of the Dark Lady, pushing into the untamed wilderness ahead of standard military units. Near the border of Tirisfal and Silverpine, an advance patrol ran into catastrophic resistance while charting enemy movements. Though Deathstalker Quinn barely survived his injuries and Erland fought his way to safety, their scouting mission yielded intelligence essential to the Forsaken occupation of Silverpine Forest. When High Executor Hadrec reviews the sealed field report, it confirms dark news: the mindless forces of the Scourge have maintained a far heavier and more aggressive presence in Silverpine than Undercity strategists anticipated. Instead of merely securing abandoned human hamlets and pacifying rogue beasts, the Sepulcher command must brace for coordinated Scourge opposition while fighting to claim the region.

quest:4495.text: A Good Friend. Dirania Silvershine grows anxious when her regular visitor, Iverron, fails to appear on time at Aldrassil. Knowing he frequents the hills near the spider-infested Shadowthread Cave to the north, she asks passing adventurers to search for him. Daily routine runs deep in the tranquil boughs of Shadowglen, making any break in pattern stand out immediately. Dirania Silvershine, tending her affairs beneath the sheltering canopy of Aldrassil, is accustomed to visits from Iverron like clockwork every day. When hours pass without a sign of him, her concern drives her to seek assistance from those setting out into the wilds of the barrow bough. Iverron has a well-known habit of wandering near the northern hollows of Shadowglen, despite the encroaching menace of webwood spiders. With Shadowthread Cave crawling with aggressive arachnids, stepping off the established paths is increasingly hazardous for careless travelers. Searching the rugged slopes just west of the cavern mouth reveals Iverron tucked away in hiding, desperate for aid.

quest:456.text: The Balance of Nature. "The Balance of Nature" is the introductory quest offered to newly awakened night elves in Shadowglen. Bestowed by Conservator Ilthalaine, it charges young adventurers with culling overgrown populations of young nightsabers and thistle boars. The task introduces new heroes to the ancient kaldorei duty of stewarding and preserving the natural harmony of Teldrassil. Teldrassil may appear wild and ancient, but its ecosystems are young and fragile. In Shadowglen, sheltered beneath the Great Tree's sprawling boughs, heavy spring rains have disrupted the forest's delicate cycle. Certain wildlife populations flourished beyond the land's capacity to sustain them, threatening to strip the glen of resources and plunge the entire ecosystem into famine. Preserving the forest requires proactive stewardship. Conservator Ilthalaine watches over the woods of Shadowglen, ensuring that no single element overtakes another. To prevent mass starvation among the animals, he sends young night elves out into the grove to thin the thistle boars and predatory nightsabers. It is an unglamorous but vital responsibility, establishing the core philosophy of kaldorei culture: harmony with nature demands active balance and difficult decisions.

quest:457.text: The Balance of Nature. This task continues Conservator Ilthalaine's effort to preserve Shadowglen's fragile ecology by culling mature thistle boars and mangy nightsabers. As Teldrassil's wildlife multiplies unchecked, night elf guardians must step in to prevent the overpopulation of predators and foragers from stripping the boughs bare. While culling young animals stabilizes future growth, the adult populations of Shadowglen also pose an immediate threat to the World Tree's ecosystem. Conservator Ilthalaine directs young defenders deeper into the forest to hunt mature thistle boars and older, mangy nightsabers before their ravenous appetites exhaust the land's finite flora and game. North of Aldrassil, the forest shifts as younger cubs give way to mottled nightsabers and aggressive boars rooting up the soil. Though killing creatures of the wild is a grim duty, kaldorei doctrine views controlled hunting as a necessary responsibility to protect the whole forest from ecological collapse.

quest:458.text: The Woodland Protector. The Woodland Protector is an introductory task in Shadowglen given by the druid Melithar Staghelm. Alerted by the whisperings of forest spirits, Melithar asks you to seek out Tarindrella, an elusive dryad who has unexpectedly returned to the grove. Her presence hints that something troubling stirs beneath the canopy of Teldrassil. While training novices beneath the boughs of Aldrassil, Melithar Staghelm receives troubling omens from the woodland spirits. The dryad Tarindrella, regarded as a protector of the wild, has reappeared in Shadowglen after an absence from Kalimdor's woodlands spanning many years. Because dryads rarely emerge without cause, Melithar fears an imbalance in the natural order.

quest:459.text: The Woodland Protector. Tarindrella, a dryad tending to Shadowglen, seeks to uncover the source behind the sudden aggression of local creatures and the disappearance of the nearby furbolgs. By investigating the wild grells and gathering samples of corrupt Fel Moss, adventurers confirm that dark magic has begun to fester in the roots of the World Tree. Even within the secluded heights of Shadowglen, the tranquil nature of Teldrassil has begun to fracture. Dryads like Tarindrella have noticed a dark shift sweeping through the woods. The once-placid furbolgs abandoned their ancestral dens, reorganizing into the aggressive Gnarlpine tribe, while feral grells and grellkin began overrunning the woodland paths. Tarindrella suspects that unnatural corruption fuels the forest's hostility. By slaying the swarming grells and collecting samples of Fel Moss, you provide undeniable proof of dark enchantments clinging to the boughs of Teldrassil. With this grim truth confirmed, Tarindrella directs young defenders toward the village of Dolanaar to confer with Druid Athridas Bearmantle.

quest:4681.text: Washed Ashore. Washed Ashore is an investigation initiated by Gwennyth Bly'Leggonde in Auberdine to examine deceased marine life along Darkshore's mist-shrouded coast. Acting on behalf of the Temple of the Moon in Darnassus, she sends adventurers to inspect the skeletal remains of a giant sea turtle submerged west of the village. The research seeks to explain why so many sea creatures are stranding themselves or dying off the shore. The misty beaches of Darkshore have become a graveyard for oceanic giants. Beached behemoths and drowned leviathans line the sands and shallows, baffling the night elves of Auberdine. Having already looked into a grounded sea creature along the strand, Gwennyth Bly'Leggonde tasks travelers with diving into the waters west of the docks, near a sunken vessel, to examine the bones of a massive sea turtle and gather evidence for the Temple of the Moon.

quest:4722.text: Beached Sea Turtle. Along the misty, surf-battered shores of Darkshore lies the carcass of a massive beached sea turtle, surrounded by scavenging murlocs. Though picked over, viable biological samples can still be recovered from the remains. Naturalists in Auberdine collect such specimens to ship back to the Temple of the Moon in Darnassus for formal study. The long coastline of Darkshore frequently catches the casualties of the Great Sea, including massive ancient sea turtles that drift ashore after death or beach themselves in confusion. Once grounded, the carcasses quickly attract scavengers. Hostile Greymist murlocs have established crude camps around this turtle's skeletal frame, carving away flesh and shell. Despite their foraging, viable bone, shell, or tissue samples often remain intact within the wreckage. Gwennyth Bly'Leggonde, stationed in the settlement of Auberdine, serves as a field researcher documenting the unusual marine life and ecological disturbances along the coast. The night elves observe these stranded beasts with both reverence and scientific curiosity. Once recovered, suitable remains are carefully cataloged and prepared for shipment to scholars in Darnassus, who seek to understand why so many pelagic giants are washing ashore.

quest:4723.text: Beached Sea Creature. Along the fog-draped strand of Mist's Edge lies the massive carcass of a sea thresher, far larger than any native to Darkshore's shallows. While local murlocs pick through the carrion, naturalists in Auberdine seek bone samples to understand why such colossal deep-sea beasts are beaching themselves along the coast. The Mist's Edge coastline is no stranger to shipwrecks and tide-washed debris, but the sudden appearance of enormous thresher remains is troubling. The creature dwarfs typical local wildlife, pointing to depths far beyond the calm waters of the Veiled Sea. Although coastal murlocs eagerly swarm and feast on the corpse, they lack the strength or coordination to bring down a leviathan of this scale. The predator succumbed to something else entirely before washing ashore. Gwennyth Bly'Leggonde in Auberdine coordinates field efforts to salvage bones and biological samples from Darkshore's stranded megafauna. Night elf researchers in Darnassus hope that by examining skeletal remains and tissue samples, they can determine whether illness, deep-sea disturbances, or arcane corruption drives these ocean giants onto the killing sands.

quest:4728.text: Beached Sea Creature. Along the misty coast of Darkshore lies the massive carcass of a sea mammal, abandoned mid-excavation. Scattered tools and an idle wheelbarrow reveal an expedition cut short, leaving the specimen to opportunistic murlocs and the curious eyes of passing travelers. The carcass resting upon the sands of Darkshore is that of an enormous marine mammal, partially gutted and heavily weathered by sea spray. Strewn about its decaying frame are a rusted wheelbarrow and discarded excavation tools, clearly showing that someone attempted an organized study of the beast before being driven off or abandoning the site in haste. The abandoned equipment belonged to dwarven field researchers of the Explorer's League operating in Darkshore. Their examination of the massive carcass came to an abrupt halt when local murlocs swarmed the site, claiming the washed-up giant for scavenging. Gwennyth Bly'Leggonde in Auberdine, acting on behalf of the Temple of the Moon, gladly accepts any salvaged bone samples to further study the unnatural wash-ups plaguing the coastline.

quest:476.text: Gnarlpine Corruption. Gnarlpine Corruption is an urgent courier task in Teldrassil delivered on behalf of the wounded Great Warden Gaerolas Talvethren. It warns the night elf leadership in Dolanaar that the Gnarlpine furbolgs have succumbed to demonic corruption and overran Starbreeze Village. This report sets the stage for military and druidic interventions to prevent the taint from reaching the sleeping druids of Ban'ethil Barrow Den. Gaerolas Talvethren lies grievously wounded near the ruins of Starbreeze Village after being ambushed by his former allies. The Gnarlpine furbolgs, long considered peaceful neighbors and stewards of the wild, have abruptly turned feral. Too injured to carry the news back to civilization himself, Gaerolas entrusts an adventurer to carry word swiftly to Athridas Bearmantle in Dolanaar before the madness spreads any further across the boughs of Teldrassil.

quest:4761.text: Thundris Windweaver. Thundris Windweaver is an Alliance quest connecting the druid Terenthis's reconnaissance of the local furbolgs to the civic leadership of Auberdine. Having confirmed the growing aggression of the nearby Blackwood tribe, adventurers are directed to report directly to Elder Windweaver. The elder seeks to understand the root causes of the encroaching taint warping Darkshore's wilderness. Following your scouting mission into the corrupted furbolg camps of Darkshore, the druid Terenthis directs you to Auberdine's village elder, Thundris Windweaver. While Terenthis investigates the spreading corruption in the wilds, Thundris oversees the daily welfare of the settlement and weighs the broader spiritual and environmental perils facing the kaldorei. The report provides leadership with clear evidence that the furbolgs are not simply territorial, but actively deteriorating under an unnatural malice. Upon receiving word of the furbolg encampment, Thundris confirms that Auberdine has been wrestling with mounting hostility from native forest dwellers for some time. More distressing than the aggression alone is the creeping corruption infecting Darkshore's soil, flora, and waters. Believing that healing the land requires discovering the wellspring of this blight, Thundris turns his focus toward tracing the taint upstream, enlisting capable allies to investigate the region's waterways.

quest:4762.text: The Cliffspring River. The Cliffspring River is a major waterway in northern Darkshore that is rapidly turning foul and threatening the settlement of Auberdine. Thundris Windweaver tasks Alliance investigators with gathering a water sample from beneath a river bridge waterfall to confirm the creeping blight. Thundris suspects a deeper source of corruption beyond the riverbanks. Running down from the eastern highlands, the Cliffspring River empties into the coastal shoals along Mist's Edge, just north of Auberdine. Recently, its waters have begun to turn foul, carrying an unnatural rot toward the night elf settlement. Fearing that the wash will poison the surrounding shores and the town's supplies, Thundris Windweaver sends scouts upriver to draw samples from the waterfall pool beneath the road bridge.

quest:477.text: Border Crossings. Border Crossings is an espionage task assigned by Shadow Priest Allister in the Sepulcher to investigate Dalaran's covert operations in Silverpine Forest. By intercepting supply crates bound for the Dalaran encampment near Pyrewood Village, the Forsaken hope to uncover why the Kirin Tor are actively supporting the human bastion of Ambermill. While Ambermill stands as the main stronghold of surviving human resistance in eastern Silverpine Forest, the magi of Dalaran have not left them to stand alone. Wagon shipments filled with supplies and arcana have been smuggled out of the Hillsbrad Foothills, crossing through Silverpine to supply forward outposts and staging grounds. One such logistical camp sits just north of Pyrewood Village, manned by Dalaran personnel watching the road. Shadow Priest Allister and the Forsaken leadership at the Sepulcher find Dalaran's intense investment in Ambermill troubling. To them, a provincial town would hardly justify the Kirin Tor risking resources and lives deep within Forsaken-claimed territory unless some greater strategic or magical objective was at stake. Investigating the crates gives the Forsaken direct intelligence on what Dalaran is shipping west.

quest:478.text: Maps and Runes. Maps and Runes is a Forsaken reconnaissance mission in Silverpine Forest. After discovering a suspicious shipment shipped toward Ambermill, adventurers recover a rune-inscribed pendant to deliver to Shadow Priest Allister at the Sepulcher for further investigation. While intercepting logistics around Ambermill, Horde agents uncover a Dalaran crate concealed along the border routes. Rather than mundane supplies, the container holds detailed regional charts and an enigmatic, rune-inscribed pendant. Recognizing the potential danger of Dalaran's arcane reach so close to their borders, scouts carefully retrieve the artifact to avoid alarming the surrounding human sentries.

quest:481.text: Dalar's Analysis. Dalar's Analysis is a Horde quest in Silverpine Forest linking Shadow Priest Allister's espionage against Ambermill with the arcane research of Dalar Dawnweaver. After uncovering a rune-inscribed pendant from a Dalaran supply crate, adventurers bring the relic to Dalar at the Sepulcher for scrutiny. The artifact reveals that the surviving mages of Dalaran are marshaling significant magical power for a hidden initiative. Following a raid on a Dalaran supply crate at a camp north of Pyrewood Village, Shadow Priest Allister receives a rune-inscribed pendant found beneath a bundle of old maps. Recognizing that its enchantment lies beyond his spiritual purview, Allister directs the relic to Dalar Dawnweaver, an arcane scholar stationed at the Sepulcher who is better suited to decipher Dalaran's magical warding.

quest:4811.text: The Red Crystal. Sentinel Glynda Nal'Shea of Auberdine tasks travelers with investigating rumors of a mysterious red crystal embedded along Darkshore's eastern mountains. With hostile moonkin multiplying nearby and appearing drawn to the formation, the Sentinels need to confirm whether the anomaly truly exists. For generations, the night elves of Kalimdor viewed moonkin as gentle, mystical creatures closely tied to the wilderness. In recent days, however, aggressive packs have multiplied rapidly along the slopes east of Auberdine. While some traditionalists maintain reverence for the moonkin, Sentinel Glynda Nal'Shea prioritizes the town's safety and cannot ignore the rising danger. Reports suggest the beasts are flocking to a specific location along the eastern peaks. Scouts and wanderers brought whispers of an unnatural red crystal jutting from the rocky hillside high above Darkshore. Because wild rumors spread easily in the fog-bound coast, Glynda seeks boots on the ground to separate myth from fact. Finding the crimson monolith confirms that the anomaly is very real, leaving the Sentinels to puzzle out why the local moonkin are inexplicably drawn to it and whether its presence portends a sinister influence over the land.

quest:4812.text: As Water Cascades. As Water Cascades is an Alliance quest in Darkshore where players test the nature of the mysterious red crystal jutting from the eastern mountain wall. By pouring sacred moonwell water from Auberdine over its surface, players attempt to pierce its opaque exterior and uncover where it came from. After the red crystal is first sighted high on the eastern cliffs of Darkshore, Sentinel Glynda Nal'Shea devises a way to examine its composition safely. Moonwell waters carry potent divine and restorative magic, blessed by the night elves' devotion to Elune. Glynda reasons that dousing the alien monolith with water drawn from the moonwell in Auberdine will trigger a reaction, cutting through its strange, opaque shell without destroying it outright.

quest:482.text: Dalaran's Intentions. Dalaran's Intentions is a Silverpine Forest quest delivered by Dalar Dawnweaver to Shadow Priest Allister. Having studied a rune-inscribed pendant bound for the Kirin Tor in Ambermill, Dalar realizes the wizards intend to tap a dormant ley energy node beneath the town, prompting the Forsaken leadership at the Sepulcher to plan a counter-offensive. While examining a rune-inscribed pendant recovered from a Dalaran supply crate, Dalar Dawnweaver remembers an old Kirin Tor survey. Ambermill was not chosen by the mages by coincidence; the quiet village rests directly atop a dormant ley energy node. Awaking such a subterranean nexus requires immense magical reserves, and the enchanted pendants worn by the wizards serve as key components in channeling and catalyzing that power. The Forsaken cannot tolerate a fortified, power-fueled Kirin Tor outpost threatening the southern approaches to the Sepulcher and Tirisfal Glades. Whatever grand ritual the magi are preparing, harnessing raw ley lines would grant Dalaran an enormous strategic advantage in Lordaeron. Dalar sends word urgently to Shadow Priest Allister to formulate a strategy that will stall the wizards' progress before their ritual reaches completion.

quest:487.text: The Road to Darnassus. The main road connecting the settlement of Dolanaar to the night elf capital of Darnassus is under constant threat from corrupted Gnarlpine furbolgs. Moon Priestess Amara coordinates scouts and travelers to keep this crucial trade and messenger route clear of ambushes. The road spanning west from Dolanaar toward Darnassus is the primary overland artery in Teldrassil. Vital trade goods, political missives, and travelers must move along it daily to maintain connection between the capital city and the boughs of the great tree. Because Teldrassil is relatively young and wild, maintaining secure roads is critical for the fledgling kaldorei communities. Rather than peaceful forest dwellers, the Gnarlpine furbolg tribe in Teldrassil has fallen victim to a foul corruption. Driven mad by whatever sickness plagues the boughs of the World Tree, they strike outward from hidden dens beneath the ridges. Stalking the tree line alongside the road, Gnarlpine ambushers prey on unwary couriers and travelers, turning what should be a peaceful forest trek into a deadly gauntlet. To counter the ambushers, Moon Priestess Amara keeps watch outside Dolanaar. Blending the spiritual authority of Elune's priesthood with the militant vigilance of the Sentinels, she directs capable adventurers to strike down the ambushers near their dens below the road, ensuring safe transit to the gates of Darnassus.

quest:492.text: A New Plague. This quest marks the grim culmination of Apothecary Johaan's initial research in Brill on behalf of the Royal Apothecary Society. Having harvested venom, blood, and vile concoctions across Tirisfal Glades, Johaan sends you to the cellar of Gallows' End Tavern to test his lethal brew on a captive dwarven mountaineer. Throughout your time aiding Apothecary Johaan, your efforts have steadily built toward refining a lethal toxin. The Royal Apothecary Society pursues an ambitious and shadowy agenda on behalf of Lady Sylvanas Windrunner: crafting a new plague that bypasses undead biology while annihilating the living. In this final step, Johaan brews what he euphemistically calls a 'special drink' and tasks you with administering it directly to an imprisoned enemy of the Forsaken. Beneath Gallows' End Tavern in Brill, the Deathguard maintains a damp cellar used as a makeshift holding cell for captives awaiting interrogation or disposal. Among them sits a captured Dwarven Mountaineer, an operative of the Ironforge reconnaissance units trespassing in Tirisfal Glades. Defiant and thirsty, he eagerly accepts a drink, completely unaware of its true alchemical payload.

quest:5041.text: Supplies for the Crossroads. Supplies for the Crossroads is a Horde task issued by Thork to recover essential provisions taken during Razormane quilboar raids. By reclaiming these lost supply crates from thorny encampments, adventurers help sustain the Crossroads amidst constant regional conflict. The Crossroads serves as the central junction for Horde travel, trade, and defense throughout the Barrens. Keeping such a hub operational requires a steady stream of cargo flowing from Durotar and Mulgore. When a supply caravan is ambushed, the outpost faces immediate shortages of provisions, tools, and arms vital for enduring the harsh wilderness. The culprits behind the raid are the Razormane quilboar, native swine-beasts who contest Horde dominance across central Kalimdor. Rather than destroying the stolen goods, the quilboar dragged the heavy crates back to their fortified thorn-bush camps to hoard for themselves. Thork charges trusted warriors with penetrating deep into Razormane grounds to reclaim what rightfully belongs to the Horde.

quest:5261.text: Eagan Peltskinner. This brief introductory task directs newly arrived recruits in Northshire Valley to speak with Eagan Peltskinner, a local furrier stationed outside Northshire Abbey. With predator numbers swelling along the valley's fringes, Eagan requires capable adventurers to hunt timber wolves and gather pelts. Northshire Valley may appear pastoral, but its quiet orchards and fields are bordered by wild woods crawling with timber wolves. Deputy Willem often directs recruits outside the abbey's walls to Eagan Peltskinner, who works nearby on the abbey grounds. Eagan is eager to put newcomers to work thinning the aggressive packs while securing valuable pelts for his craft. The rising wolf population around Northshire is more than an annoyance; it threatens workers, acolytes, and supply lines moving in and out of the valley. Directing young champions to Eagan serves a dual purpose for Stormwind's marshals: it keeps the nearby paths safe without tying up the garrison's few remaining guards, who already face rising tensions across Elwynn Forest.

quest:5481.text: Gordo's Task. Gordo's Task is an errand in Tirisfal Glades given by Gordo, a wandering abomination trying to gather flora along the road to Brill. Unsuited for delicate fieldwork, he recruits travelers to pick Gloom Weed and deliver it to his handler, Junior Apothecary Holland. Gordo is an abomination who trudges back and forth along the countryside between Deathknell and Brill. While abominations excel at brute combat and heavy hauling, their massive, sutured hands make fine manipulation almost impossible. Sent into the meadows to gather ingredients for the Royal Apothecary Society, Gordo quickly realizes his blunt fingers crush more stems than they pluck, prompting him to bully or bribe passersby into doing the tedious work for him.

quest:5482.text: Doom Weed. Doom Weed is a task given by Junior Apothecary Holland in Brill to gather noxious flora sprouting near Tirisfal's northern mass graves. Holland recruits passing adventurers after becoming frustrated with the clumsy harvesting efforts of the abomination Gordo. Junior Apothecary Holland conducts research on behalf of the Royal Apothecary Society from the settlement of Brill. Seeking to advance his experiments, he requires quantities of doom weed, a vile plant that infests the blighted soil of Tirisfal Glades. Finding Gordo incapable of discerning the proper reagents, Holland turns to sharper hands to salvage his harvest. Doom weed thrives in places heavily corrupted by death and plague, proliferating densely around the mass gravesite situated just north of the Brill graveyard. Gathering the flora is made perilous by aggressive Rot Hide gnolls that prowl the desecrated burial mounds, scavenging among the remains and defending the overgrown trenches.

quest:5541.text: Ammo for Rumbleshot. Gunsmith Hegnar Rumbleshot is running low on shot and powder for the riflemen practicing outside Anvilmar. A missing crate of ammunition was abandoned in the snowy wilds near the Grizzled Den when a courier was routed by hungry wendigo. Loslor Rudge at Steelgrill's Depot keeps steady supply lines flowing to tradesmen across Dun Morogh, but the valley's wildlife often interferes. His latest shipment of heavy ammunition never reached Hegnar Rumbleshot's roadside workshop. While camping near the cave system known as the Grizzled Den, the terrified courier crossed paths with local wendigo and fled for his life, abandoning the heavy wooden crate in the snow. Hegnar Rumbleshot operates a gun shop situated right along the main road leading away from Anvilmar. The clearing outside his forge sees constant traffic from Ironforge riflemen, mountaineers, and dwarven mortar squads looking to zero their sights and drill with live fire. Without steady crates of powder and lead from suppliers like Loslor, the riflemen's marksmanship training quickly grinds to a dead stop.

quest:5621.text: Garments of the Moon. Garments of the Moon is an introductory rite of service for young night elf priests in Dolanaar. Assigned by priest trainer Laurna Morninglight, it tasks an initiate with tending to Sentinel Shaya, a wounded defender patrolling the woods south of the settlement. Fulfilling this duty marks an initiate's formal recognition within the Sisterhood of Elune. Within the boughs of Teldrassil, the Sisterhood of Elune tends both to the spiritual life of the kaldorei and the practical defense of their borders. When Sentinel Shaya is wounded while patrolling the dangerous wilderness south of Dolanaar, priest trainer Laurna Morninglight cannot abandon her post to render aid. Instead, she charges a newly trained initiate with proving their devotion by mending Shaya's wounds and bolstering her constitution with protective magic. Priests who restore Sentinel Shaya's vigor return to Dolanaar to receive their formal robes of office. These garments signify that the young acolyte has moved beyond mere classroom instruction to practical, lifesaving service under the moon's grace. In kaldorei society, supporting the Sentinels is not merely a military task; it is an act of communion with Elune and an essential duty to the safety of Teldrassil.

quest:5622.text: In Favor of Elune. "In Favor of Elune" is a rite of passage for young night elf priests ready to step out of the sheltered boughs of Shadowglen. Directed by Priestess Shanda, novitiates travel down the path to Dolanaar to seek further guidance and training under Laurna Morninglight. For an initiate serving Elune within Aldrassil's secluded shelter, learning begins with simple prayers and defensive invocations under the watchful eye of Priestess Shanda. Yet the cloistered life of Shadowglen cannot prepare a priestess or priest for the turmoil gripping the wider world. Once an initiate demonstrates steady faith and discipline, Shanda sends them down the shadowed forest path toward Dolanaar to continue their education. Reaching Dolanaar marks an essential milestone in a night elf's divine vocation. There awaits Laurna Morninglight, a respected priestess tasked with preparing disciples for the trials facing Teldrassil. Beyond advanced instruction in moonlit spellcraft, arriving in Dolanaar prepares the acolyte to claim their first formal vestments, marking their official standing within the Sisterhood of Elune.

quest:5623.text: In Favor of the Light. In Favor of the Light marks an early milestone for novice priests training within Northshire Valley. Given by Priestess Anetta, it directs the fledgling minister beyond the cloistered abbey to Goldshire. There, Priestess Josetta awaits to deepen their spiritual discipline and guide them further into the faith of the Holy Light. Northshire Abbey provides shelter and initial instruction for novices, but clerical training in the Church of the Holy Light demands practical ministry out in the world. Once an initiate demonstrates basic mastery of prayer and divine healing, Priestess Anetta sends them south along the sunlit roads to Goldshire. The journey signifies a transition from secluded student to active parish servant amidst the everyday trials of the Elwynn populace. At the Lion's Pride Inn in Goldshire, Priestess Josetta tends to local spiritual needs and oversees rising acolytes. Josetta builds directly upon the fundamentals laid down at the abbey, testing the initiate's ability to offer solace, ward the faithful, and mend the injured. Stepping under her guidance introduces the young priest to the duties required of the Church's servants across the broader kingdom.

quest:5624.text: Garments of the Light. Garments of the Light is an early trial for novice priests in Goldshire, assigned by Priestess Josetta. Rather than an abstract test of faith, the church sends the acolyte east to Crystal Lake to mend and bolster the wounded Guard Roberts. Fulfilling this duty proves the student's mastery of healing and earns them their first official vestments recognized by the Church of the Holy Light. Within the traditions of the Church of the Holy Light, novice disciples are rarely elevated purely on doctrine. Priestess Josetta, who instructs acolytes arriving in Goldshire from Northshire Abbey, tests an initiate's practical mastery over divine power before granting formal church recognition. When reports reach town that Guard Roberts lies wounded by the lake east of Goldshire, Josetta turns an everyday misfortune into a proving ground, dispatching the young priest to tend to him. The assignment requires more than simply closing flesh; the acolyte must mend the guard's wounds with restorative prayers and bolster his resilience with a blessing of fortitude. In these troubled times, with Stormwind's military stretched thin and local garrisons beleaguered by kobolds and bandits, Josetta stresses that the priesthood's duty extends directly into martial survival. Returning Guard Roberts to active duty serves the township immediately while demonstrating that the initiate can sustain defenders under fire. Upon returning to the Lion's Pride Inn after treating the soldier, the young priest receives their first formal set of robes. These garments signify outward approval and fellowship from the priesthood in Stormwind. Though wearing them is not strictly mandatory for future training, the robes stand as a visible declaration that the church recognizes the wearer as an ordained servant of the Holy Light.

quest:5625.text: Garments of the Light. Garments of the Light is an early rite of passage for fledgling dwarven priests in Dun Morogh. Directed by Priest Trainer Maxan Anvol in Kharanos, the initiate is tasked with aiding a wounded mountaineer just outside town to earn their vestments. Traditionally, acolytes of the Holy Light undergo formal trials to prove they are worthy of wearing church vestments. In Kharanos, however, priest trainer Maxan Anvol favors practical results over ceremony. With local patrols hard-pressed against troggs and wild beasts, theoretical exams take a back seat when actual defenders lie bleeding in the snow. To earn their robes, young priests are sent just south of town to locate Mountaineer Dolf, who was wounded in the line of duty. By mending Dolf's injuries with restorative prayers and bolstering his constitution with Power Word: Fortitude, the initiate proves that their devotion translates directly into survival for the defenders of Ironforge. Upon aiding the mountaineer, Maxan Anvol presents the acolyte with their formal garments. Beyond providing warm insulation against Dun Morogh's chill, these robes serve as a visual badge of office, signaling to wounded wanderers and local guards alike that a servant of the Light is present to offer aid.

quest:5626.text: In Favor of the Light. "In Favor of the Light" marks a young priest's rite of passage from the isolated training grounds of Coldridge Valley into the wider reaches of Dun Morogh. Instructed by Branstock Khalder, novitiates are sent through the mountain tunnel to Kharanos to further their studies under Priest Trainer Maxan Anvol. It signals that an acolyte is ready to shoulder real responsibilities and earn the traditional vestments of their calling. In the secluded cradle of Coldridge Valley, dwarven priests begin their studies under the watchful eye of instructors like Branstock Khalder. Once a novice demonstrates sufficient dedication and grasp of Holy magic, their preliminary instruction comes to an end. Rather than keeping them sheltered in Anvilmar, Khalder directs promising students beyond the mountains to Kharanos, where the demands of ministry and defense intersect with the daily struggles of Dun Morogh's folk. Reaching Kharanos requires trekking through the Coldridge Pass tunnel into the windswept snows of central Dun Morogh. Waiting at the settlement is Maxan Anvol, a senior priest tasked with guiding students beyond rudimentary prayers. Anvol believes firmly that devotion to the Holy Light requires equal measures of moral character, physical hardiness, and an unyielding will. For acolytes who prove their resolve under his tutelage, Anvol prepares to bestow their first formal garments of office.

quest:5627.text: Stars of Elune. Stars of Elune marks a major milestone in a young night elf priest's communion with the Moon Goddess. Upon proving their dedication to their people, acolytes are invited to the Temple of the Moon in Darnassus to learn sacred arts unique to the Sisterhood of Elune. Night elf priests do not draw their holy power from the broad philosophical tenets of the Light, as humans and dwarves do, but directly from their goddess, Elune. When an acolyte shows steadfast dedication while serving the realm, the Sisterhood in Darnassus recognizes that devotion. Summoned to the Temple of the Moon, the priest is deemed worthy of deeper communion and offered insight into sacred spells passed down through thousands of years of worship. Upon answering the call of Priestess Alathea, an initiate receives direct instruction in holy mysteries unique to their heritage, such as Starshards. These spells channel the radiant, celestial wrath and grace of the White Lady. Receiving this instruction signifies that an acolyte has graduated beyond basic training and is prepared to venture beyond the protective canopy of Teldrassil in Elune's name.

quest:5628.text: Returning Home. "Returning Home" is a summons sent to young night elf priests who have wandered as far as the human lands of Elwynn Forest. Priestess Josetta in Goldshire relays an urgent message from Darnassus, bidding the novice return to the Temple of the Moon to further their spiritual training under Priestess Alathea. Night elves are an unusual sight in Elwynn Forest, and a fledgling acolyte wandering among human settlements catches immediate attention. When such a priest arrives in Goldshire, Priestess Josetta greets them with both warmth and news. A Sister of Elune has traveled across continents seeking the young devotee, bearing an urgent command from the Temple of the Moon: it is time to return to Kalimdor and advance their calling. At the heart of Darnassus stands the Temple of the Moon, the epicenter of night elven faith and leadership. Priestess Alathea and High Priestess Tyrande Whisperwind oversee the instruction of the Sisterhood, keeping close watch over their disciples even when curiosity carries them overseas. Upon returning, initiates are welcomed back with motherly concern and immediately set onto deeper studies regarding the celestial mysteries of the Moon Goddess.

quest:5629.text: Returning Home. Returning Home marks a rite of passage for young night elf priests serving across Teldrassil. After proving themselves in the wilds, novitiates are summoned to the majestic Temple of the Moon in Darnassus to present themselves before Priestess Alathea and High Priestess Tyrande Whisperwind. Priests who spend their early days tending to the wounded and cleansing corruptions around Dolanaar quickly attract the attention of the Sisterhood of Elune. Trainer Laurna Morninglight intercepts promising initiates, explaining that Priestess Alathea has sent word asking for an audience. While aiding the local settlements is essential, every devotee must cultivate their communion with the Moon Mother and answer the higher calling of the faith. The path leads beyond the boughs of Teldrassil into the grand heart of Darnassus: the Temple of the Moon. Rising above the city under the gentle glow of Elune's grace, the sanctuary acts as both the supreme house of worship and the spiritual capital of the kaldorei. To be invited back into these halls means one is no longer treated merely as a fledging student, but as an initiate recognized directly by the leadership of the priesthood. When travelers step before Priestess Alathea, the greeting is warm and maternal. Alathea shares the leadership's watchful pride, noting that both she and High Priestess Tyrande Whisperwind rejoice whenever initiates venture into the uncertain outside world and return unharmed. This homecoming signals the start of deeper sacred trials under Alathea's direct mentorship.

quest:5630.text: Returning Home. Returning Home is a summons for wandering night elf priests operating far from Kalimdor in the snowy crags of Dun Morogh. Directed by the dwarven priest trainer Maxan Anvol, the novice is instructed to return to the Temple of the Moon in Darnassus to report to Priestess Alathea. Night elves who choose to begin their adventures alongside their dwarven allies face the bitter biting cold of Dun Morogh, a far cry from the serene forests of Teldrassil. In Kharanos, the dwarven priest trainer Maxan Anvol takes note of the elf's fortitude before passing along an urgent message: a priestess of Elune passed through seeking them out, carrying orders from Darnassus that require their immediate return. The journey demands a trek back to the sacred boughs of Teldrassil, leading directly to the Temple of the Moon. There, Priestess Alathea welcomes the traveler back into the fold of the Sisterhood of Elune. Relieved to see another devotee return unscathed from foreign lands, Alathea swiftly prepares the priest for their next rites of devotion, beginning with the Stars of Elune.

quest:5631.text: Returning Home. Returning Home is an Alliance priest quest that summons promising night elf acolytes who have been traveling abroad back to Teldrassil. Guided by Brother Joshua in human lands, the young priest is recalled to the Temple of the Moon in Darnassus by Priestess Alathea for advanced guidance in the mysteries of Elune. While night elf priests occasionally travel to human domains like Stormwind to share spiritual fellowship with the Church of the Holy Light, their deepest ties remain bound to the Sisterhood of Elune. When Brother Joshua informs an acolyte that a night elf emissary has come searching for them, it signals that their early wanderings are done. Their home temple requires their presence for deeper training under the guidance of High Priestess Tyrande Whisperwind's inner circle. Returning across the seas to Darnassus brings the traveler directly to the sanctum of the Temple of the Moon. Priestess Alathea greets the returning acolyte with warmth, celebrating their safe passage through a troubled world. The safe return of their young disciples is a source of joy for both Alathea and Tyrande, but it is also the prologue to more demanding spiritual trials.

quest:5632.text: Returning Home. Returning Home is a summons sent to promising night elf priests serving outside the capital. Priestess Alathea calls initiates back to the Temple of the Moon in Darnassus to recognize their growth in the Sisterhood of Elune and bestow advanced guidance. As nascent priests journey abroad in the service of their people, their spiritual growth does not go unnoticed. While visiting Nara Meideros in Stormwind's Park, a messenger from the Sisterhood of Elune arrives bearing urgent word: the order's leaders require the initiate's presence in Darnassus. It serves as both an evaluation and a rite of recognition, marking the transition from a fledgling novitiate into an active servant of the Mother Moon. The summons directs the traveler straight to Priestess Alathea within Darnassus's crowning sanctuary, the Temple of the Moon. Overseen by High Priestess Tyrande Whisperwind, the Sisterhood keeps close watch over its dispersed members. Returning safely to the temple grounds honors the community and the goddess, demonstrating that Elune's grace has guided and preserved the priest through early trials in the wild.

quest:5633.text: Returning Home. Returning Home is a summons for night elf priests traveling abroad in Ironforge to return to the Temple of the Moon in Darnassus. An emissary of the Sisterhood sought out wandering acolytes, directing them back to Priestess Alathea for urgent training and spiritual duties.
