Even while wandering far from Teldrassil in the bustling subterranean halls of Ironforge, night elf priests remain bound to the Sisterhood of Elune. Braenna Flintcrag, a dwarven priest trainer in the Mystic Ward, passes along a message left by a visiting night elf priestess. The messenger came seeking young disciples abroad, carrying word that their mentors require their presence immediately back in the capital. Upon arriving at the Temple of the Moon in Darnassus, returning acolytes report directly to Priestess Alathea. Welcoming her student back under the watchful gaze of High Priestess Tyrande Whisperwind, Alathea expresses relief at their safe journey across the seas. The urgent summons serves as the threshold to deeper devotion, opening the way for sacred duties such as the Stars of Elune.

quest:5634.text: Desperate Prayer. Desperate Prayer is a rite of passage for fledgling human priests in Stormwind City. Bestowed by High Priestess Laurena in the Cathedral of Light, it marks an acolyte's dedication to preserving life across the turbulent lands of the Alliance. By completing this spiritual instruction, priests are granted an emergency blessing to heal their own wounds when all else fails. Priests serving within the Cathedral of Light are taught to channel their faith outward to shield comrades, mend mortal wounds, and smite evil. Yet even the most devout servants of the Holy Light find themselves isolated, cornered, or pushed to the edge of mortal endurance. Desperate Prayer represents an intimate, emergency communion—a raw cry for divine intervention when an acolyte's personal survival hangs by a thread. High Priestess Laurena oversees many of the clergy within Stormwind's Cathedral Square, assessing when an acolyte has proven worthy of deeper doctrinal secrets. By demonstrating true dedication to the virtues of the Light across the kingdom, human initiates receive this sacred lesson not merely as an instrument of survival, but as a solemn affirmation that their continued service remains essential to the realm.

quest:5635.text: Desperate Prayer. Desperate Prayer is an introductory quest for fledgling Alliance priests serving the Church of the Holy Light. After demonstrating initial devotion and discipline in Elwynn Forest, promising acolytes are summoned to the Cathedral of Light in Stormwind to further their sacred training under High Priestess Laurena. Novice priests serving in the outlying settlements of Elwynn Forest begin their journey under local mentors like Priestess Josetta in Goldshire. When a disciple proves capable in spirit and deeds, word quickly reaches the senior priesthood in the capital. Recognition comes in the form of a direct summons to the grand Cathedral of Light, the spiritual heart of the Kingdom of Stormwind, signaling that the time has come to undertake formal, deeper responsibilities in the faith. Upon arriving at the Cathedral, acolytes present themselves to High Priestess Laurena. As one of the preeminent leaders of the Church within the city, Laurena oversees the spiritual foundation and practical training of newly elevated priests. Her instruction prepares devotees for the harsh trials facing the Alliance, imparting critical knowledge of the Light's miracles—including the vital plea for salvation known among human practitioners as Desperate Prayer.

quest:5636.text: Desperate Prayer. Desperate Prayer is an Alliance priest quest directing traveling servants of the Holy Light back to Stormwind City. Initiated by the night elf priestess Laurna Morninglight in Dolanaar, it calls human priests visiting Teldrassil home to complete vital spiritual training under High Priestess Laurena. While visiting the ancestral boughs of Teldrassil, priests faithful to the Holy Light may find themselves noticed by the local Sisterhood of Elune. In Dolanaar, Priestess Laurna Morninglight serves as an unexpected liaison, delivering word that a fellow priest traveled across continents seeking you out. Recognizing the urgency of the summons, Laurna encourages you to return to your homeland without delay, offering Elune's blessing alongside well-wishes for your own faith. The journey requires crossing the Great Sea to the grand Cathedral of Light situated in the heart of Stormwind City. There, High Priestess Laurena oversees the spiritual growth of the Alliance's faithful. Acolytes who have demonstrated early promise are summoned before her to master deeper mysteries of devotion, specifically the emergency invocation known as Desperate Prayer—a life-saving gift granted only to dedicated disciples in their darkest hour.

quest:5637.text: Desperate Prayer. Desperate Prayer is a rite of passage quest calling promising dwarven priests from Dun Morogh to the grand Cathedral of Light in Stormwind. High Priestess Laurena summons rising acolytes to advance their spiritual devotion and unlock specialized holy techniques. It marks a priest's transition from local training into the wider service of the Alliance. Priests who begin their service among the snows of Dun Morogh eventually outgrow the instruction of local mentors like Maxan Anvol in Kharanos. When an acolyte shows true promise, a formal summons arrives from High Priestess Laurena herself. Such direct attention from the leadership of the Cathedral of Light signifies that the young priest is ready for deeper mysteries and greater responsibilities within the faith. While Ironforge maintains its own holy traditions in the Mystic Ward, the Church of the Holy Light in Stormwind serves as a central spiritual heart for humans and dwarves alike. Journeying south via the Deeprun Tram connects dwarven acolytes to the broader ecclesiastical community, solidifying the shared spiritual brotherhood between the two allied kingdoms.

quest:5638.text: Desperate Prayer. Desperate Prayer is a rite-of-passage summons for developing priests visiting the Park in Stormwind City. Directed by the night elf priestess Nara Meideros, novice clerics are sent across the canals to the Cathedral of Light to continue their holy instruction under High Priestess Laurena. It marks the moment an initiate transitions from basic field duty to deeper, specialized communion with the Holy Light. Within the serene grove of the Park, night elf priestesses like Nara Meideros maintain communion with Elune amid the bustle of Stormwind. Yet the bonds of faith among the Alliance's spiritual guides cross cultural divides. When an envoy from the Cathedral Square seeks out a promising student, Nara passes along the summons with quiet encouragement, assuring the initiate that the call carries good tidings rather than cause for alarm. Upon crossing Cathedral Square and stepping beneath the soaring white stone arches of the Cathedral of Light, the initiate reports to High Priestess Laurena. As one of Stormwind's most senior clerical leaders, Laurena guides young acolytes beyond mere foundational prayers. She imparts the sacred invocation known as Desperate Prayer—a personal plea for divine intervention that can instantly mend grievous wounds when a servant of the Light stands on the precipice of death.

quest:5639.text: Desperate Prayer. Desperate Prayer is a rite of passage for dwarven priests coming of age in Ironforge. Dispatched by High Priest Rohan, acolytes journey through the Deeprun Tram to Stormwind to continue their training under High Priestess Laurena. Reaching the grand Cathedral of Light marks an initiate's transition into deeper mysteries of healing and survival. Within the stone vaults of Ironforge's Mystic Ward, High Priest Rohan oversees dwarven initiates dedicated to the Holy Light. When an acolyte demonstrates sufficient discipline and faith, Rohan directs them southwest to the human kingdom of Stormwind. Human and dwarven clerics maintain close spiritual bonds, and advanced theological instruction is centralized in the grand halls of Stormwind City. Upon arriving via the subterranean Deeprun Tram, acolytes ascend to the Cathedral Square. There, within the majestic Cathedral of Light, High Priestess Laurena tests candidates on behalf of the Church. Her instruction focuses on the desperate appeals a priest must make in the crucible of battle—pleas for divine intervention when physical endurance fails and death looms near.

quest:5640.text: Desperate Prayer. Desperate Prayer is a quest given to young human and dwarven priests visiting Darnassus, directing them back to their own spiritual traditions in Stormwind. Priestess Alathea recognizes that while night elves draw strength from Elune, followers of the Holy Light must seek out mentors of their own faith. Completing this journey returns the acolyte to High Priestess Laurena in the Cathedral of Light. Priests walking the paths of the Alliance draw upon fundamentally different sacred sources. Within Darnassus, the Priesthood of Elune tends to the moon goddess, channeling her gentle radiance and celestial wrath. When human and dwarven acolytes travel beneath Teldrassil's boughs, mentors like Priestess Alathea politely recognize the divide: while she honors Elune and respects the Holy Light, she cannot instruct another race in the deeper prayers tied to an entirely different devotion. To master abilities born of absolute faith—such as calling forth emergency divine intervention in one's darkest hour—initiates of the Holy Light are told to journey back home. High Priestess Laurena presides over training within the soaring marble arches of Stormwind's Cathedral of Light, ready to guide returning priests into the deeper rites of their calling.

quest:5648.text: Garments of Spirituality. Garments of Spirituality is a rite of passage for fledgling Horde priests in Durotar, assigned by Tai'jin in Razor Hill. Initiates are sent into the field to locate and mend the wounds of an injured grunt standing vigil against Kul Tiras survivors. Completing the task earns a priest their first ceremonial vestments and formal recognition among the Horde's spiritual practitioners. In the arid scrub south of Razor Hill, the Horde faces relentless skirmishes against remnants of Grand Admiral Daelin Proudmoore's forces. Rather than sending prospective priests into abstract rituals, the troll trainer Tai'jin tests their discipline in real combat triage. Initiates are charged with seeking out Grunt Kor'ja, a warrior critically injured while repelling human infiltrators, to tend her injuries and bolster her constitution before she succumbs. Restoring Kor'ja to fighting condition proves the young priest's readiness to bear the mantle of Horde spiritual tradition. In recognition of saving a frontline defender, Tai'jin bestows the Garments of Spirituality. For both orcish allies and Darkspear trolls, these robes signify that the wearer is not merely an apprentice studying incantations, but a reliable lifeline capable of keeping the Horde's warriors alive in battle.

quest:5649.text: In Favor of Spirituality. "In Favor of Spirituality" is a foundational rite of passage for young Darkspear priests departing the Valley of Trials. Directed by Ken'jai to report to the priest trainer Tai'jin in Razor Hill, initiates take their first real steps beyond the secluded training den into the wider challenges of Durotar. The journey highlights the delicate balance the Darkspear strike between honoring their ancestral troll heritage and integrating into the newly forged Horde. After mastering their basic rites under Ken'jai in the secluded Valley of Trials, Darkspear acolytes are ready to leave the training grounds behind. The winding paths out into Durotar lead directly to the crossroads settlement of Razor Hill. For a young priest, this journey represents a major milestone: transitioning from basic survival drills in the dirt to shouldering spiritual and cultural responsibilities for the tribe. Ken'jai is candid about the Darkspear's position within Thrall's Horde. While the trolls deeply value the orcs' loyalty and lessons of honor, not every ancestral tradition fits smoothly under the eyes of their allies. Darkspear spiritual leaders instruct their pupils to quietly preserve their heritage, holding fast to their identity while continuing to serve the Horde. Tai'jin at Razor Hill welcomes these acolytes into that deeper understanding, guiding them toward self-sufficiency and communal strength.

quest:5650.text: Garments of Darkness. Garments of Darkness is a foundational rite of passage for fledgling Forsaken priests in Brill. Dark Cleric Beryl tasks initiates with healing and fortifying an injured Deathguard, testing their grasp of supportive magics before they delve deeper into the shadows. While the Forsaken priesthood draws renown and distinct identity from shadow and darkness, its elders recognize the enduring pragmatic necessity of restoration. Dark Cleric Beryl teaches that understanding the dark demands an understanding of the light and restorative arts. A priest who seeks only ruin is cautioned to study arcane magic instead; the priesthood's true calling involves strengthening and preserving comrades just as much as afflicting enemies. To demonstrate mastery, the initiate is sent north of Brill's cemetery to aid Deathguard Kel. Stationed against prowling gnoll packs, Kel has sustained injuries holding the line. By binding his wounds with healing spells and bolstering his stamina with protective enchantments, the acolyte proves capable of maintaining the defenders of Tirisfal Glades, earning Beryl's vestment and acceptance into the priesthood's higher mysteries.

quest:5651.text: In Favor of Darkness. In Favor of Darkness marks a Forsaken priest's transition beyond the starting crypts of Deathknell toward advanced instruction in Brill. Entrusted by Dark Cleric Duesten, the fledgling disciple travels to study under Dark Cleric Beryl to master the delicate balance between the Holy Light and the Shadow. While priests of other races revere the Holy Light as an unblemished source of moral virtue, the Forsaken approach faith through the harsh lens of their own undeath. As Dark Cleric Duesten teaches, the Forsaken were forged in corruption and discarded like carrion. Their survival demands understanding both Light and Shadow without sentimentality. In Favor of Darkness directs new disciples out of Deathknell's cloistered graveyard to confront the wider reality awaiting them in Tirisfal Glades. The road leading northeast out of Deathknell brings the fledgling priest over a wooden covered bridge and into the ruined hamlet of Brill. There, in the upper quarters of the local inn, Dark Cleric Beryl waits to test the initiate's resolve. Beryl values ambition and cold practicality over blind devotion, demanding that a Forsaken priest wield divine power as a weapon and a tool rather than a moral crutch.

quest:5654.text: Hex of Weakness. Hex of Weakness is an early rite of passage quest given to young Darkspear troll priests who have proven their initial worth in Razor Hill. Sent north into Orgrimmar by Tai'jin, the initiate seeks out Ur'kyo to be welcomed deeper into the tribe's spiritual circle and instructed in the loa's darker arts. For a fledgling troll priest in Durotar, lessons continue in the barracks of Razor Hill under the watchful eye of Tai'jin. Once an acolyte displays sufficient mastery over the basic balance of spiritual communion and shadow magic, basic tutelage ends. Tai'jin directs the promising priest away from Razor Hill and northward across the red dirt canyons toward the Horde capital, where elder practitioners oversee the tribe's broader magical traditions. Within Orgrimmar, the Darkspear maintain their own distinct cultural sanctuary in the Valley of Spirits, separated from the clanging forge-works and warrior grounds of the orcs. Here, amidst towering totems and shaded huts, the elder priest Ur'kyo awaits new initiates. To be brought into his circle means embracing the ancestral traditions of the jungle trolls—balancing reverence for ancestral loa with the potent curses and hexes that sap an adversary's strength in battle.

quest:5726.text: Hidden Enemies. Hidden Enemies is the opening chapter of Warchief Thrall's investigation into cultist infiltration within Durotar. Aware that demonic sympathizers are operating right under the Horde's nose, Thrall tasks a promising young adventurer with recovering a Lieutenant's Insignia from Skull Rock to initiate a covert operation. While the nascent Horde struggles to carve out a secure home in Durotar, Warchief Thrall faces an insidious threat far deadlier than centaur raids or quilboar incursions: internal betrayal. The demonic cult known as the Burning Blade has rooted itself right outside the gates of Orgrimmar, preying on lingering demonic corruption and thirst for dark power. Thrall recognizes that sending his official Kor'kron guards or known commanders would merely scatter the cultists into deeper hiding. He needs someone untainted by high-profile associations to serve as his discreet eyes and ears. East of Orgrimmar lies Skull Rock, a rugged cavern infested with warlocks, voidwalkers, and fanatical cultists. Thrall sends the adventurer straight into this nest with a specific mission: claim a Lieutenant's Insignia from one of the Burning Blade leaders. This emblem is far more than a battlefield trophy; it is a vital credential meant to grant the bearer access to the cult's shadowy hierarchy, enabling a deeper sting operation designed to reveal who directs the cult's movements from behind the scenes.

quest:5727.text: Hidden Enemies. Following the discovery of cult activity in Skull Rock, Warchief Thrall directs you to infiltrate the Burning Blade within Orgrimmar itself. By presenting a cult lieutenant's insignia to the warlock Neeru Fireblade, you test his loyalties and pierce the veil of the Shadow Council operating right under the city's surface. Rather than strike directly at the sinister elements harboring in the Cleft of Shadow, Thrall chooses cunning over haste. He is well aware that Neeru Fireblade feigns loyalty while quietly serving the cultists. Striking Neeru immediately would merely alert his masters and sever any trail leading deeper into the conspiracy. Instead, Thrall provides the insignia taken from the cult in Durotar, bidding you to masquerade as an initiate to discover what Neeru knows.

quest:579.text: Stormwind Library. Deep within the Royal Library of Stormwind Keep, librarian Donyal Tovald manages a collection of historical texts and regional accounts. By order of the young King Anduin Wrynn, funds have been allocated to transcribe copies of these works for citizens and scholars who bring official library scrips. This service allows adventurers to study the history, factions, and legends of Azeroth firsthand. While Highlord Bolvar Fordragon and Lady Katrana Prestor oversee defense and court politics in King Varian's absence, young King Anduin has directed royal resources toward education. Recognizing that understanding history is crucial for the kingdom's future, Anduin sponsored the transcribing of ancient manuscripts and historical journals. The Royal Library, nestled in the halls of Stormwind Keep, serves not merely as a royal vault for state secrets, but as a repository where documented lore is preserved and copied for those in royal service. Transcribing delicate parchment by hand requires significant time, ink, and royal sanction. To manage this distribution, the librarian Donyal Tovald accepts official library scrips, issued to adventurers and scholars across Alliance territories. In exchange, Tovald provides faithful duplicates of historical tomes, covering everything from the ancient histories of the Eastern Kingdoms to accounts of distant lands, offering context for ongoing conflicts beyond the capital's walls.

quest:5921.text: Moonglade. Moonglade is an introductory rite of passage for young night elf druids learning to commune with the sacred lands of Kalimdor. Guided by Mathrengyl Bearwalker in Darnassus, novices learn the spell to magically transport themselves across the world into Moonglade to meet Dendrite Starblaze in Nighthaven. This marks the beginning of their spiritual journey toward mastering the strength of the bear form. Moonglade stands apart from the rest of Azeroth as an ancient sanctuary dedicated to the teachings of Cenarius. Under the watchful stewardship of Keeper Remulos, its tranquil groves provide peace and deep communion with nature. For a young druid, learning to project one's spirit across the land into Moonglade via the teleportation spell is a critical step, granting constant access to the heart of druidic wisdom regardless of mortal distances. While Moonglade is open to all who walk the path of the wild, it is not free of tension. A growing rift divides Arch Druid Fandral Staghelm in Darnassus and Keeper Remulos in Moonglade over the stewardship of nature and the creation of Teldrassil. Despite these philosophical fractures within the Cenarion Circle, young acolytes are still welcomed unconditionally into the haven of Nighthaven to pursue their sacred studies. Arriving in Nighthaven brings the novice before Dendrite Starblaze, an elder tasked with guiding fledglings along the ways of the Claw. Before any initiate can claim the mantle of the bear, they must be immersed in its perspective: endurance, fury, and unyielding defense of the wild. Starblaze receives each new student with reverent deference to Father Cenarius, commencing the trials of the Great Bear Spirit.

quest:5922.text: Moonglade. This quest marks a young tauren druid's introduction to Moonglade, the sacred sanctuary of Cenarion druidism. Guided by Turak Runetotem in Thunder Bluff, the initiate learns to traverse the waking world to commune directly with nature's ancient keepers. Moonglade stands apart from the turbulent politics of Kalimdor. Sheltered beneath primeval boughs and watched over by Keeper Remulos, the son of Cenarius, this ancient valley is a neutral refuge for all who walk the path of nature. Whether night elf or tauren, any druid who enters Nighthaven does so as an equal peer under the timeless mantle of the Cenarion Circle. To aid your spiritual and martial development, Turak Runetotem teaches you a unique transport spell tied to the valley itself. By invoking the mystic bond between druids and the natural world, you step across hundreds of leagues in a heartbeat. This sanctuary will serve as both a study hall and an enduring refuge throughout your journey.

quest:5923.text: Heeding the Call. Heeding the Call marks the moment an apprentice night elf druid catches the attention of the Cenarion Circle's senior leadership. Summoned to Darnassus to meet Mathrengyl Bearwalker, the young initiate begins the sacred path toward mastering their first animal aspect, the bear. Novice druids honing their craft across Teldrassil—or studying abroad in far-off realms like Stormwind—eventually receive a personal summons. Instructors such as Kal in Dolanaar, Denatharion in Darnassus, or Theridran across the Great Sea carry word that Mathrengyl Bearwalker wishes to oversee their training personally. As the direct assistant to Arch Druid Fandral Staghelm, Mathrengyl is one of the most respected and knowledgeable mentors among the night elves, and his attention is an unmistakable sign that an apprentice is ready for genuine trials. Reaching Mathrengyl on the upper level of Fandral Staghelm's towering residence in the Cenarion Enclave opens the door to deeper mysteries. To serve nature properly, a druid must learn to embody its living creatures rather than merely observing them. Mathrengyl welcomes candidates with the news that their first great undertaking will be embracing the strength, endurance, and spirit of the bear—a journey that will take them far beyond Teldrassil to sacred ancestral grounds.

quest:5926.text: Heeding the Call. Heeding the Call marks a novice druid's summoning to Elder Rise in Thunder Bluff for advanced personal instruction. Relayed by innkeepers and kin across Horde settlements, the summons directs aspiring shapeshifters to Turak Runetotem. This meeting sets off the sacred trials required to master the form and spirit of the bear. Word travels quickly across the plains of Mulgore and through the dusty thoroughfares of Orgrimmar. Whether heard from Innkeeper Gryshka among the orcs, Innkeeper Pala in Thunder Bluff, or Gennia Runetotem in Bloodhoof Village, the message is the same: Turak Runetotem has noticed your early progress. The Cenarion Circle does not summon practitioners lightly, and this invitation signals that your days of elementary herb-gathering and basic spellweaving have earned you deeper communion with nature's wild spirits. Turak Runetotem serves as an assistant to Archdruid Hamuul Runetotem, guiding young tauren toward their ancestral duty inside the large Cenarion tent on Elder Rise. Welcoming initiates into a broader understanding of Cenarius's legacy, Turak instructs them that animals and plants are both allies and solemn charges. Meeting him is the opening threshold of the rite: stepping beyond basic mentorship to confront the trials of body and heart required to commune directly with the Great Bear Spirit.

quest:5931.text: Back to Darnassus. This quest marks the return of a novice night elf druid from the sacred groves of Moonglade to Darnassus. Having communed with the Great Bear Spirit, the initiate reports back to Mathrengyl Bearwalker in the Cenarion Enclave to begin practical shapeshifting trials. After communing with the Great Bear Spirit in Moonglade, a young druid must bridge the divide between timeless nature sanctuaries and the unsettled world. Dendrite Starblaze sends the initiate back from Nighthaven to Darnassus, entrusting the next phase of training to the local mentors watching over Teldrassil. Mathrengyl Bearwalker awaits in the Cenarion Enclave, guarding nature even in places where the balance falters. Receiving the blessing of the Great Bear Spirit is merely the first step; Mathrengyl prepares the initiate to anchor that fierce ancestral wisdom into physical form through demanding trials of body and heart.

quest:5932.text: Back to Thunder Bluff. "Back to Thunder Bluff" is an essential rite of passage for young tauren druids returning from the sacred glades of Moonglade. Having communed with the Great Bear Spirit, the initiate is sent by Dendrite Starblaze back to Elder Rise to continue training under Turak Runetotem. Moonglade stands apart from the factional divides of the mortal world, serving as a sanctuary where night elf and tauren practitioners of nature magic gather as the Cenarion Circle. After communion with the Great Bear Spirit, night elf mentor Dendrite Starblaze sends the young tauren back to their people. While night elves often view tauren as fledglings in the formalized teachings of Cenarius, Starblaze readily acknowledges the profound wisdom and balance maintained by Turak Runetotem. Upon climbing back to the sweeping heights of Elder Rise in Thunder Bluff, the novice stands before Turak Runetotem transformed. Communing with ancient totemic spirits like the Great Bear Spirit is deeply ingrained in tauren culture, yet undertaking the Path of the Claw marks a serious commitment. With the spiritual connection forged, Turak prepares the druid to put that newfound strength and endurance into active practice.

quest:6.text: Bounty on Garrick Padfoot. Bounty on Garrick Padfoot is an Alliance bounty contract issued by Deputy Willem at Northshire Abbey. It directs young recruits to hunt down a notorious local thief who has been harassing Elwynn's farmers and merchants from a secluded shack near the vineyards. Northshire Valley was once considered a secure sanctuary for training recruits and tending sacred vineyards, but the recent collapse of law and order across Elwynn has left it exposed. Bands of thieves have crept into the valley, and a cutthroat named Garrick Padfoot quickly rose to lead them. For weeks, Garrick and his gang have plundered shipments, robbed merchants along the roads, and threatened the local farmers. With the Stormwind guards stretched thin protecting the capital and outer borders, local marshals and deputies must rely on eager volunteers to keep peace in Northshire. Deputy Willem places a public bounty on Garrick's head to rid the valley of his gang once and for all. Taking down Padfoot at his rundown shack east of the river strikes an early blow against the broader lawlessness seeping into the human heartland.

quest:6001.text: Body and Heart. Body and Heart is the culminating trial in a young night elf druid's initiation into the path of the claw. Instructed by Mathrengyl Bearwalker in Darnassus, an initiate must travel into the darkshore wilderness, summon the moonkin guardian Lunaclaw, and prove they possess both inner resilience and martial strength before claiming the form of the bear. Night elf druid initiates are directed by Mathrengyl Bearwalker in Darnassus to venture east of the coastal settlement of Auberdine. There, tucked inside a natural cavern inhabited by wild moonkin, sits an ancient Moonkin Stone. By anointing this sacred monolith with Cenarion Moondust, the initiate rouses Lunaclaw, the ancient defender of the stone, who will challenge any claimant wishing to inherit the sacred strength of the claw.

quest:6002.text: Body and Heart. Body and Heart is the culminating trial for young tauren druids seeking to master Bear Form. Dispatched by Turak Runetotem in Thunder Bluff, the initiate must travel to the border of Mulgore and the Barrens to summon and best Lunaclaw at the Moonkin Stone. To truly follow the path of the Druid of the Claw, tauren initiates must unite spiritual conviction with physical resilience. After communion with the Great Bear Spirit in Moonglade, a druid's training is put to an active test. Turak Runetotem, the elder druid trainer atop the Elder Rise in Thunder Bluff, bestows Cenarion Lunardust upon worthy aspirants, charging them to seek out a sacred stone resting near the arid frontier where Mulgore meets the Barrens. Resting west of Camp Taurajo, the Moonkin Stone marks a rare Cenarion site in southern Kalimdor. Moonkin are not native to the sun-scorched plains of central Kalimdor, making the presence of the guardian beast Lunaclaw deeply significant. By scattering the lunardust across the ancient monument, the druid calls forth Lunaclaw in battle. Defeating the creature proves the aspirant commands both strength of body and clarity of heart, earning the beast's blessing and unlocking the inner essence of the bear.

quest:6061.text: Taming the Beast. Taming the Beast is the foundational rite of passage for young tauren hunters in Bloodhoof Village. Guided by trainer Yaw Sharpmane, the hunter ventures into Mulgore to tame an adult plainstrider, taking the first step toward forging a spiritual bond with the creatures of the Earthmother. For the tauren, hunting has never been purely about slaying beasts for meat and hides. Ancestral traditions hold that overcoming and communion with the wildlife of Mulgore allows a hunter to intake their spirits and draw closer to the Earthmother. Taming a companion beast elevates this connection, turning what could be an adversary into a lifelong partner aligned with the natural balance of the plains. Yaw Sharpmane begins an initiate's instruction not with ferocious apex predators, but with the swift and watchful plainstriders roaming Mulgore's grasslands. Armed with an enchanted taming rod, the hunter must face an adult plainstrider, calm its wild instincts, and earn its trust. This initial trial proves the hunter's resolve and prepares them for the more demanding beasts that follow.

quest:6062.text: Taming the Beast. This trial marks a young Horde hunter's first step into the art of beast taming. Guided by the veteran Thotar in Razor Hill, aspiring hunters use an enchanted taming rod to subdue and bond with a vicious dire mottled boar. For orc and Darkspear troll hunters coming of age in Durotar, surviving alone in the wilderness is only half the battle. A true master of the wilds must learn to project authority over nature itself, turning hostile beasts into loyal allies. Hunter trainer Thotar entrusts novices with an enchanted taming rod, challenging them to face down a fierce wild boar without resorting to a lethal arrow. Dire mottled boars roam the arid brush surrounding Razor Hill. Though brutish and ill-tempered, their resilience and ferocity make them ideal introductory subjects for taming. Withstanding their charges and enduring their aggression while channeling the rod's power requires patience and iron resolve—virtues essential for any tracker of the Horde.

quest:6063.text: Taming the Beast. This quest is the first trial in a night elf hunter's journey to mastering beast companionship. Instructed by Dazalar in Dolanaar, an aspiring hunter must use an enchanted taming rod to bond with a wild Webwood Lurker. It tests the hunter's ability to respect and commune with nature rather than attempting to violently dominate it. For the kaldorei, hunting is not merely about tracking quarry or surviving in the wilds; it is a sacred relationship with nature. Hunter trainers like Dazalar teach that nature is far greater than any individual mortal. Animals are not beasts of burden or tools to be forcibly bent to one's will, but autonomous creatures that require mutual respect. To prove readiness for a lifelong beast companion, novice hunters must demonstrate mastery over the primal instincts of local wildlife through ancient techniques rather than brute force. The trials begin with the giant arachnids infesting the boughs of Teldrassil. Dazalar entrusts the hunter with a specialized taming rod, directing them to seek out a Webwood Lurker. Venturing into the shadowed thickets, the hunter must face the venomous spider and establish an empathetic channel while withstanding its attacks. Successfully establishing this temporary mental bridge proves the hunter can commune even with the eerie, skittering predators of the World Tree.

quest:6064.text: Taming the Beast. Taming the Beast is the first trial in a dwarven hunter's journey to mastering companion beasts in Dun Morogh. Guided by Grif Wildheart in Kharanos, young trackers learn to quell and bond with a ferocious Large Crag Boar using an enchanted taming rod. Up to this point, dwarven mountaineers and trackers rely solely on their gunplay, traps, and wilderness instincts. Yet the true soul of a hunter lies in forging a lifelong partnership with a wild beast. Grif Wildheart, stationed outside the Thunderbrew Distillery in Kharanos, oversees this rite of passage. Rather than expecting a novice to permanently bind the first beast they come across, Grif instructs them to test their patience and resolve against several native species of Dun Morogh. The first trial pits the tracker against a Large Crag Boar, one of the rugged, thick-hided swine that roam the snowy foothills of Dun Morogh. Armored in bristling fur and tough flesh, these beasts are stubborn and aggressive, making them an ideal starting test of will. By wielding the enchanted Taming Rod provided by Grif, the hunter must withstand the boar's charge and soothe its ferocity until it submits to their command.

quest:6065.text: The Hunter's Path. The Hunter's Path is a vital milestone for young tauren hunters in Mulgore, directing them toward advanced training in beast companionship. Dispatched by their local mentors once their basic marksmanship and tracking are proven, novices are sent to Bloodhoof Village to seek the counsel of hunter trainer Yaw Sharpmane. This journey initiates the spiritual and practical trials required to tame and bond with wild beasts. To the nomadic Shu'halo, hunting is sacred rather than mere sport. A hunter must understand the balance of nature, honor the spirits of the plains, and show respect for the animals that sustain the tribes. When a young hunter demonstrates sufficient prowess in surviving the wild and wielding a bow or gun, their elders recognize that they are ready to step beyond solitary tracking. The directive to seek out seasoned mentors marks the threshold of true adulthood in tauren culture. The path leads novitiates across the sweeping grasslands of Mulgore to Bloodhoof Village, a central gathering settlement nestled beside Stonebull Lake. There awaits Yaw Sharpmane, an experienced huntsman well-versed in the temperament of the local fauna. Speaking with Sharpmane is not a mere formality; it signals a hunter's readiness to undertake the demanding trials of beast taming, learning how to commune with predators rather than merely hunt them.

quest:6068.text: The Hunter's Path. The Hunter's Path is a rite of passage directing young orc and troll hunters to Razor Hill. Under the guidance of master hunter Thotar, fledgling trackers learn the vital discipline of binding wild predators to their will. Up to this point, an apprentice hunter in Durotar relies solely on their own bow and cunning. Tracking prey through red clay canyons and harsh scrubland teaches patience, but true mastery in the Horde requires bonding with the untamed fauna of the land. Class trainers recognize when a student has grown capable enough to walk this road, directing them straight to Razor Hill. Waiting at Razor Hill is Thotar, a veteran hunter steeped in the wild lore of Durotar. Thotar serves as the mentor who instructs novitiates in the perilous ritual of subduing ferocious beasts without breaking their spirit. Meeting him is the first step toward walking the wilderness with a loyal companion at one's side.

quest:6074.text: The Hunter's Path. The Hunter's Path is a rite of passage offered to novice dwarven hunters across Dun Morogh once they reach basic competence in tracking and marksmanship. Local trainers direct their apprentices to Grif Wildheart in Kharanos to begin learning the art of taming wild beasts as permanent companions. Until a hunter masters the art of beast bonding, they walk the snowy crags of Dun Morogh alone, relying solely on axe, rifle, or bow. Trainers like Olmin Burningbeard and Tristane Shadowstone watch their pupils closely until they demonstrate the poise required to face a savage creature without killing it. Once a novice shows sufficient discipline, they are sent down the mountain roads toward Kharanos. In Kharanos, Grif Wildheart oversees the final trials of dwarven huntsmanship. Taming a beast is considered far more demanding than bringing one down for meat or pelt; it requires patience, physical endurance, and an intuitive bond with the wild predators of the mountains. Wildheart acts as the gateway to these trials, preparing the hunter for the grueling task of testing their willpower against Dun Morogh's fiercest wildlife.

quest:6081.text: Training the Beast. Training the Beast is the culminating rite of passage for young orc and troll hunters in Durotar. After demonstrating mastery over the wild beasts of the plains, hunters are sent from Razor Hill to Orgrimmar to study under veteran master hunter Ormak Grimshot. Completing this journey teaches the novice how to care for, feed, and hone the skills of their lifelong animal companion. In the arid canyon lands of Durotar, mastering a bow and surviving the harsh elements is only half of a hunter's duty. After proving their resilience by taming Durotar's fierce boars, crab scavengers, and armored scorpid stalkers, young hunters are ready for the true responsibility of stewardship. Thotar, stationed in Razor Hill, dispatches them north through the red clay gulches straight to the fortified gates of Orgrimmar. Within the bustling capital, aspiring track-masters must seek out the Valley of Honor, an enclave where warrior spirits and veteran stalkers hone their craft. There dwells Ormak Grimshot, one of the Horde's most revered master hunters. Ormak looks past raw youth to see whether a hunter possesses the patience required not just to command a beast, but to sustain and nurture it through famine, battle, and loss. A beast won through force of will remains wild until an understanding is forged between hunter and companion. Ormak imparts the sacred traditions required to maintain that bond: the knowledge of which foods nourish each creature's spirit, the discipline needed to teach them lethal techniques, and the spiritual focus required to revive a fallen beast should it collapse in the line of duty.

quest:6082.text: Taming the Beast. This quest marks the final trial in a young Horde hunter's basic rites of passage in Durotar. Guided by the veteran hunter Thotar in Razor Hill, an aspiring tracker must confront and tame a dangerous armored scorpid. Conquering this armored predator proves mastery over wild beasts and unlocks the lifelong ability to tame, call, and dismiss a true companion. Before a hunter is permitted to roam Kalimdor with a loyal animal companion, they must prove they can command the harshest wildlife Durotar has to offer. Razor Hill's hunter trainer, Thotar, sends trainees to subdue three distinct creatures with an enchanted taming rod. Having previously tested their mettle against dire boars and swift surf crawlers, hunters are tasked with facing the armored scorpid—a venomous, heavily plated predator that embodies resilience and lethal speed. Subduing an armored scorpid is not an act of mere slaughter, but a demonstration of focus and dominance while under relentless assault. Thotar urges hunters to emulate the beast's quick, confident strikes. Returning to Razor Hill after successfully charming the venomous arachnid proves that the hunter possesses the calm will necessary to maintain control. With the taming rod returned, Thotar imparts the innate techniques of the wild, allowing the hunter to seek out and bind a permanent companion of their own choosing.

quest:6083.text: Taming the Beast. The second trial in a young hunter's rite of mastery in Durotar, directed by the trainer Thotar in Razor Hill. Aspiring orc and troll hunters are sent to the coastline near the Echo Isles to pacify a surf crawler, expanding their bond beyond terrestrial beasts to coastal wildlife. Having successfully mastered a dire mottled boar, a fledgling hunter is tasked by Thotar to turn their attention toward the sea. Durotar's harsh environment includes jagged coasts and shallow reefs teeming with armored crustaceans. Facing a surf crawler requires patience and fortitude, as these armored crabs resist intrusion into their coastal domain. Thotar teaches that any beast a hunter binds must become an extension of their own strength. By subduing an aquatic creature like the surf crawler with the taming rod, the hunter learns to adapt their commanding presence across different temperaments and environments, proving their readiness for permanent companions.

quest:6084.text: Taming the Beast. This quest is the second trial in the dwarf hunter initiation given by Grif Wildheart in Kharanos. After learning to handle the brute resilience of a crag boar, the young hunter is tasked with mastering the swiftness and lethal grace of a native snow leopard. While crag boars teach a mountaineer how to withstand raw ferocity and absorb blows, Grif Wildheart emphasizes that a master hunter must understand different styles of combat. He points his students southeast toward the prowling snow leopards of Dun Morogh. Grif compares these graceful predators to an elegantly crafted rifle: outwardly striking, yet concealing devastating power beneath their pristine white coats. Using an enchanted taming rod, the hunter must confront a wild leopard and bend its hunting instincts into partnership. Snow leopards test agility, speed, and sharp reflexes rather than pure endurance. Mastering such a creature demonstrates that the novice can harmonize with predators that strike swiftly from the snowy crags, taking another step toward true command over the beasts of the wild.

quest:6085.text: Taming the Beast. This quest marks the final trial in a dwarven hunter's basic training under Grif Wildheart in Kharanos. By using an enchanted rod to subdue and understand an aggressive Ice Claw Bear, the hunter demonstrates mastery over sheer brute strength. Completing this exercise unlocks the foundational abilities needed to tame, call, and dismiss a permanent wild companion. Throughout Dun Morogh, mountaineers and scouts have long relied on hardy beasts to endure the freezing crags. After directing his students to practice on swift and cunning predators, master huntsman Grif Wildheart tasks budding hunters with capturing an Ice Claw Bear. Found prowling the snowdrifts east of Kharanos, these massive beasts embody raw physical power and relentless endurance—qualities every dwarven huntsman must learn to control. The trials with the Taming Rod are strictly educational exercises meant to teach hunters how wild instincts respond to will and calm intent. Once the rod holds the bear docile, the temporary bond fulfills its purpose. Returning the tool to Grif concludes the formal trials, prompting the master to share the permanent secrets of beast mastery: how to pacify any compatible wild creature and call upon it throughout a lifetime of adventure.

quest:6086.text: Training the Beast. Training the Beast is the culminating rite of passage for young dwarven hunters in Dun Morogh. Having mastered the art of soothing and taming wild predators in the snowy crags, novice rangers are directed into the heart of Ironforge to learn how to sustain, discipline, and care for a lifelong animal companion. After proving their mettle against the savage beasts of Dun Morogh—soothing large crag boars, snow leopards, and sturdy ice claw bears with a taming rod—apprentice hunters complete their trial under the watchful eye of Grif Wildheart near Kharanos. Yet capturing the wild heart of an animal is only half the bond. Grif sends his newly seasoned pupils up the mountain pass into Ironforge to find the military district known as the Hall of Arms. Within the stone vaults of Ironforge's Hall of Arms stands Belia Thundergranite, one of the dwarven kingdom's most revered master animal trainers. Belia imparts the essential knowledge that turns a wild, terrified beast into a fiercely loyal partner. Her teachings go far beyond simple commands: she shows young hunters how to nourish their pets, teach them new battlefield skills, and even call their spirits back from death should they fall defending their master. Dwarven tradition emphasizes that beast mastery is fundamentally built on respect rather than subjugation. Belia reminds every young hunter that an animal companion reflects the care it receives. If kept well-fed, respected, and properly trained, a beast will offer unwavering loyalty against troggs, frost trolls, and any threat that dares imperil Khaz Modan.

quest:6087.text: Taming the Beast. This trial marks the second stage of a tauren hunter's initiation into the art of beast taming. Guided by hunter trainer Yaw Sharpmane in Bloodhoof Village, the novice is charged with mastering the swift and fearless prairie stalker. Having successfully mastered the defensive endurance of the adult plainstrider, Yaw Sharpmane challenges the young hunter to look beyond mere survival. The prairie stalker represents an entirely different hunting philosophy: relentless speed, pack coordination, and fearless aggression. To tame one requires approaching a cunning predator without breaking stride, mirroring the wolf's own decisive nature. For the tauren, hunting with a beast is never about servitude or raw subjugation. Yaw Sharpmane stresses that the hunter and predator must fight as one cohesive unit, bound by mutual respect and shared rhythm. By bonding with the prairie stalker under the open skies of Mulgore, the hunter learns to complement a partner's assault and move in tandem during the heat of battle.

quest:6088.text: Taming the Beast. This trial marks the final lesson in a young tauren hunter's training under Yaw Sharpmane in Bloodhoof Village. By using a taming rod to bond with a wild swoop, the hunter proves mastery over creatures of the air and earns the sacred trust of the Earthmother. Completing this task grants the permanent knowledge required to tame and command a lifelong companion. Having already subdued ground-dwelling predators in the rolling plains of Mulgore, Yaw Sharpmane turns your focus toward the open heavens. The swoop is a fierce, sharp-beaked bird of prey known for its sweeping dives and intimidating demeanor. Bringing such a wild, airborne hunter under control tests your reflexes and your calm, demanding that you endure its talons while using the enchanted rod to align your spirit with its instincts. For the tauren, hunting and animal companionship are fundamentally spiritual pursuits rather than mere subjugation. By mastering creatures of both earth and sky, you demonstrate the balance and respect necessary to walk the plains without disrupting nature. Yaw Sharpmane recognizes this maturity, taking back his temporary taming rod and passing on the lasting techniques of calling, dismissing, and permanently taming a companion of your own choosing.

quest:6089.text: Training the Beast. Training the Beast is the culminating rite of passage for young tauren hunters in Mulgore. After demonstrating the spiritual patience and resolve required to soothe the wild beasts of the plains, hunters are sent to Thunder Bluff to learn the lifelong discipline of bonding with, nourishing, and commanding a permanent animal companion. Having successfully tested their spirit against the dangerous predators of Mulgore—plainstriders, prairie stalkers, and swoops—tauren hunters are judged ready for the true mantle of the hunter. Yaw Sharpmane, the mentor in Bloodhoof Village, entrusts the novice with a journey to Hunter Rise in Thunder Bluff. There stands Holt Thunderhorn, a legendary figure among the shu'halo whose reputation for communing with the wilds is surpassed only by his reverence for the Earthmother. To the tauren, a beast is not a simple weapon or thrall; it is a partner granted through harmony with the natural world. Holt Thunderhorn imparts the vital knowledge required to sustain this partnership. A hunter must learn not only how to guide the creature's combat instincts, but how to nourish its body through regular feeding, mend its injuries, and call its spirit back should it fall defending its companion on the plains.

quest:61.text: Shipment to Stormwind. Shipment to Stormwind is an Alliance delivery quest that concludes William Pestle's candle venture in Elwynn Forest. After gathering large wax candles from the local kobold vermin, adventurers carry the packaged shipment up the road into the Trade District of Stormwind to William's brother, Morgan Pestle. The Pestle brothers maintain an alchemical trade between the pastoral hamlets of Elwynn Forest and the bustling avenues of Stormwind City. William gathers herbs, reagents, and raw goods out in Goldshire, while his brother Morgan runs Pestle's Apothecary in the capital's Trade District. Because William cannot easily leave his post at the Lion's Pride Inn, he relies on travelers heading into the city gates to handle courier duties. William's parcel contains large candles gathered from kobolds in Elwynn's mines. He and Morgan run an apothecary in Stormwind, and William says he collects the candles for their wax. Delivering the shipment brings those supplies to Morgan in the Trade District.

quest:6101.text: Taming the Beast. This trial marks the second phase of a night elf hunter's pet taming training under Dazalar in Dolanaar. Hunters are tasked with subduing a nightsaber stalker using an enchanted taming rod to better appreciate the shifting diversity of wild beasts. It deepens the bond of understanding between the wilderness of Teldrassil and the sentinel trackers who walk beneath its boughs. While early lessons focus on understanding fundamental instincts, Dazalar emphasizes that nature's only constant is its continuous change. Every species of the forest carries a distinct temperament, and a hunter must learn to adapt their will accordingly. In the shadow of Teldrassil's canopy, this means engaging creatures that are cunning, stealthy, and far more predatory than simple webspinners. Nightsabers are revered by the kaldorei as sacred predators, fierce guardians, and stealthy companions of the Sentinels. For a novice hunter, channeling the power of the taming rod against a nightsaber stalker requires steady nerve and calm authority. By bending the predatory aggression of the stalker into a receptive bond, the hunter proves they can command more than merely docile or lesser creatures of the woods.

quest:6102.text: Taming the Beast. This quest marks the final trial in a young night elf hunter's basic training. Under the direction of Dazalar in Dolanaar, hunters must tame a predatory owl of the skies before unlocking the power to choose a true, lifelong companion. Before completing their initial beastcraft, night elf hunters must establish harmony with creatures from every corner of Teldrassil's ecosystem. Having previously proven their will against beasts of the underbrush, Dazalar charges the hunter with bringing down the spirit of the skies: the Strigid Screecher. These watchful birds of prey roost high across the boughs west of Dolanaar, requiring patience and a steady nerve to pacify with the enchanted Taming Rod. Succeeding with the Strigid Screecher fulfills the ancient lessons of communion between kaldorei hunters and nature. Upon returning the spent rod to Dazalar, the apprentice leaves behind training exercises and earns the full art of calling, dismissing, and permanently taming beasts of their own choosing across Azeroth.

quest:6103.text: Training the Beast. Training the Beast is the culminating rite of passage for fledgling night elf hunters in Teldrassil. After proving their mastery by taming wild beasts across the boughs, hunters are sent to Darnassus to learn the deeper arts of pet care and discipline from Jocaste. Before a night elf hunter can roam Kalimdor with a loyal companion by their side, they must master more than just the taming rod. While subduing a wild creature proves basic strength and will, an untutored beast remains an unpredictable liability. Once an initiate demonstrates their capability in the wilderness surrounding Dolanaar, Dazalar directs them inward to Darnassus to complete their training. Within the serene groves of the Cenarion Enclave, the revered hunter Jocaste imparts the essential arts of companionship. She instructs the young hunter in how to properly nourish their pet, resurrect it should tragedy strike, and nurture its fighting instincts through training. To night elves, this relationship is rooted in deep reverence for nature rather than simple domination.

quest:6121.text: Lessons Anew. "Lessons Anew" is an initiation quest given to developing Alliance druids by Mathrengyl Bearwalker in Darnassus. It directs initiates to travel to the sacred haven of Moonglade to meet with Dendrite Starblaze and begin their training in the art of purging venom and toxins. Druids hold a sacred connection to the living world, inherited through the teachings and blessings of the demigod Cenarius. Among these boons is the power to cleanse foul venoms through simple incantation. However, such potent gifts are never bestowed lightly upon initiates. To truly respect the miraculous ease of their magical arts, young druids must first understand the painstaking mundane toil required to fight toxins without nature's direct intervention. Mathrengyl Bearwalker, the druid trainer residing in the Cenarion Enclave of Darnassus, instructs his student to bypass local practice and journey directly to Moonglade. There in the quiet village of Nighthaven, Dendrite Starblaze coordinates the Cenarion Circle's broader efforts and stands ready to assign the novitiate an urgent, practical task.

quest:6122.text: The Principal Source. The Principal Source is an essential rite of passage for young night elf druids learning to understand and mend the natural world. Dispatched from Moonglade by Dendrite Starblaze, initiates must collect corrupted water from Cliffspring Falls in Darkshore to help Auberdine naturalist Alanndarian Nightsong halt a spreading sickness among the forest deer. Cliffspring Falls provides the primary freshwater supply for the northern reaches of Darkshore. When wildlife—particularly the local deer populations—began succumbing to an unnatural, lingering malady, the Cenarion Circle turned their attention to the river. Suspecting that the aquifer itself was compromised, Dendrite Starblaze in Moonglade entrusts novice druids with the crucial task of traveling to the mouth of the cavern beneath the falls to gather an untouched sample of the tainted water. Sampling the water is not without peril. Vicious naga have established a presence inside Cliffspring River Cave, nesting near the very headwaters of the falls. Their presence around the subterranean spring poses a direct threat to anyone investigating the blight. Despite the danger, securing an uncontaminated sample from the cave mouth is the only way for the Cenarion Circle to study the agent sickening the wilderness.

quest:6123.text: Gathering the Cure. Gathering the Cure is an essential trial for young night elf druids learning to master nature's healing powers in Darkshore. Guided by Alanndarian Nightsong in Auberdine, the druid collects vital natural reagents to brew a restorative salve for the region's ailing wildlife. This task lays the practical foundation for understanding how herbal remedies combat venom and disease. Following the discovery of a contaminated water source plaguing the local wildlife, Alanndarian Nightsong in Auberdine sets out to concoct an effective curative salve. While the sampled Cliffspring water forms the base of the mixture, genuine healing requires potent natural catalysts. The afflicted forest deer cannot recover on their own, making the gathering of wholesome remedies a matter of urgency for the Cenarion Circle. The restorative salve demands two crucial flora: Earthroot and Lunar Fungus. Earthroot provides pure curative properties, requiring the practiced eye of an herbalist to harvest from the rocky soil. To lend the mixture potency, Alanndarian sends the druid into the nearby eastern caves to gather fungal blooms that flourish in the dark, nestled among increasingly territorial and agitated moonkin.

quest:6124.text: Curing the Sick. Curing the Sick is an essential trial for young Alliance druids, tasking them with using a prepared salve to heal the poisoned wildlife wandering Darkshore. By directly relieving the afflicted deer, initiates address the encroaching malaise troubling northern Kalimdor before reporting back to the Cenarion Circle in Moonglade. Across the shadowed forests of Darkshore, from the waters of the Cliffspring River south to the borders of Ashenvale, the local wildlife suffers from a persistent sickness. Sickly deer wander aimlessly through the mist, weakened by unnatural toxins seeped into the soil and streams. Having gathered the necessary reagents, Alanndarian Nightsong entrusts an aspiring druid with a freshly brewed curative animal salve to treat the afflicted creatures in the field.

quest:6125.text: Power over Poison. Power over Poison marks the culmination of a young druid's trial to master venomous afflictions. Having learned to brew an herbal remedy by hand in Darkshore, the initiate returns to Darnassus to receive the Cenarion Circle's magical blessing to cleanse toxins at will. Before granting a druid the innate magical ability to purge toxins, the Cenarion Circle demands that initiates understand the suffering of common folk. In Darkshore, Alanndarian Nightsong tasks young practitioners with gathering Earthroot and Lunar Fungus manually, brewing a physical salve to heal stricken wildlife. This lesson ensures that when a druid channels nature's power to cure poison, they do so with deep empathy for those who must fight venom without spiritual intervention. Once the physical cure has proven effective in Auberdine, Starblaze sends the druid back across the sea to Darnassus. Within the boughs of the Cenarion Enclave, Mathrengyl Bearwalker awaits their return. Pleased with the initiate's grace under pressure, Mathrengyl formally bestows the art of natural cleansing, granting permanent mastery over venoms. Yet the trial also brings troubling news: the presence of virulent poisons in the wilds around Auberdine points to an unnatural blight disturbing the land's delicate balance.

quest:6126.text: Lessons Anew. Lessons Anew is a rite of passage for young tauren druids, initiated by Turak Runetotem on the Elder Rise of Thunder Bluff. It directs apprentices to travel to the sacred haven of Moonglade to begin mastering the art of cleansing natural and unnatural poisons. Guided by the night elf Dendrite Starblaze, this lesson sets aside mock trials in favor of confronting an urgent, real-world poisoning crisis. Druids hold a sacred mandate to protect the wilds, which includes the miraculous ability bestowed by Cenarius to purge virulent toxins with a simple incantation. However, such potent magic is not handed over without grounding. Turak Runetotem insists that before channeling divine energies to effortlessly dispel blights, a druid must understand the physical toll of venom and learn to treat it through grounded, mundane means. Rather than conducting training solely on the bluffs of Mulgore, promising acolytes are sent north through sacred pathways to Moonglade. There, within the peaceful village of Nighthaven, ancient night elf mentors such as Dendrite Starblaze oversee the education of both elf and tauren practitioners. This shared instruction highlights the delicate truce that exists within the Cenarion Circle, rising above the political strife separating Horde and Alliance.

quest:6127.text: The Principal Source. "The Principal Source" is a Horde druid quest tasked by Dendrite Starblaze in Moonglade. It sends initiating druids to Dreadmist Peak in the northern Barrens to sample tainted pool water and bring it to Tonga Runetotem at the Crossroads. The sample provides the foundation needed to understand a spreading poison afflicting the region's wildlife. Dreadmist Peak looms northwest of the Crossroads, high enough that its elevated springs and pools influence the surrounding weather patterns and natural moisture of the arid northern Barrens. Unfortunately, demon-worshiping cultists of the Burning Blade have established a presence on its crags. Dendrite Starblaze recognizes that foul sorcery atop such a vital natural vantage point can contaminate the entire surrounding basin. Across the northern savanna, sickly gazelles have been seen stumbling north of the main east-west crossroads trail. Tonga Runetotem, seeking aid on behalf of the local tauren, reached out to the Cenarion Circle to help discover what was poisoning the herd. By braving the peak and recovering a pure sample of the tainted waters, druids provide Tonga with the crucial catalyst required to analyze the malady and brew an antidote.

quest:6128.text: Gathering the Cure. Gathering the Cure is a sacred rite of passage for young tauren druids stationed at the Crossroads. Tasked by Tonga Runetotem, the druid gathers earthroot and sturdy kodo horns to craft a curative salve for the poisoned gazelles of the Barrens. Having secured a sample of water from Dreadmist Peak, Tonga Runetotem requires raw reagents to brew an effective physical antidote. While natural water provides the salve's base, common earthroot provides foundational medicinal qualities, and ground kodo horn gives the mixture the restorative potency needed to shock venom out of a creature's system. For a young druid, obtaining these ingredients means relying on the gifts of the earth and culling local beasts. Alchemy and herbal lore are traditional ways to counteract specific toxins, but each unique poison typically demands an exact, tailored cure. Tonga uses this laborious preparation to teach initiates the limits of physical medicines. True mastery over natural poisons comes not from carrying endless varieties of dried herbs and horns, but from attuning directly to nature's healing energies—a profound lesson that leads directly into the druidic art of Cure Poison.

quest:6129.text: Curing the Sick. Curing the Sick is an essential trial for young Horde druids, tasking them with healing afflicted wildlife in the northern Barrens. By applying a freshly concocted herbal salve to ailing gazelles, initiates demonstrate both their practical field medicine and their commitment to preserving natural balance. Completing this duty proves their dedication directly to the Cenarion Circle in Moonglade. Across the northern savanna of the Barrens, grazing gazelles have begun succumbing to an unnatural affliction. After gathering earthroot and kodo horns to assemble a curative remedy, Tonga Runetotem at the Crossroads entrusts a young druid with administering the field treatment. The initiate must search north of the main crossroads to find and minister to ten suffering animals, providing immediate relief before the rot takes further root in the ecosystem. Once the salve is dispensed, the druid's path leads back into the tranquil boughs of Moonglade. There, Dendrite Starblaze recognizes the initiate's compassion and vigilance. He notes that the suffering of the gazelles is merely a symptom of a deeper, insidious corruption stalking Kalimdor's wilderness. By tending to the lowliest beasts, tauren druids demonstrate that reverence for Cenarius transcends tribal boundaries, earning deeper secrets of poison cleansing and nature magic.

quest:6130.text: Power over Poison. Power over Poison is the concluding rite in a young Horde druid's trial to master restorative nature magic. Having cured afflicted gazelles around the Crossroads using only herbal mixtures, the initiate returns to Turak Runetotem on Thunder Bluff's Elder Rise to receive the true gift of Cure Poison. Before granting a fledgling druid the innate magical power to cleanse venoms, the Cenarion Circle demands they understand the physical reality of affliction. Dendrite Starblaze sent the novice to the Crossroads, where Tonga Runetotem had them gather earthly reagents for a curative salve made by hand. Only by treating the poisoned plains gazelles of the Barrens without spiritual aid does the student witness the agonizing struggle ordinary creatures face against natural and unnatural toxins. With the trial complete, Dendrite sends the initiate back to Turak Runetotem, the grand druid trainer residing on the Elder Rise in Thunder Bluff. Turak observes that the strange, virulent poisons surfacing near the Crossroads threaten the natural balance of the plains and warrant grave concern. Commending the initiate's grace under pressure, Turak permanently imparts the spiritual art of curing poisons, entrusting them to safeguard Kalimdor's living creatures.

quest:6181.text: A Swift Message. Quartermaster Lewis at Sentinel Hill needs urgent armor shipments from Stormwind to equip the People's Militia. Because Westfall receives almost no official military aid, he sends you to Thor the gryphon master to carry an urgent requisition note to the capital by air. Sentinel Hill stands isolated against a rising tide of Defias outlaws and gnolls, starved of direct military aid from Stormwind. Quartermaster Lewis relies on private contacts in the capital to keep the People's Militia supplied with weapons and armor. With gear running thin, his only lifeline is Osric Strang, an armorer located in Old Town. Getting an urgent requisition to him requires swift travel, leading Lewis to enlist travelers to contact Westfall's gryphon master, Thor. Gryphons provide the Kingdom of Stormwind with an invaluable rapid transit and courier network. Perched at Sentinel Hill, Thor manages the outpost's aerial link back to the capital. Handing Lewis's note to Thor opens the skies between Westfall and the royal city, demonstrating how crucial the gryphon riders are to sustaining frontier garrisons cut off from formal aid.

quest:6261.text: Dungar Longdrink. This errand introduces adventurers to Dungar Longdrink, the chief gryphon master of Stormwind. After collecting emergency supplies from Osric Strang, couriers must arrange for swift aerial transport to deliver the gear back to the embattled defenders in Westfall. Westfall is strained to its breaking point by Defias outlaws and feral harvest golems, leaving Quartermaster Lewis and the People's Militia desperate for provisions. When Lewis sent word to the capital for fresh equipment, armorer Osric Strang packed up everything requested. Moving military cargo on foot through the bandit-ridden roads of Elwynn and Westfall takes valuable time, making the kingdom's newly forged aerial routes an essential lifeline. Perched in the Trade District, Dungar Longdrink coordinates Stormwind's courier and passenger gryphons. The majestic beasts, traditionally raised and handled by Wildhammer dwarves, provide reliable transport across human lands so long as roosts on both ends know each other. By bringing Osric's heavy crate directly to Dungar, couriers learn how aerial logistics work, establishing a direct connection between the capital's stockpiles and frontier outposts like Sentinel Hill.

quest:6281.text: Continue to Stormwind. This errand introduces adventurers in Westfall to the speed and convenience of the Kingdom of Stormwind's gryphon network. Entrusted with an urgent requisition from Sentinel Hill, travelers take flight directly to Old Town to deliver word to the merchant Osric Strang. After Quartermaster Lewis in Sentinel Hill prepares a requisition note, the local gryphon master Thor offers the fastest route out of the contested plains. For a modest fee, travelers mount one of the kingdom's trained gryphons and soar above the dusty farmlands, the river border of Elwynn Forest, and over the high white ramparts of Stormwind City itself. Upon landing in the capital's trade roosts, the courier heads into Old Town to locate Osric Strang at his shop, Limited Immunity. Osric provides equipment and supplies to the frontier, though his grim reception highlights the growing rift between the beleaguered People's Militia in Westfall and the distracted rulers in Stormwind Keep.

quest:6285.text: Return to Lewis. Return to Lewis marks the final leg of an introductory courier flight, delivering desperately needed armor from Stormwind directly to Sentinel Hill. Entrusted with Osric's Crate by Dungar Longdrink, couriers fly across the skies of Elwynn and Westfall on gryphonback to resupply the embattled People's Militia. Westfall is slipping out of the kingdom's grasp, besieged by Defias bandits, ravenous gnolls, and mechanical harvest reapers. With overland supply routes harassed and roads dangerous for solitary wagons, the flight master network provides a crucial lifeline. Osric, an armorer based in the Old Town of Stormwind, prepared a heavy crate of armor intended to reinforce the battered volunteers of the People's Militia at Sentinel Hill. Gryphons are remarkably loyal and well-trained beasts, but navigating them across the lands requires established familiarity. As Dungar Longdrink explains to novice couriers, while gryphons instinctively know how to return home to their capital roost in Stormwind, they will only carry a rider to a remote outpost once the traveler has physically met the destination's flight master. Having previously checked in with Thor at Sentinel Hill, the skies over the frontier open up for rapid transit. Upon landing at Sentinel Hill, the delivered crate is received by Quartermaster Lewis, the officer tasked with outfitting Gryan Stoutmantle's volunteer force. Lewis immediately sets to work distributing the armor among the frontier defenders. For Sentinel Hill, reliable aerial contact with the capital means the difference between holding the line and being completely overrun by the Defias Brotherhood.

quest:6321.text: Supplying the Sepulcher. Supplying the Sepulcher is a logistical task issued by Deathguard Podrig at the Sepulcher in Silverpine Forest. To keep the local Deathguard detachment equipped against feral horrors and Scourge prowling the woods, an urgent weapon requisition must be routed via bat handler Karos Razok toward weapon suppliers in the Undercity. While Deathguard Podrig reports that the Sepulcher is relatively well-stocked, continuous attrition in Silverpine Forest consumes equipment at an alarming rate. Between feral beasts, prowling Scourge remnants, and aggressive local threats, frontline gear wears down or gets abandoned in skirmishes. Under orders from Executor Hadrec, Podrig drafts a direct requisition order addressed to Gordon Wendham, a weapon dealer operating out of the capital. Securing a steady flow of replacement blades and armor is essential if the Forsaken hope to retain their fragile footholds outside Tirisfal Glades. Moving critical correspondence and military supplies through Silverpine's mist-choked roads on foot is slow and prone to ambush. To bypass these perils, the Forsaken rely on captive, trained vampire bats. Handing Podrig's requisition to bat handler Karos Razok integrates foot soldiers into the broader aerial logistics network of the Undercity, establishing the aerial transit lines that tie outlying garrisons directly to Sylvanas's capital.

quest:6322.text: Michael Garrett. Michael Garrett is a simple courier task linking trade in the Undercity with the Forsaken's flight network. After collecting supplies packed by Gordon Wendham in the Trade Quarter, you are directed to deliver the crate to the bat handler Michael Garrett to arrange aerial transport out toward the Sepulcher. It highlights how the Forsaken utilize trained vampire bats to connect their capital with outposts across Lordaeron. Running a fledgeling kingdom carved out of the ruins of Lordaeron requires constant logistics. Outposts like the Sepulcher in Silverpine Forest rely heavily on goods, munitions, and provisions moving out from the Undercity. Gordon Wendham packs the necessary field supplies into a single crate in the city's Trade Quarter, but carting freight by ground through blighted forests is both slow and vulnerable to ambush by Scourge remnants or wild beasts. To bypass the dangers on the roads, the Forsaken rely on captive vampire bats bred and maintained by skilled handlers. Michael Garrett oversees these winged beasts from his roost in the Undercity's Trade Quarter. Delivering the cargo to him ensures the supplies can be strapped to a bat and flown directly over the hills to Silverpine, teaching new couriers how the capital coordinates with remote settlements.

quest:6323.text: Ride to the Undercity. Ride to the Undercity introduces fledgling Forsaken adventurers to the Horde's aerial flight network across Lordaeron. Carrying weapon requisitions from the embattled outpost of the Sepulcher, couriers take a dread bat directly into the Undercity's Trade Quarter to resupply regional defenders. Maintaining lines of communication between the Forsaken capital and its frontline outposts requires swift, reliable transit. Karos Razok, the bat handler stationed at the Sepulcher in Silverpine Forest, manages the trained dread bats that ferry messengers and supplies across the plagued landscape. With roads crawling with hostile beasts, Moonrage worgen, and remnants of the Scourge, taking to the skies is the safest and fastest way to ensure urgent military requests reach the capital. Upon touching down in the Undercity's bustling Trade Quarter, the courier delivers Podrig's equipment requisition directly to Gordon Wendham. As an Undercity weaponsmith dedicated to the Dark Lady's cause, Wendham ensures that regional outposts like the Sepulcher remain outfitted with clean, battle-ready armaments. Sustaining these defensive hubs is vital for the fledgling Forsaken nation as it secures its borders against surrounding enemies.

quest:6324.text: Return to Podrig. Return to Podrig is a logistics quest concluding a courier run between Silverpine Forest and the Undercity. After delivering a dispatch to the capital, the courier is entrusted with a crate of weapons to ferry back to Deathguard Podrig at the Sepulcher using the Forsaken bat handler network. Outposts throughout Lordaeron depend heavily on regular shipments from the Undercity to remain operational. At the Sepulcher in Silverpine Forest, Deathguard sentries face pressure from local worgen, Dalaran remnants, and Scourge stragglers. Supplying remote garrisons with freshly forged armaments is vital to holding the region under Forsaken control. Bat Master Michael Garrett operates the central roost in the Undercity's Trade Quarter, serving as the hub for Forsaken aerial travel. While bats naturally return to the capital, riders must first coordinate with local handlers like Karos Razok before flights to distant outposts can be charted. Flying Gordon's Crate across Lordaeron's skies teaches couriers how the Forsaken bind their scattered strongholds together.

quest:6341.text: The Bounty of Teldrassil. The Bounty of Teldrassil is an introductory errand given by Nessa Shadowsong in Rut'theran Village. Seeking to compare the unusual size and abundance of island fish with those caught along the mainland, she prepares a collection of bones and scales to be shipped across the strait to Darkshore. Delivering this package to the local hippogryph handler marks the first step in crossing the sea to Auberdine. Beneath the massive boughs of the World Tree, the sheltered waters surrounding Rut'theran Village teem with remarkably large and plentiful marine life. Nessa Shadowsong, observing the remarkable yields hauled in by local fishermen, seeks to discover whether this vitality extends to the ancient mainland coast or remains unique to the waters nourished by Teldrassil. To test her theory, she prepares a collection of scales and bones to be examined by Laird, a fellow fishmonger based across the water in Auberdine. Transporting cargo and travelers across the open sound between the island bough and mainland Kalimdor requires reliable wings. Rather than sending the parcel by small skiff, Nessa directs travelers directly to Vesprystus, the village hippogryph master. By handing the collection to him, travelers arrange the logistics needed to mount a trained beast and deliver the samples directly to the docks of Darkshore.

quest:6342.text: Flight to Auberdine. This errand introduces adventurers leaving Teldrassil to the night elves' aerial transit network. Tasked by the hippogryph master Vesprystus at Rut'theran Village, travellers take wing across the sea to deliver a bundle of oversized marine specimens to Laird in Auberdine. For many young adventurers departing the boughs of Teldrassil, Rut'theran Village marks the threshold between sanctuary and the wider world. While a mundane ferry plies the strait between the island haven and mainland Kalimdor, the night elves rely equally on their bonded hippogryphs. Entrusted with a parcel of rare fish parts from Nessa Shadowsong, travellers mount one of these winged beasts to establish their very first flight path onto the shores of Darkshore. The delivery itself is of keen interest to the fishermen of Darkshore. Laird, awaiting Nessa's findings at the docks of Auberdine, inspects the catch to find enormous scales the size of fists and a jawbone nearly twice the size of mainland specimens.
