The island waters around the base of the World Tree seem to produce altered or abnormally large life, a curiosity that hints at the potent, restless nature of Teldrassil itself.

quest:6343.text: Return to Nessa. This quest sends young travelers from Auberdine back to Rut'theran Village to deliver Laird's findings to Nessa Shadowsong. It concludes an introductory errand teaching adventurers how to navigate transit between the mainland of Kalimdor and Teldrassil. Having delivered Nessa Shadowsong's initial inquiries to Laird in Auberdine, travelers are charged with carrying his written observations back across the water. Laird notes stark differences in the fish catches between Darkshore and Teldrassil's shores, suspecting that the great World Tree itself alters local marine life. To make the journey back to Rut'theran Village, adventurers can either hire a flight from the hippogryph master Caylais Moonfeather or board the regular ferry running from the Auberdine pier. Upon receiving Laird's reply at Rut'theran Village, Nessa expresses fascination with the pronounced disparity in marine life. While the massive size of the fish near the World Tree provides an immediate boon to local fishermen, the underlying cause remains an open question among the Kaldorei. Nessa resolves to share the findings with her fellow villagers, content for now to harvest the abundant sea life while keeping a watchful eye on what forces might truly be responsible.

quest:6344.text: Nessa Shadowsong. Nessa Shadowsong is an introductory courier quest offered by Mydrannul in Darnassus. It guides fledgling adventurers down from the World Tree to Rut'theran Village to meet the fishing merchant Nessa Shadowsong. This task serves as the initial step connecting the canopy capital to the shores and harbors below. Within Darnassus, Mydrannul watches over travelers looking for work and purpose. When fishing merchant Nessa Shadowsong needs a package delivered across the sea to Darkshore, Mydrannul directs able couriers toward the coast. While many young night elves spend their early journeys entirely within the boughs of Teldrassil, this simple request encourages them to look outward to the mainland. Reaching Rut'theran Village requires stepping through the glowing roots of the city's western portal near the Temple Gardens. The gateway descends through the World Tree to its ocean-level roots, where fishing docks and hippogryph perches connect Teldrassil to the rest of Kalimdor. There, Nessa Shadowsong tends to her trade, preparing shipments meant for the port settlement of Auberdine.

quest:6361.text: A Bundle of Hides. A Bundle of Hides is an introductory delivery task in the Barrens given by the tauren Jahan Hawkwing at the Crossroads. He asks travelers to take cured game pelts across central Kalimdor to Thunder Bluff for leatherworking. The errand serves to introduce new Horde couriers to the Crossroads wind rider roost and the mechanics of flight transport. The Crossroads is the bustling heart of commerce and travel throughout the Barrens, connecting orcs, trolls, and tauren across the arid plains. Hunters constantly harvest hides and meat from the savanna's roaming beasts, but local outposts lack the facilities to process every raw material on site. Jahan Hawkwing gathers pelts from regional hunts and relies on passing travelers to route them west to Thunder Bluff, where master leatherworkers can craft vital gear for the Horde. Carrying heavy cargo across the rugged trails of the Barrens and up into Mulgore on foot is a grueling journey exposed to quilboar ambushes and predators. To expedite trade, Jahan directs couriers straight to Devrak, the Crossroads' wind rider master. Entrusting goods to Devrak and taking wing aboard a trained wyvern demonstrates the vital logistical network tying the Horde's scattered settlements together.

quest:6362.text: Ride to Thunder Bluff. This quest sends young Horde adventurers taking their first flight path across Kalimdor aboard a wind rider. Entrusted with a shipment of cured hides, travelers depart the dry crossroads of the Barrens to deliver valuable leatherwork supplies directly to the heights of Thunder Bluff. For many travelers making their way through the Barrens, booking a flight with Devrak marks their first journey through the skies on the back of a wind rider. These winged wyverns provide vital aerial links between the dispersed settlements of the fledgling Horde, avoiding the perilous ground routes prowled by quilboar and centaur packs. The shipment consists of a bundle of cured hides prepared in the Barrens and destined for Ahanu, a craftsman working out of Hewa's Armory in Thunder Bluff. Nestled right beneath the great wind rider roost on the central mesa, Ahanu relies on raw supplies brought in from hunting outposts across the plains to outfit local warriors and hunters.

quest:6363.text: Tal the Wind Rider Master. Tal the Wind Rider Master is a simple courier task connecting Mulgore leatherworkers with merchants in the Barrens. The leatherworker Ahanu entrusts a parcel of finished hides to be flown out of Thunder Bluff. Delivered directly to Tal, the mesa's flight master, it introduces fledgling Horde travelers to the wind rider transport network. Trade between Mulgore and the arid scrub of the Barrens is essential for the young Horde. Ahanu, a leatherworker selling his wares on Thunder Bluff's lower rise, produces durable leather goods intended for Jahan Hawkwing's trade stall at the Crossroads. Because the overland walk down the bluffs and through the golden plains takes hours on foot, merchants rely on winged couriers to ferry fragile or urgent parcels over the craggy divide. Perched upon the highest central tier of Thunder Bluff, Tal tends to the city's flock of wind riders—also known as wyverns. These intelligent, leathery-winged beasts are ideally suited for navigating Kalimdor's unpredictable thermal drafts and rugged peaks. Tal coordinates flights departing to outposts like the Crossroads, ensuring messengers and cargo pass quickly between the tauren capital and their orcish allies.

quest:6364.text: Return to Jahan. Return to Jahan marks the concluding leg of an introduction to the Horde's wind rider flight network between Mulgore and the Barrens. After visiting Thunder Bluff to deliver hides to the skinner Ahanu, travelers take a wyvern back to the Crossroads carrying finished leather wares for the merchant Jahan Hawkwing. For many travelers, this errand is their first experience soaring aboard a trained wind rider. Tal, the wind rider master perched high atop Thunder Bluff's central mesa, arranges flights across the plains of central Kalimdor. As long as a traveler has already established contact with the roost at another settlement—such as Devrak's outpost at the Crossroads—these winged beasts can effortlessly cover leagues that would otherwise demand a perilous overland trek through the Red Rocks and northern Barrens. The courier run serves an economic purpose alongside flight training. Jahan Hawkwing operates out of the bustling settlement of the Crossroads, where hunters, scouts, and mercenaries gather daily. Raw hides sent to Ahanu on the high rises of Thunder Bluff are refined into durable armor and equipment, then flown back to the dusty intersection of the Barrens to supply the Horde's expanding frontier efforts.

quest:6365.text: Meats to Orgrimmar. Meats to Orgrimmar is a short introductory logistical quest offered by Zargh at the Crossroads. He asks young orc and troll adventurers to take a package of prime Barrens meat to the settlement's wind rider master, Devrak, introducing them to flight transport back to the Horde capital. The vast plains of the Barrens support an abundance of wildlife, from zhevras and plainstriders to kodos and thunder lizards. Zargh has prepared several choice cuts intended as a personal delivery to Gryshka, the bustling innkeeper of Orgrimmar's Valley of Strength. To keep the meat fresh and avoid the long, dust-choked trek across the Southfury River into Durotar, Zargh sends runners across the Crossroads directly to the wind rider perch. Reaching Devrak marks a young Horde warrior's first formal introduction to the wind rider flight network. By partnering with the wind rider masters, the Horde connects remote outposts like the Crossroads directly to its fortified seat of power in Orgrimmar. Devrak prepares the courier and cargo for a swift aerial ride over the savannah.

quest:6384.text: Ride to Orgrimmar. This errand introduces Horde adventurers to aerial travel across Kalimdor by commissioning a wind rider from the Crossroads to Orgrimmar. Entrusted with Zargh's fresh cuts of meat, travelers land at the capital's Skytower to deliver the package directly to Innkeeper Gryshka. Crossing the arid expanse between the Crossroads and the red cliffs of Durotar on foot is grueling, but the Horde maintains a reliable network of trained wind riders to bridge the distance. Devrak, the Crossroads flight master, oversees these wyverns, dispatching messengers and travelers high above the dusty canyon trails to deliver vital dispatches and trade goods directly into the capital. The flight is not merely a sight-seeing trip; it carries a personal touch. Zargh of the Crossroads prepared a parcel of prime raw cuts destined for Innkeeper Gryshka in Orgrimmar's Valley of Strength. Once the wind rider touches down upon Orgrimmar's central Skytower, Gryshka's inn is only a brief walk away, where she eagerly accepts the gift—noting with fondness that Zargh certainly knows his way into a lady's heart.

quest:6385.text: Doras the Wind Rider Master. Innkeeper Gryshka of Orgrimmar has written a letter of gratitude to Zargh at the Crossroads and needs a courier to fly it back to the Barrens. To arrange passage, she directs travelers up to the city's skytower to consult Doras, the Horde's chief wind rider master. After receiving a fresh shipment of bulk meat flown in from the hunting grounds of the Barrens, Innkeeper Gryshka drafts a formal letter of thanks to the butcher Zargh. Lacking the time to make the overland journey through Durotar herself, she relies on the aerial courier network established between Kalimdor's major Horde settlements to speed her message back across the frontier. Doras oversees Orgrimmar's wind rider roost atop the flight tower in the Valley of Strength. His trained wyverns are the lifeblood of Horde military communication and logistics, bridging the perilous gap between the capital and outlying outposts like the Crossroads in a fraction of the time required by foot or kodo cart.

quest:6386.text: Return to the Crossroads.. This errand concludes a courier delivery between Durotar and the Barrens, carrying Gryshka's reply back to Zargh at the Crossroads. It demonstrates how wind riders serve as the vital aerial backbone linking the Horde's settlements across Kalimdor. Having delivered a parcel of prime meat to Gryshka in Orgrimmar, you are entrusted with her written reply for Zargh. Doras, the wind rider master roosted atop Orgrimmar's high bluffs, provides a mount back to the Barrens. Because you have already established contact with Devrak at the Crossroads, Doras's wyverns know the flight path, turning an arduous overland march across the Southfury River into a swift ride through the desert sky. Zargh's bold culinary courtship succeeds. Gryshka's warm response confirms that nothing impresses an orc quite like quality provisions, prompting Zargh to celebrate and even muse over an impending wedding. Beyond the romantic triumph, the journey solidifies a traveler's access to the Barrens' central transit hub.

quest:6387.text: Honor Students. Mining instructor Brock Stoneseeker rewards promising young apprentices in Thelsamar with honorary mining picks. To arrange delivery of the tools from Ironforge, he directs adventurers to enlist the aid of the local gryphon master, Thorgrum Borrelson. In the dwarf town of Thelsamar, mining is more than an occupation—it is a cornerstone of daily survival and dwarven pride. Brock Stoneseeker watches dozens of fresh recruits pass through his training, drilling them on rock composition and tunnel safety. For the students who distinguish themselves above the rest, tradition demands recognition in the form of a finely crafted honorary pick. Because local supply is limited, obtaining these picks requires reaching across Khaz Modan into the heart of Ironforge. Rather than trusting the slow, mountainous trek back through Dun Morogh on foot, Brock relies on the kingdom's aerial courier network. Thorgrum Borrelson tends the gryphon roost perched beside Thelsamar, offering rapid transit to the capital. Handing Brock's order to Thorgrum initiates a courier run that connects rural frontier training directly to the grand foundries of the dwarven capital.

quest:6388.text: Gryth Thurden. This errand introduces adventurers to Ironforge's gryphon network by tasking them with carrying a bundle of ceremonial tools to the city's gryphon master. Entrusted with the Honorary Picks by Golnir Bouldertoe, the courier must deliver them to Gryth Thurden so they can be dispatched back to Loch Modan. After traveling from Loch Modan to the Great Forge, couriers receive a bundle of Honorary Picks from Golnir Bouldertoe meant for Brock Stoneseeker's mining apprentices. Rather than making the trek back down the mountain passes on foot, Golnir advises taking advantage of the dwarven gryphon network, sending the messenger across the city to coordinate with Ironforge's master handler. Gryth Thurden manages the flight roosts within the great mountain hall, connecting Ironforge to dwarven settlements across Khaz Modan. Thurden agrees to arrange transport back to Thorgrum Borrelson in Thelsamar provided the adventurer has already scouted the route and spoken with the local handler there. The delivery teaches fledgling heroes the vital role aerial couriers play in tying the dwarven kingdom together.

quest:6391.text: Ride to Ironforge. Ride to Ironforge is an introductory courier quest that sends newly trained adventurers on their first gryphon flight from Thelsamar in Loch Modan into the dwarven capital. Entrusted with a list of top mining students from Brock Stoneseeker, the traveler carries the dispatch straight to Golnir Bouldertoe at the Great Forge. For many young mountaineers and travelers, the flight from Thelsamar to Ironforge marks their very first journey astride a gryphon. Handled by Gryphon Master Thorgrum Borrelson, this short passage carries travelers over Dun Morogh's snowy ridges and directly into the cavernous entry of the mountain fortress. The errand itself serves the Deep Mountain Mining Guild. Brock Stoneseeker regularly sends word of his most promising mining pupils from Thelsamar. Waiting at the Great Forge is Golnir Bouldertoe, who inscribes the apprentices' names onto ceremonial honorary picks to reward their hard work in Loch Modan's quarries and mines.

quest:6392.text: Return to Brock. Having delivered Brock Stoneseeker's missive to Ironforge, you are entrusted with a batch of Honorary Picks to carry back to Thelsamar. Taking advantage of the dwarven aerial transit network, you board a gryphon with Gryth Thurden to return quickly across the mountains. The great mountain stronghold of Ironforge relies on a coordinated network of gryphon roosts to maintain communication and trade with outlying settlements like Loch Modan. Gryth Thurden, Ironforge's gryphon master, oversees this transit from the city's central flight master platform. Because travelers must first establish a rapport with an aerie's handler before flying there, Gryth ensures you have already spoken with Thorgrum Borrelson in Thelsamar before saddling a mount for the return trip. Your journey serves a practical purpose beyond introducing you to gryphon travel: Brock Stoneseeker, a respected mining instructor in Thelsamar, needs new equipment for his apprentices. With the Honorary Picks safely delivered to his hands, young miners across the valley can begin working the rich copper and tin veins that line the hills surrounding the Loch.

quest:6395.text: Marla's Last Wish. Marla's Last Wish is an early Forsaken task given by Novice Elreth in Deathknell. It asks you to hunt down the Scourge-enslaved remnants of Samuel Fipps so he can be buried beside his murdered wife, Marla. The task reflects the fledgling Forsaken society's yearning to honor human ties and distinguish themselves from the mindless Scourge. Before the Third War devastated Lordaeron, Marla and Samuel Fipps lived together as husband and wife. When the plague swept through their lands, Samuel succumbed to the contagion and was reanimated as a mindless thrall of the Scourge. Though Marla was spared undeath, she could not escape Samuel himself, who brutally slew her in his mindless frenzy. Despite dying at her husband's hands, Marla harbored no hatred in her final moments. Her dying wish, remembered by Novice Elreth, was to rest eternally beside her husband in the Deathknell graveyard. Novice Elreth dispatches Forsaken adventurers northeast of Deathknell to locate Samuel Fipps, who still wanders among a ruined campsite. Putting an end to Samuel's torment serves a dual purpose: it cleanses an encroaching Scourge minion from the valley and allows his physical remains to be carried back to Marla's resting place. As Elreth emphasizes, honoring the deceased and respecting their final wishes is a vital moral distinction separating the newly liberated Forsaken from the mindless malice of the Scourge.

quest:64.text: The Forgotten Heirloom. Farmer Furlbrow and his wife Verna fled their home when masked brigands overran their pumpkin patch in Westfall. In the frantic rush to escape, Furlbrow left behind a cherished family heirloom inside his farmhouse wardrobe. Recovering the pocket watch represents a rare chance to salvage something personal from the encroaching chaos gripping the region. Like many homesteaders throughout Westfall, Farmer Furlbrow and his wife Verna were driven from their land through brute force. Roused from their beds by sudden shouts and violence among the pumpkin patches, the couple had only moments to bundle what few belongings they could carry before fleeing their farm. In the panic, Furlbrow was forced to leave behind a pocket watch gifted to him by Verna's father on their wedding day, leaving it behind in the wardrobe of their occupied farmhouse. The Furlbrow pumpkin farm now teems with Defias thugs, looters, and opportunistic thieves such as Benny Blaanco who pick through the remains of abandoned homes. For ordinary folk, returning to retrieve personal treasures is a death sentence. By securing the watch from the wardrobe amidst the ransacked rooms, adventurers deliver a small measure of dignity to a family that has lost nearly everything else to the rising tide of lawlessness.

quest:7.text: Kobold Camp Cleanup. Kobold Camp Cleanup is an early military task assigned by Marshal McBride to newly arrived recruits in Northshire Valley. The mission directs volunteers to cull the kobold vermin lurking in the northern woods, attempting to keep the aggressive subterranean scavengers from overwhelming the abbey grounds. It serves as an initiate's first true test in defending the borders of the Kingdom of Stormwind. Northshire Valley was once a quiet sanctuary for prayer, agriculture, and novice training, but recent years have stretched Stormwind's military thin. With the King missing and royal garrisons dispersed, wild creatures and opportunists push boldly against civilization's edge. Marshal McBride organizes local defense from inside Northshire Abbey, relying on fresh volunteers to suppress encroaching threats before they disrupt abbey operations or threaten the surrounding vineyards. Kobolds are cowardly, candle-obsessed cave-dwellers by nature, usually content to pick at underground seams away from direct sunlight. However, an entire clan has pressed into the northern timberline of Northshire. Left unchecked, their sheer numbers turn scavenging into open raiding. McBride's order to hunt down kobold vermin serves a dual purpose: it winnows their vanguard and proves whether a recruit possesses the resolve needed to protect the realm.

quest:730.text: Trouble in Darkshore?. Trouble in Darkshore? is an introductory Alliance quest offered by Chief Archaeologist Greywhisker in Darnassus. Concerned after weeks of silence from an excavation team sent across the sea, he asks travelers to journey to Auberdine to investigate their disappearance. It bridges the dwarven scholarly expedition with the wild, shadowy coast of Darkshore. In the grand night elven capital of Darnassus, dwarven researchers from Ironforge pursue the ancient mysteries of Kalimdor. Chief Archaeologist Greywhisker sent an excavation party across the water to Darkshore to unearth artifacts of antiquity. When weeks go by without a single missive or progress report, Greywhisker grows anxious, fearing that his field crew has encountered perils they were ill-equipped to survive alone. Greywhisker laments that many in the Alliance dismiss dwarven archaeology as little more than an eccentric hobby. However, findings in Khaz Modan have convinced his colleagues that an ancient, terrifying force threatens Azeroth spanning from Lordaeron to Kalimdor. Digging into Darkshore's ruins is not merely an academic endeavor—it is an effort to understand historic cataclysms and the deep-seated menaces buried beneath ancient soil.

quest:745.text: Sharing the Land. Assigned by Baine Bloodhoof in Bloodhoof Village, this task sends young Horde adventurers to curb the destructive poaching of the local Palemane gnolls. By culling their tanners, skinners, and poachers, you protect Mulgore's wildlife and learn the tauren philosophy of living in balance with the Earth Mother. The tauren hold deep reverence for the natural world, taking from it only what is necessary to survive and honoring the Earth Mother in all things. The Palemane gnolls, having settled south of Bloodhoof Village and in a cavern to the west, harbor no such respect. Rather than hunting in moderation, they aggressively butcher wildlife across the plains, leaving stripped carcasses and upset ecosystems in their wake. For a people striving to build a peaceful homeland in Mulgore, this reckless slaughter cannot be tolerated. Baine Bloodhoof initially hoped to resolve the matter peacefully, attempting to open dialogue with the encroaching gnolls. The Palemanes rejected every overture, answering diplomacy with hostility and continued devastation. Seeing that negotiation is futile, Baine turns to force. Young braves are sent directly to their hunting camps to put down the poachers, tanners, and skinners before the grasslands suffer permanent damage. This mission serves as a rite of passage and a moral lesson for growing champions. Upon returning from the culling, Baine reminds the adventurer that taking life must never be done out of malice, but out of necessity to maintain harmony. Life and death exist as an interconnected circle where one cannot thrive without the other, a foundational truth every guardian of Mulgore must carry forward.

quest:746.text: Dwarven Digging. Dwarven Digging is a quest in Mulgore given by Baine Bloodhoof in Bloodhoof Village. Concerned that dwarven excavations will enrage the native beasts and defile the sacred earth, Baine tasks young Horde defenders with sabotaging their efforts by confiscating and shattering their pickaxes. Northwest of Bloodhoof Village, dwarven prospectors have begun staking out a dig site in the rolling hills of Mulgore. The Explorer's League and its excavation crews seek titan relics and earthen secrets across Kalimdor, but their operations rarely respect indigenous lands or customs. To the tauren, the earth is a living mother to be revered, not stripped and hollowed for stones and metal. Baine Bloodhoof recognizes that the dwarven machinery and relentless blasting threaten the fragile harmony of the plains. Beyond the physical destruction, the commotion agitates the local wildlife, stirring the plains kodos into frenzy. By smashing the prospectors' tools at their own forges, the tauren hope to send a blunt message and stall the encroachment before lasting harm is done.

quest:747.text: The Hunt Begins. The Hunt Begins is a foundational rite of passage for young adventurers in Camp Narache on Red Cloud Mesa. Tasked by Grull Hawkwind, initiates are sent to hunt local plainstriders to provide meat and feathers for the village. Fulfilling this task marks the first step toward earning the respect of Chief Hawkwind and eventually gaining entry into Thunder Bluff. On the heights of Red Cloud Mesa, survival and tradition intertwine. The tauren hunt out of necessity to feed and clothe their people, while also viewing the stalk and chase as a vital test of discipline and sport. When the stores of Camp Narache run lean, the community looks to its rising youth to gather fresh plainstrider meat for cooking and sturdy feathers for tribal garments. No aspiring hero simply walks off Red Cloud Mesa into the wider reaches of Mulgore without proving their worth. Grull Hawkwind serves as a primary judge of character for the newcomers, insisting that one must prove their capability before stepping before his father, Chief Hawkwind. Bringing in a clean hunt demonstrates not only self-reliance, but devotion to supporting the tribe.

quest:748.text: Poison Water. Poison Water begins the tauren effort to purge pollution from Mulgore's sacred wells. Entrusted by Mull Thunderhorn in Bloodhoof Village, young Horde defenders gather natural components from the plains to craft a restorative ritual totem. The grassy plains of Mulgore are sacred ground to the tauren, but insidious forces have begun threatening their vital lifeblood. Mull Thunderhorn, an elder stationed in Bloodhoof Village, discovers that goblin interlopers and their lackeys have tainted the precious water wells that sustain the tribes and the local wildlife. The pollution strikes directly at the spiritual heart of the nomadic people who recently settled here. To counteract industrial contaminants, Mull relies on traditional tauren shamanism rather than crude remedies. Cleansing the Winterhoof Water Well requires crafting a potent ritual totem imbued with the vitality of Mulgore's indigenous predators. He sends hunters to track prairie wolves for their paws and mature plainstriders for their talons across the southwestern plains, enlisting the strength of the land to heal its own wounds.

quest:752.text: A Humble Task. A Humble Task is an early rite of duty given by Chief Hawkwind in Camp Narache. As the Chieftain attends to pressing tribal concerns on the Red Cloud Mesa, he asks a young adventurer to venture southeast and check on his elderly mother at the local water well. The request emphasizes communal responsibility, elder reverence, and the daily harmony essential to the tauren way of life. In the shadow of Camp Narache, every member of the tribe is expected to pull their weight and share in the harmony of life. For young tauren coming of age, tribal duty is not measured solely in battle prowess against quilboars or predators; it begins with basic social responsibility. Chief Hawkwind demonstrates this ethos directly: bound to his post by administrative and defensive leadership, he places his trust in novice adventurers to watch over the community's vulnerable elders. Mulgore's Red Cloud Mesa relies on vital natural water wells scattered beyond the perimeter of the encampment. Early in the morning, Greatmother Hawkwind left the village unattended to retrieve fresh water from the southeastern spring. In a land stalked by territorial wildlife and encroaching Bristleback quilboars, an elder remaining absent for hours raises quiet concern, prompting Hawkwind to send aid to ensure she is unharmed.

quest:753.text: A Humble Task. A Humble Task is an introductory rite of service in Red Cloud Mesa, where an elder tests a fledgling adventurer's humility and diligence. By carrying fresh well water across the plains to Camp Narache's leader, young tauren learn that serving their people starts with the simplest duties. Greatmother Hawkwind has walked many trails in her long life, and while her spirit remains steady, her legs no longer carry her across the plains with the speed of her youth. Stationed near the water well on the southern edges of Red Cloud Mesa, she tends to her responsibilities with patient resolve. When aspiring tribal defenders cross her path, she redirects their youthful energy toward practical community needs, offering them a chance to prove their worth through service rather than violence. The task asks the initiate to haul a filled water pitcher back northwest to Camp Narache and present it directly to the settlement's leader, Chief Hawkwind, who happens to be the Greatmother's son. In tauren society, survival across the arid plains of Mulgore demands shared labor and reliable supplies of fresh water. Demonstrating respect for the community's elders by shouldering their burdens is considered the cornerstone of becoming a true protector of the tribe. Chief Hawkwind sees more than a mere chore completed when a young wanderer arrives bearing water from his mother. In tauren custom, an individual's readiness to champion their people across wider lands begins with humility and an unprompted willingness to help. By demonstrating this quiet discipline, the initiate catches the chief's eye and earns recommendation for the ancient Rites of the Earthmother, the true spiritual tests that open the gates to Thunder Bluff.

quest:754.text: Winterhoof Cleansing. Winterhoof Cleansing is a rite entrusted to Horde adventurers by Mull Thunderhorn in Bloodhoof Village. After goblin operations fouled the local springs, a consecrated totem must be carried into the Venture Company's territory to purify the Winterhoof Water Well. Restoring this spring is a vital first step in healing the poisoned waters of central Mulgore. The grassy plains of Mulgore rely on a delicate network of ancestral water wells to sustain both wild game and the scattered tauren tribes. Recently, ruthless industrial mercenaries of the Venture Company moved into the rolling hills southeast of Bloodhoof Village. Their operations have contaminated the local aquifers, leaving the Winterhoof Water Well rank and toxic. Wild beasts shun the tainted water, and the nearby camps face an impending crisis if the corruption spreads further through the earth. To counter the industrial filth, Mull Thunderhorn carves and enchants a ritual cleansing totem infused with the blessings of the Earth Mother. However, delivering this remedy requires braving armed Venture Company goons who have staked their claim over the spring. By placing the totem directly at the wellhead, an adventurer dispels the foul runoff, allowing clean, life-giving water to rise once more from the depths of the earth.

quest:756.text: Thunderhorn Totem. Thunderhorn Totem is a task given by Mull Thunderhorn in Bloodhoof Village to craft a sacred cleansing totem. To combat goblin-borne pollution spreading through Mulgore's water wells, young Horde champions must gather natural talons from plains predators to bind the land's primal strength into ritual wood. As the Venture Company's industrial exploitation poisons Mulgore's precious water sources, Mull Thunderhorn works urgently to craft remedies. Creating the Thunderhorn Cleansing Totem requires the natural essences of the plains' most focused hunters: prairie stalkers and flatland cougars. By taking the claws of these predators roaming east and west of Bloodhoof Village, the ritual channels the raw, uncorrupted predatory vigor of the wildlife directly into the totem. Tauren tradition sees a profound distinction between hunting for sustenance or spiritual balance and the wholesale plunder practiced by the goblins. Mull emphasizes that the purity with which native predators hunt is vital for purifying corrupted earth. Where goblin machinery defiles the springs with oil and industrial waste, the natural strength of the beasts contending with the land provides the spiritual catalyst needed to restore the Thunderhorn Water Well.

quest:757.text: Rite of Strength. The Rite of Strength is the initial trial in the traditional Rites of the Earthmother undertaken by young tauren at Camp Narache. To demonstrate their bravery and defense of the tribe, initiates must cull encroaching Bristleback quilboar in Brambleblade Ravine and present their belts to Chief Hawkwind. For a young tauren seeking recognition from tribal elders and eventual acceptance in Thunder Bluff, completing the Rites of the Earthmother is an essential duty. Bestowed by Seer Graytongue, the Rite of Strength serves as the starting trial. It demands physical courage and decisive action in defense of Red Cloud Mesa, testing whether an initiate can face the tribe's mortal foes without flinching. The chosen crucible for this trial is Brambleblade Ravine, a thorn-choked gash east of Camp Narache occupied by Bristleback quilboar. These aggressive interlopers continuously trespass on ancestral lands, ambushing hunting parties and raiding camp supplies under cover of darkness. Slaying them and claiming their belts serves as both proof of valor and a necessary measure to keep the settlement secure.

quest:758.text: Thunderhorn Cleansing. Thunderhorn Cleansing is an essential spiritual rite in Mulgore, charging travelers with purifying the corrupted Thunderhorn Water Well. Armed with a ritual totem prepared by Mull Thunderhorn, adventurers restore the contaminated spring vital to the local tribe. Successful purification earns the heartfelt approval of the Thunderhorn ancestors. Water wells across the sweeping plains of Mulgore are vital lifelines for the tauren nomadic tribes who recently settled the grasslands. When foul poisons taint these underground springs, both wildlife and nearby settlements face devastating consequences. The Thunderhorn Water Well, situated north of Bloodhoof Village, fallen victim to contamination, requires deliberate spiritual intervention to heal the troubled land. To counteract the corruption, Mull Thunderhorn crafts a consecrated Cleansing Totem imbued with spiritual potency. Carrying this relic directly to the poisoned waters allows adventurers to channel ancestral power into the spring, dispersing the toxins and restoring pristine natural balance. Mull receives direct confirmation of the deed's success when the spirits of Thunderhorn ancestors visit him in a dream to express their enduring gratitude.

quest:759.text: Wildmane Totem. Wildmane Totem represents the third and final stage in Mull Thunderhorn's efforts to craft cleansing totems for Mulgore's poisoned wells. To restore the Wildmane Well, the ritual demands offerings taken from the territory's fiercest natural predators: prairie wolf alphas. After securing the materials required to consecrate totems for the Winterhoof and Thunderhorn wells, only one afflicted source remains in central Mulgore: the Wildmane Well. The poisoned water across the plains threatens both migrating wildlife and settlements, demanding powerful primal ingredients to restore the earth's natural balance. To counter the potent corruption lingering in the northern waters, Mull Thunderhorn requires a sacrifice of ferocity. Prairie wolf alphas prowl the grasslands, particularly around the towering bluffs beneath Thunder Bluff. Harvesting their teeth channels the relentless drive and resilience of Mulgore's apex hunters directly into the crafting of the cleansing totem. In tauren spiritual tradition, drawing upon the land's creatures carries emotional and elemental weight. Mull views the gathering of alpha teeth not as conquest, but as a somber necessity where the sacrifice of Mulgore's predators helps heal the Earth Mother's stricken waters.

quest:760.text: Wildmane Cleansing. Wildmane Cleansing marks the culmination of the tauren ritual efforts to purify the vital watering holes of Mulgore. Entrusted by Mull Thunderhorn in Bloodhoof Village, heroes take the completed Wildmane Totem north to cleanse the final poisoned well. Driving back goblin pollutants restores balance to the plains and secures the pastoral livelihood of the tauren tribes. Water is sacred lifeblood across the sun-drenched plains of Mulgore, sustaining the herds, the soil, and the nomadic tribes who have recently gathered around Thunder Bluff. When the Venture Company and encroaching goblins began contaminating these aquifers with toxic industrial runoff, the tauren elders recognized an existential threat. Following the purification of the Winterhoof and Thunderhorn wells, the Wildmane Water Well stands as the third and final corrupted site requiring spiritual intervention. Crafted from specific elements gathered across the region, the Wildmane Cleansing Totem channels the restorative power of ancestral spirits and elemental earth. Planting the totem beside the foul waters north of Thunder Bluff disperses the foul chemicals, drawing out the toxins and reviving the natural flow. By completing the ritual, the tauren safeguard their people from disease and send an unmistakable message that the despoiling of their sacred ground will not be tolerated.

quest:763.text: Rites of the Earthmother. Rites of the Earthmother marks the transition of a young tauren out of the secluded Red Cloud Mesa and into the wider plains of Mulgore. Having proven your mettle in Camp Narache, Chief Hawkwind sends you north to Bloodhoof Village with a carved totem to continue the ancient trials under Baine Bloodhoof. For generations, young tauren have tested their strength within the safe cradle of Camp Narache on Red Cloud Mesa. Completing the initial trials proves one has the discipline and resolve to survive, but the sacred Rites of the Earthmother require far more than surviving local wildlife. Chief Hawkwind recognizes when an initiate has outgrown the mesa's sheltered hunting grounds and must step into the broader community. To bridge the journey between Narache and the central settlements, Chief Hawkwind provides a hand-carved totem as a mark of introduction. Bearing this emblem down the winding path to Bloodhoof Village, you present yourself to Baine Bloodhoof, the young chieftain of the village and son of High Chieftain Cairne Bloodhoof. The totem serves as testament to your readiness for the rites of spirit and wisdom that lie ahead.

quest:764.text: The Venture Co.. Investigating a ravaged Venture Company caravan in Mulgore uncovers an aggressive buildup of Venture Company goblins digging into the eastern hills. Having had their formal requests for mining permits flatly rejected, the company chose to quarry the Earth Mother's soil anyway, prompting Morin Cloudstalker to commission a lethal response. The tauren of Mulgore revere the land as an extension of the Earth Mother, cherishing its pristine plains and balanced wildlife. When the Venture Company approached the tribes seeking rights to blast and excavate the rolling hills for raw ore, their petitions were categorically denied. Undeterred by tribal decrees or territorial sovereignty, the relentless cartel sneaked heavy machinery, laborers, and overseers directly into Mulgore's eastern ridges to mine illicitly. Tauren scouts like Morin Cloudstalker recognize that corporate greed cannot be reasoned with through diplomatic appeals once picks hit the stone. With documents recovered from a ravaged Venture Co. caravan confirming the company's mining operation, Morin dispatches Horde champions to cut down both the taskmasters cracking the whips and the laborers driving the drills. The bloody reprisal is intended to ensure the Venture Company calculates the cost of trespassing as far too steep.

quest:765.text: Supervisor Fizsprocket. Supervisor Fizsprocket is a high-ranking Venture Company overseer stationed within the mining tunnels of Mulgore. Charged by Morin Cloudstalker with putting an end to the goblin enterprise's calculated pillaging, Horde adventurers enter the mine to eliminate him and recover his detailed clipboard. Documents recovered from a destroyed Venture Company caravan revealed that the Venture Company was not merely digging for ore—they were deliberately formulating schemes to drive the tauren from Mulgore entirely. By uprooting the locals, the rapacious corporation sought unchecked freedom to strip the rolling hills and deep subterranean veins of every natural resource.

quest:766.text: Mazzranache. Maur Raincaller in Bloodhoof Village has fallen victim to a venomous bite from Mazzranache, a legendary plainstrider that terrorized his grandfather a generation ago. Struck by fever and delirious nightmares, the tauren requires a potent remedy brewed from Mulgore's wildlife before the infection claims his life. For years, Maur Raincaller regarded Mazzranache as little more than a harrowing family tale passed down by his grandfather. The elder tauren spoke of an unusually savage plainstrider armed with glowing red eyes, razor-sharp talons, and a toxic bite that defied the peaceful nature of most Mulgore wildlife. When Maur crossed paths with the beast out on the open grass, the legend proved all too real, leaving him severely wounded and struggling to make it back to safety. The creature's venom works swiftly, inducing high fevers and nightmarish delirium. To purge the venom before it turns fatal, traditional tauren medicine relies on the vitality of the local beasts. Maur requires a prairie wolf heart, a flatland cougar femur, a plainstrider scale, and a swoop gizzard. By combining the essences of these varied hunters and scavengers, he can brew a concoction capable of halting the necrotic spread and nursing him back to health.

quest:767.text: Rite of Vision. The Rite of Vision is a pivotal coming-of-age trial within the Rites of the Earthmother, testing a young adventurer's spiritual maturity. Initiated by Baine Bloodhoof, the quest directs aspirants to seek counsel from the village seer, Zarlman Two-Moons. Undertaking this journey is essential for anyone seeking the blessings and respect of the elders on the rises of Thunder Bluff. For generations, the nomadic tauren have turned to the Earthmother to guide their people across the plains of Kalimdor. Now gathered within the safe borders of Mulgore, their spiritual traditions remain the cornerstone of their society. The Rite of Vision is one of the ancient trials known as the Rites of the Earthmother. While earlier trials test an initiate's physical strength and connection to the hunt, the Rite of Vision demands an inward journey, directing young tauren and honored allies to commune directly with the spirits. Before any spiritual vision can be sought, an initiate must be prepared by someone steeped in ancient wisdom. In Bloodhoof Village, that responsibility falls to the revered shaman Zarlman Two-Moons. Entrusted by Baine Bloodhoof to prepare travelers, Zarlman possesses the keen sight to recognize those walking the path of the ancestors, offering the preliminary rites and sacred preparations necessary to pierce the veil of the physical world.

quest:771.text: Rite of Vision. The Rite of Vision is a foundational spiritual trial undergone by young tauren stepping beyond the Red Cloud Mesa into greater Mulgore. To pierce the veil and receive guidance from ancestral spirits, initiates must gather natural reagents to brew the Water of the Seers under the watchful eye of Zarlman Two-Moons in Bloodhoof Village. Before any vision can be granted, the initiate must demonstrate an intimate understanding of the natural gifts found across Mulgore. Zarlman Two-Moons instructs the seeker to collect well stones found near the sacred communal water wells and ambercorn fallen beneath the roots of Mulgore's ancient trees. These natural elements are not merely physical objects; to the tauren, they hold the latent magic and lifeblood of the Earth Mother, ready to be channeled into ritual use. Once gathered, Zarlman combines the stones and ambercorn into the potent Water of the Seers. When consumed beside the village's tribal flame, this ceremonial draft clears the mind and summons an ethereal guide. Following this manifestation across the plains forms the true heart of the rite, testing the initiate's ability to walk between the physical world and the spiritual whispers of the land.

quest:772.text: Rite of Vision. The Rite of Vision is the spiritual climax of an ancient trial undertaken by young tauren in Bloodhoof Village. By drinking the sacred Water of the Seers beside the tribal bonfire, initiates summon a spectral guide to lead them toward their destiny. After gathering the necessary ritual herbs and passing the initial trials of faith, an initiate is granted the Water of the Seers by the village shaman, Zarlman Two-Moons. This potent draught must be ingested before the roaring tribal fire at the heart of Bloodhoof Village. When consumed with a focused and respectful mind, the sacred waters expand the drinker's perception beyond physical sight, bridging the veil between the material plane and the spiritual realm. Upon drinking the brew, the flames yield an ethereal apparition: an ancestral ghost wolf. The spirit does not speak or fight, but silently lopes northwest across the rolling plains of Mulgore. A true initiate must heed its quiet path, tracking its journey away from the village and deep into the rocky hills where the hermit Seer Wiserunner awaits in secluded meditation. Reaching Seer Wiserunner at the mouth of his mountain cavern signifies the successful completion of the vision. This journey across the grassy hills tests an initiate's patience, trust in ancestral guidance, and attunement to the Earth Mother. Passing this rite grants the young adventurer the right to undergo the ultimate test of adulthood: the Rite of Wisdom.

quest:773.text: Rite of Wisdom. The Rite of Wisdom is the concluding trial in the traditional Rites of the Earthmother undertaken by young adventurers in Mulgore. After purifying their sight through the Rite of Vision, petitioners travel to the sacred burial grounds of Red Rocks to commune with an Ancestral Spirit and receive the blessing of the dead. Having cleared their perception through the Rite of Vision, young protectors are directed east of Thunder Bluff toward Red Rocks. This ancient burial ground holds the physical remains and lingering spirits of those who fought and died to carve out a peaceful existence in Mulgore. Passing the trial requires approaching the resting grounds with proper reverence and communion, facing whatever territorial threats roam the hills to seek the counsel of the honored dead. At the summit of Red Rocks, the communion with the Ancestral Spirit is not a test of martial strength, but of spiritual readiness and continuity. The spirits resting there represent the generation that fought alongside Cairne Bloodhoof to establish Thunder Bluff and safeguard the tribes. By receiving their blessing, the supplicant officially inherits the solemn duty of protecting the city, earning their place as a recognized adult and defender worthy of entering Thunder Bluff with pride.

quest:775.text: Journey into Thunder Bluff. Journey into Thunder Bluff is the culminating pilgrimage marking the end of a young hero's trials across Mulgore. Having completed the sacred Rites of the Earthmother under the guidance of the spirits, the adventurer is granted an audience with the High Chieftain of the tauren, Cairne Bloodhoof. Before any traveler or fledgling warrior can truly claim to have proven themselves in Mulgore, they must undergo the ancient Rites of the Earthmother. These trials test strength, vision, and wisdom across the rolling plains and ancestral sites of the land. Once the Ancestral Spirit acknowledges the final rite, the initiate is deemed worthy of entering the city of Thunder Bluff not as a mere visitor, but as an honored defender of the tauren people. The quest directs the traveler from the sacred ground where the spirits wander straight to the towering heights of Thunder Bluff. Perched atop the mesas, the city is a beacon of peace carved from red stone and supported by sweeping rope bridges and massive wooden elevators. There, on the High Rise, High Chieftain Cairne Bloodhoof awaits to personally greet those who have walked the path of the ancestors.

quest:776.text: Rites of the Earthmother. This trial, set directly by High Chieftain Cairne Bloodhoof, tasks rising heroes with hunting down the great kodo beast Arra'chea across the plains of Mulgore. Though an initiate may have completed the traditional rites of passage, Cairne expects his people to continually reaffirm their strength, tracking, and devotion to the tribe. Returning with Arra'chea's horn proves an adventurer is ready to serve the wider Horde beyond the mesas. Reaching Thunder Bluff marks the end of simple youth for a tauren, but High Chieftain Cairne Bloodhoof does not let young hunters rest on their laurels. To Cairne, earning a place among the high bluffs is merely the beginning of one's responsibility to the United Tauren Tribes. Rather than sending initiates against petty pests, he demands proof of real fieldcraft: the tracking and clean harvest of one of Mulgore's most renowned wandering beasts. The quarry is Arra'chea, a massive, legendary kodo whose looping trek winds across the golden grasses northeast of Thunder Bluff. To fell such a creature takes more than brute force; it demands patient stalking across the open savannah and respect for a titan of the plains. Bringing Arra'chea's horn back to the high rise earns not just personal glory, but provisions for the city, as Cairne immediately dispatches skinners and gatherers to ensure nothing of the sacred beast goes to waste.

quest:780.text: The Battleboars. The Battleboars is a rite-of-passage hunting quest given by Grull Hawkwind in Camp Narache. Young tauren are tasked with culling the vicious war-trained boars of Brambleblade Ravine to defend tribal lands and feed the settlement's youth. To the east of Red Cloud Mesa lies Brambleblade Ravine, a thorn-choked scar held by the Bristleback quilboar. As tensions between the Shu'halo and the quilboar escalate into open war, the Bristlebacks have trained vicious battleboars to probe tauren boundaries and terrorize their traditional hunting grounds. Left unchecked, these aggressive beasts threaten not only game trails but the safety of Camp Narache itself. For the tauren, hunting serves both defensive necessity and communal sustenance. Grull Hawkwind instructs initiates to bring back the snouts and flanks of the slain battleboars. Even beasts trained by quilboar hands are not wasted; their meat and gristle are harvested to prepare hearty stew for the tribe's youth, turning a quilboar weapon into nourishment for the next generation of tauren defenders.

quest:781.text: Attack on Camp Narache. Attack on Camp Narache is a vital discovery made within the quilboar den of Brambleblade Ravine. A dirt-stained map reveals that the aggressive Bristleback tribe is actively plotting an organized siege against Camp Narache. Delivering these plans to Chief Hawkwind alerts Camp Narache in time to summon aid from Bloodhoof Village. While scouting deep inside the caverns of Brambleblade Ravine, young tauren adventurers uncover a crude, dirt-stained map laying on the rock floor. Upon closer inspection, the parchment reveals deliberate tactical markings made by the Bristleback quilboar. Rather than engaging in mere opportunistic skirmishes, the quilboar are coordinating a full-scale, prolonged siege against Camp Narache. Carrying the attack plans back to Camp Narache provides Chief Hawkwind with crucial intelligence. Recognizing the dire threat posed to the relatively undefended camp and its young initiates, Hawkwind prepares to send word to Bloodhoof Village for reinforcements. The intercepted map transforms what could have been a catastrophic ambush into a prepared defense.

quest:783.text: A Threat Within. A Threat Within marks the beginning of service for defenders answering Stormwind's call in Northshire Valley. Directed into Northshire Abbey to meet Marshal McBride, fresh volunteers discover that the kingdom's military is spread thin abroad, leaving local garrisons unable to handle domestic troubles without civilian aid. Northshire Valley was once a quiet retreat dedicated to prayer, farming, and monastic study. Today, it stands as the first line of defense against domestic unrest in Elwynn Forest. Stormwind's regular military forces have been widely deployed across distant fronts, leaving the capital's heartlands dangerously understaffed. With few official soldiers stationed locally, the Stormwind Guard must recruit any willing volunteer who arrives at the abbey gates. Inside Northshire Abbey, Marshal McBride coordinates the valley's defenses amidst growing regional pressures. While foreign perils threaten the Alliance from afar, lawless bandits, infesting vermin, and subterranean pests exploit the power vacuum right on the kingdom's doorstep. Answering this summons draws recruits into immediate martial service, beginning with clearing the abbey's immediate perimeter before confronting the deeper rot taking root across Elwynn.

quest:784.text: Vanquish the Betrayers. Vanquish the Betrayers is a Horde military strike ordered by Gar'Thok in Razor Hill to reclaim Tiragarde Keep from human invaders. Kul Tiran forces under Lieutenant Benedict have reoccupied the stronghold, directly violating the fragile peace between Durotar and Theramore. Eliminating their garrison is critical to securing the eastern coast of the orcish homeland. When Thrall led the Horde across the Great Sea to Kalimdor, he formed an uneasy alliance with Lady Jaina Proudmoore to vanquish the Burning Legion at Mount Hyjal. That peace was shattered when Jaina's estranged father, Grand Admiral Daelin Proudmoore, arrived with the formidable navy of Kul Tiras. Blaming all orcs for the atrocities of the Old Horde, the Admiral invaded Durotar and seized coastal footholds, including Tiragarde Keep. Though Daelin was eventually slain at Theramore, remnants of his fleet refuse to honor any pact or surrender their hatred. Following the fall of the Grand Admiral, Tiragarde Keep was briefly broken, but Kul Tiras reserves under Lieutenant Benedict have since retaken the fortress. From this fortified redoubt between Razor Hill and Sen'jin Village, the sailors and marines harass travelers and threaten the eastern sea approaches. Gar'Thok views their entrenched position as an immediate danger to the security of Durotar, calling upon Horde warriors to strike directly at Benedict's command.

quest:786.text: Thwarting Kolkar Aggression. Thwarting Kolkar Aggression is a vital Horde defense mission handed out by the scout Lar Prowltusk near Sen'jin Village. Players are tasked with infiltrating Kolkar Crag to destroy three sets of coordinated invasion plans before the centaur clan can strike the fledgling settlements of Durotar. While scouting western Durotar, the troll tracker Lar Prowltusk slipped into Kolkar Crag under cover of night. What he discovered was alarming: the Kolkar centaurs were not merely mounting disorganized coastal raids, but coordinating an ambitious, three-pronged invasion aimed squarely at the orc and Darkspear homelands. The centaur warlords divided their battle strategies among three distinct leaders, intending to strike the Valley of Trials, Sen'jin Village, and the gates of Orgrimmar itself. To avert catastrophic fighting across the dry red canyons of Durotar, recruits are sent deep into Kolkar Crag to cut the head off the serpent. Infiltrating the dusty encampment and burning the three attack scrolls disrupts the centaurs' chain of command. While Lar Prowltusk remains confident that the Horde would inevitably crush any full invasion, destroying these documents spares Durotar's defenders costly bloodshed while their young nation is still finding its footing.

quest:787.text: The New Horde. The New Horde is an introductory task in the Valley of Trials given by the veteran warrior Eitrigg. It directs fresh recruits to report to Gornek within the Den to begin their training. Through this brief summons, Eitrigg shares his personal journey and Thrall's guiding vision for a redeemed Horde. Eitrigg stands in the Valley of Trials under orders from Warchief Thrall to evaluate and mentor the newest hopefuls of the Horde. Having abandoned the Old Horde after the Second War, disillusioned by its corruption by the Burning Legion, Eitrigg lived in quiet exile until captured by humans. Rescued by Thrall, he chose to return after learning of the young Warchief's dream: an honorable Horde rooted in ancestral shamanism, entirely severed from demonic masters. Before any recruit can venture beyond the harsh canyons of the Valley of Trials, they must prove their mettle. Eitrigg sends newcomers into the shaded cavern known as the Den to speak with Gornek. Though Gornek rarely minces words about the crude state of incoming aspirants, his oversight ensures that only those who master discipline and survival are permitted into the wider reaches of Durotar.

quest:791.text: Carry Your Weight. Carry Your Weight is an introductory task offered by Furl Scornbrow atop the watchtower overlooking Razor Hill. Too old to fight on the front lines, the scarred veteran asks young Horde adventurers to salvage canvas from local human and centaur hostiles so he can fashion supplies to aid their journey. Furl Scornbrow is a veteran of the Third War who marched alongside Warchief Thrall during the pioneering of Durotar and the desperate defense at Mount Hyjal. Now slowed by age and old injuries, he no longer wields his axe in battle. Instead, he maintains a steady vigil from the Razor Hill watchtower, sounding the alarm against incursions while supporting the next generation of defenders. With signal horn alerts growing less frequent as the Horde's grip on the region tightens, Furl passes his hours crafting practical gear. Sturdy canvas is hard to come by in the arid canyons of Durotar, but it is carried in abundance by both the Kul Tiran interlopers along the eastern shore and the nomadic Kolkar centaur roaming the plains. Scavenging scraps from these hostile forces provides Furl the cloth needed to stitch utility bags for active scouts.

quest:792.text: Vile Familiars. Vile Familiars is an early task given by Zureetha Fargaze to newly arrived champions in the Valley of Trials. While monitoring the valley's trials, Zureetha discovered an insidious coven of the Burning Blade hiding in a nearby cavern. To check their sudden spread, recruits are sent to hunt down the demonic familiars creeping out into the red dirt of Durotar. The Valley of Trials is meant to be a proving ground where young orcs and Darkspear trolls demonstrate their strength, discipline, and loyalty to Thrall's Horde. It was intended to test recruits against native predators like scorpids and boars, not demonic corruption. Yet, hidden in a cave to the northeast, agents calling themselves the Burning Blade have established a secret coven right under the watchful gaze of the valley's overseers. Zureetha Fargaze, an instructor sent to guide newcomers near the Den, noticed the subtle taint before it could overrun the canyon. Minor demonic creatures known as Vile Familiars have begun pouring from the cave's mouth, hurling fire and menacing anyone who wanders too close. Before the Horde can root out the masters hiding in the shadows, young recruits are tasked with cutting down these lesser servants to keep the valley secure.

quest:794.text: Burning Blade Medallion. Assigned by the warlock Zureetha Fargaze, this task sends young Horde initiates deep into the Burning Blade Coven cave in the Valley of Trials. There, players must confront a hidden cultist and recover an artifact of dark magic known as the Burning Blade Medallion. The mission reveals that demonic corruption is actively taking root right under the Horde's nose. While young orcs and trolls undergo basic trials of combat and survival in the Valley of Trials, an insidious menace lurks in the shadows. Through her divinations, the warlock Zureetha Fargaze senses that the vile familiars infesting the northern bluffs are merely the vanguard of a darker presence. Deep within a nearby cavern, the Burning Blade cult has established a hidden coven, practicing dark arts and harboring dangerous relics of demonic power.

quest:8.text: A Rogue's Deal. A seemingly casual favor for Calvin Montague in Deathknell sends a traveler on the road to the Gallows' End Tavern in Brill. The errand involves ferrying a mysterious, unaddressed message to Innkeeper Renee under the guise of an ordinary courier run. Lounging amidst the solemn graves and ruined chapels of Deathknell, Calvin Montague presents himself as an exhausted fighter burdened by too many Scourge zombies and creeping spiders. Claiming he simply needs a hand delivering a message to Brill, he entrusts passing adventurers with an unmarked letter. His breezy demeanor and promise of generous coin make the task appear as nothing more than a harmless favor meant to point freshly awakened Forsaken toward the region's main town.

quest:804.text: Sarkoth. Having avenged the wounded troll Hana'zua by slaying the monstrous scorpid Sarkoth, an adventurer must carry word of his plight back to the Den. Gornek must be alerted so that rescue can reach the stricken scout before his venomous wounds claim his life. Stranded upon the high bluffs of the Valley of Trials, the Darkspear scout Hana'zua found himself venom-struck and unable to return down the treacherous paths unassisted. Though vengeance was delivered upon Sarkoth—the dread scorpid that felled him—pride alone cannot carry an envenomed warrior across the arid stones. Bound to his rock, he relies on a passing initiate to bring word back down to the training encampment. Returning to Gornek at the Den concludes the trial. Gornek immediately recognizes the menace of Sarkoth and swiftly organizes aid for Hana'zua. In the eyes of the Horde commanders, stepping aside from one's personal training to vindicate and rescue a fallen stranger embodies true honor, proving an initiate's worth long before they march out into Durotar proper.

quest:805.text: Report to Sen'jin Village. Report to Sen'jin Village marks the moment young Horde initiates leave the secluded Valley of Trials behind to alert the Darkspear trolls of demonic cult activity. Entrusted by Zureetha Fargaze, messengers carry word of the Burning Blade to Master Gadrin, discovering that shadow magic already threatens the nearby coasts. After proving their combat mettle and recovering dark medallions from the Burning Blade Coven within the Valley of Trials, novices are declared ready for the wider world. Zureetha Fargaze recognizes that the demonic presence within the sacred proving grounds is no isolated nuisance, but a symptom of a creeping blight across Durotar. She directs young adventurers east past the ravine's mouth and south toward the coast to warn the Darkspear tribe.

quest:806.text: Dark Storms. Dark Storms is a critical task assigned by Orgnil Soulscar in Razor Hill to strike down a rogue warlock corrupting the land. A goblin named Fizzle Darkstorm has entrenched himself in Thunder Ridge on behalf of the insidious Burning Blade cult. Eliminating him is vital to safeguarding Durotar from demonic resurgence before the cultists spread further. While young Horde defenders patrol the borders of Durotar, internal corruption festers right under their watch. Orgnil Soulscar, conducting inquiries from Razor Hill, discovered that Thunder Ridge to the northwest has fallen under the sway of dark magic. The ravine is crawling with Burning Blade cultists who bring ruin and chaos to the local wildlife and land. Directing the cultist activity within the ridge is Fizzle Darkstorm, an opportunistic goblin warlock allied with the Burning Blade. Rather than serving commerce or cartel interests, Fizzle wields fel power directly in service of the cult's subversive agenda. Slaying him and claiming his twisted claw proves to Orgnil that the cult's immediate leadership in the ravine has been broken.

quest:808.text: Minshina's Skull. Master Gadrin of Sen'jin Village is haunted by the desperate cries of his deceased brother, Minshina. Slain and subjected to dark magic by the rogue witch doctor Zalazane on the Echo Isles, Minshina's soul remains bound inside his own severed skull. Freeing the fallen troll requires infiltrating Zalazane's ritual grounds to reclaim the relic and release his spirit from eternal torment. Master Gadrin serves as one of the Darkspear tribe's spiritual anchors in Sen'jin Village, but his mind is tormented by dark visions. His brother Minshina fell victim to Zalazane's betrayal when the mad warlock seized control of the Echo Isles. Minshina perished during the conflict, but in troll tradition and voodoo mysticism, physical death does not always grant peace. Minshina's tormented voice speaks into Gadrin's dreams, pleading for salvation from a fate worse than death. Zalazane does not simply kill his former brethren; he ensnares their souls to fuel his dark sorcery. Minshina's essence was ritually bound to his own skull, which now rests amidst a blasphemous circle of power on the largest of the Echo Isles. Guarded by hexed trolls and bathed in candlelit ritual, the skull serves as a focal point for the traitor's twisted mojo. So long as it sits within the circle, Minshina remains an eternal captive to Zalazane's will.

quest:809.text: Ak'Zeloth. Ak'Zeloth is an early Horde quest dispatched by the warlock Neeru Fireblade from deep within Orgrimmar's Cleft of Shadow. Driven by evidence of lingering demonic corruption, Neeru sends adventurers into the Barrens to rendezvous with his field contact stationed near the border. Following the discovery of a Burning Blade insignia collar in Durotar, Neeru Fireblade claims to hunt down demonic remnants threatening the newly settled Horde. Presenting himself as a watchdog against fel taint, Neeru directs adventurers toward the arid plains of the Barrens, warning that a dark cult is gathering around an artifact of vile power known as the Demon Seed.

quest:812.text: Need for a Cure. Stranded along the rugged cliffs of northwestern Durotar, the Darkspear troll Rhinag lies poisoned by a venomtail scorpid. With precious little time before the toxin finishes him, he relies on a courier to sprint to Orgrimmar and retrieve a cure from Kor'ghan. The arid canyons of Durotar are crawling with venomtail scorpids, aggressive predators whose sting carries a swift, debilitating neurotoxin. Rhinag made the mistake of dropping his guard while battling the beasts near the borderlands. Knowing that the venom coursing through his veins will kill him in under an hour, he is unable to walk the distance to the city gates himself and must place his survival in the hands of whoever passes his remote camp. Rather than trusting an ordinary apothecary or shaman, Rhinag directs travelers deep beneath Orgrimmar into the shadowy subterranean caverns of the Cleft of Shadow. There dwells Kor'ghan, an enigmatic practitioner familiar with the harsh poisons of Durotar's wastes. Kor'ghan possesses the knowledge required to brew an effective counter-agent, though he rarely gives his aid freely to those who have not proven their mettle.

quest:813.text: Finding the Antidote. Finding the Antidote is an urgent task undertaken for Kor'ghan in Orgrimmar to brew a cure for the poisoned hunter Rhinag. Facing a strict deadline before the venom proves fatal, an adventurer must gather venomtail poison sacs from scorpids outside the city walls. It highlights the unforgiving nature of Durotar's wildlife and the necessity of wilderness preparation. While hunting throughout Durotar, a Darkspear troll named Rhinag made the perilous mistake of engaging native venomtail scorpids without bringing along an antidote. Stung and succumbing rapidly to their potent toxins, he was forced to send for immediate aid. The task falls to Kor'ghan, an experienced hunter residing in Orgrimmar, to mix a restorative draught before the poison finishes its work. Creating an antidote requires harvesting the source of the affliction itself: the venom sacs of mature venomtails lurking outside the gates of Orgrimmar. Kor'ghan notes that chastising Rhinag for his lack of preparation must wait, as every moment counts. Once the sacs are quickly retrieved and brought back into the city, Kor'ghan synthesizes the draught so it can be rushed straight to the dying hunter.

quest:816.text: Lost But Not Forgotten. Lost But Not Forgotten is a somber quest given by Misha Tor'kren at her homestead northwest of Razor Hill. Desperate for closure, she asks travelers to search the dangerous banks of the Southfury River for any trace of her headstrong son, Kron. Northwest of Razor Hill, tucked away in the arid red wastes of Durotar, sits the humble Tor'kren farmstead. Here lives Misha Tor'kren, an orc mother paralyzed by sorrow and anxiety. Days earlier, her son Kron declared he was heading west toward the Southfury River on the border of the Barrens to hunt the river's ferocious crocolisks. Despite her warnings about the deadly beasts, Kron's stubborn pride drove him to storm off to prove his mettle. He has not been seen since.

quest:817.text: Practical Prey. Practical Prey is a hunting task given by the leatherworker Vel'rin Fang in Sen'jin Village. Facing a growing population and dwindling stockpiles, the Darkspear tribe must harvest durable tiger hides from the neighboring Echo Isles to craft essential shelters, clothing, and gear. Life along the arid coast of Durotar is harsh, and the Darkspear trolls exiled to Sen'jin Village must make full use of every resource. Tiger pelts are among the most versatile materials available, essential for stitching together tents, heavy blankets, and reinforced armor. As the settlement swells with refugees and returning scouts, stockpiles have worn thin, compelling craftspeople like Vel'rin Fang to commission new hunts. The Darkspear maintain a deliberate relationship with the predators of their territory. Rather than overhunting the native Durotar tigers, the trolls generally allow the prowlers to thrive unmolested, culling them only when tribal stores require replenishment. Venturing across the water to the Echo Isles to stalk these predators serves both practical necessity and a traditional test of patience, discipline, and wilderness skill.

quest:818.text: A Solvent Spirit. Master Vornal of Sen'jin Village tests fledgling adventurers by demanding reagents to compensate for his failing eyesight. He sends prospective pupils to harvest makrura eyes and crawler mucus along the coast of Durotar. While he scoffs at the idea of taking an apprentice, the task serves as a deliberate trial of patience and resolve. Master Vornal sits in Sen'jin Village, burdened by age and diminishing vision. Where primal magic once flowed naturally to his fingertips, he now leans heavily on alchemy to sharpen his perceptions and weave his arts. Despite his mounting physical decline, the stubborn troll refuses to take on an apprentice, claiming neither the Darkspear nor the orcs of Durotar have produced anyone worthy of his tutelage. Rather than straightforward instruction, Vornal demands raw materials from the harsh coastline: intact makrura eyes and vials of crawler mucus. Sourcing undamaged eyes from the armored, snapping makrura requires delicate strikes, while gathering sufficient mucus tests an adventurer's willingness to endure tedious, menial work. To Vornal, hunting these littoral beasts is less about the reagents and more about weeding out those who lack focus. For Master Vornal, time and patience are the ultimate measures of strength. He expects brash youths to give in to frustration or abandon the chore entirely. Returning to Sen'jin Village with pristine ingredients demonstrates not only survival skills along the dangerous reefs of the Echo Isles channel, but the discipline necessary to master the subtle arts of alchemy.

quest:819.text: Chen's Empty Keg. Discarded in the wilds of the Barrens lies an empty keg bearing the inscription of Chen Stormstout. Finding it begins a journey into the past deeds of the famed wandering brewmaster who once lent his fighting skills to the founding of Durotar. Scattered across the arid expanses of the Barrens, travelers occasionally stumble upon an abandoned wooden barrel. Unlike the common casks left behind by Razormane quilboar or Kolkar centaur, this barrel features careful craftsmanship and a distinct inscribed plaque: 'Chen Stormstout - May your spirit be raised and always raise your spirits.' It is an unusual relic to find baking beneath the Kalimdor sun, prompting anyone curious enough to seek out someone knowledgeable in brewing to understand how it got there. Taking the vessel to Brewmaster Drohn in Ratchet reveals its origins. Drohn recognizes the craftsmanship instantly: it belonged to Chen Stormstout, the legendary Pandaren wanderer who journeyed alongside Rexxar during the critical battles that secured Durotar for Thrall's Horde. Though years have passed since Chen walked the red earth of Kalimdor, his legendary brew recipes and wandering spirit remain vivid memories among the realm's seasoned brewers.

quest:823.text: Report to Orgnil. Report to Orgnil is an early Horde quest dispatched by Master Gadrin from Sen'jin Village. It directs fledgling adventurers northward to Razor Hill to warn Orgnil Soulscar about the insidious reach of the Burning Blade cult. This dispatch helps coordinate Durotar's scattered defense against demonic corruption brewing right in the orcs' homeland. While Sen'jin Village grapples with its own local woes—most notably Zalazane's treachery on the Echo Isles—Master Gadrin recognizes that reports of the Burning Blade cult represent a far wider danger. Whispers of demonic corruption were uncovered in the Valley of Trials, and the Darkspear witch doctor knows these threats cannot be handled in isolation. He dispatches traveling heroes north along the dusty road to Razor Hill, where the local orc authorities maintain a broader watch over Durotar. Stationed in the military encampment of Razor Hill, Orgnil Soulscar is an orc charged with rooting out domestic evils and safeguarding the central heartlands. When adventurers deliver Gadrin's warning, Orgnil wastes no time integrating the reports from both the Valley of Trials and Sen'jin Village. Recognizing that the shadow of the Burning Blade looms dangerously close, he quickly mobilizes forces to dismantle the cultists before their dark rituals can unseat the young nation.

quest:825.text: From The Wreckage..... Gar'Thok of Razor Hill directs Horde scouts to scavenge the sunken remains of Grand Admiral Proudmoore's fleet off the Scuttle Coast. By recovering advanced Gnomish Tools from the watery wreckage, the Horde hopes to dissect Alliance engineering and turn that technological advantage to its own benefit. When Grand Admiral Daelin Proudmoore brought the naval might of Kul Tiras to Kalimdor, his vessels choked the shoreline near Tiragarde Keep. Following his defeat, shattered hulls settled along the Scuttle Coast. While the surviving Kul Tiran soldiers fortify the keep itself, the remnants of their armada lie broken on the shoals, slowly rotting beneath the tide. Orcish warfare traditionally relies on raw strength, iron, and blood, but the Horde recognizes the dangerous edge provided by Alliance ingenuity. Gnomish technicians accompanied the expeditionary fleets, outfitting the Alliance vessels with complex machinery and precision gear. Gar'Thok seeks to recover these submerged tools so the Horde can unravel the mechanics behind them. The salvaged tools are not meant to remain gathering dust in Razor Hill. Gar'Thok arranges for them to be transported by caravan directly to Orgrimmar. By reverse-engineering gnomish instruments, Horde craftspeople and tacticians aim to better counter Alliance devices in coming conflicts while bolstering their own emerging industries.

quest:826.text: Zalazane. Master Gadrin of Sen'jin Village tasks Horde champions with traveling to the Echo Isles to end the treachery of the witch doctor Zalazane. Driven mad by dark magic, Zalazane enslaved his fellow tribesmen and seized the Darkspear trolls' rightful home, forcing them into exile on Durotar's coast. When the Darkspear tribe fled their sunken island home and followed Thrall across the Great Sea, they established a settlement on the Echo Isles just off Durotar's southeast coast. Zalazane, a respected and potent witch doctor of the tribe, fell prey to a lust for power. Harnessing mind-enslaving hexes, he subjugated many of his kin and launched a violent uprising. The remaining free Darkspear, led by Vol'jin, were driven from their ancestral camps across the water, forced to build a temporary refuge at Sen'jin Village. Zalazane was not content merely driving the tribe away. From his hilltop redoubt on the largest Echo Isle, he regularly sends raiding parties across the channel to snatch more Darkspear and drag them into his thrall. Those afflicted become mindless voodoo and hexed thralls, utterly lost to the tribe. Master Gadrin views this not merely as an occupation of land, but as an existential threat: until Zalazane's severed head is brought before the elders, no Darkspear can ever truly be safe.

quest:827.text: Skull Rock. Assigned by the hermit Margoz, this task directs Horde adventurers into the cavern of Skull Rock just east of Orgrimmar. The cave has been overrun by the Burning Blade cult, who use painful demonic devices to bind themselves to dark magic. Securing these cursed artifacts allows Margoz to study the cult's presence right on the capital's doorstep. Skull Rock is a forbidding cave nestled in the craggy hills of northeastern Durotar. While seemingly isolated, it sits distressingly close to the mighty gates of Orgrimmar. Rather than housing wild beasts or mere outlaws, the caverns harbor a cell of the Burning Blade—the shadowy demonic cult that has long plagued orcish society. Within these dim tunnels, cultists conduct unholy rituals under the nose of the Warchief's scouts. The cultists operating within Skull Rock wear Searing Collars, torcs designed to scorch and brand their own flesh. According to Margoz, this self-inflicted torment is far from mindless cruelty; the searing agony and fel sorcery embedded in the metal serve to attune the wearers to demonic power. By recovering these artifacts, Margoz intends to unravel the exact spells and bindings empowering the Burning Blade's ranks.

quest:828.text: Margoz. Margoz is a Horde quest tasking adventurers with seeking out an isolated orc shaman who watches over the northern reaches of Durotar. Following the confrontation with fel corruption in the canyon, Orgnil Soulscar directs champions to consult Margoz before assaulting a nearby cultist stronghold. The wise hermit provides crucial counsel regarding the growing shadow cast by the Burning Blade. After discovering the depths of fel taint at Thunder Ridge, Orgnil Soulscar recognizes that brute strength alone will not suffice to cleanse Durotar. He directs his champions toward Margoz, an experienced orc shaman who keeps a lonely camp in the crags northeast of Razor Hill.
