Positioned between the jagged heights of Drygulch Ravine and the eastern sea, Margoz keeps watch over dark omens that the bustling warriors of Orgrimmar often overlook. Margoz possesses crucial intelligence regarding the Burning Blade's true power base in northern Durotar: a concealed cavern system known as Skull Rock, carved directly into the mountain cliffs outside Orgrimmar's southern gates. By conferring with Margoz, travelers learn that the cultists operate far closer to Thrall's capital than the Warchief's guards realize. The shaman ensures that anyone sent to purge the coven does not walk blindly into demonic ambush.

quest:829.text: Neeru Fireblade. This quest sends Horde adventurers from Margoz in Durotar to Orgrimmar's shadowy underbelly. Entrusted with a demonic Searing Collar recovered from the Burning Blade cult, you are directed to Neeru Fireblade, a prominent warlock residing in the Cleft of Shadow who claims to study dark arts only to protect the Horde. After recovering Searing Collars from the cultists lurking in Skull Rock, the shaman Margoz discovers that unraveling their foul sorcery exceeds his ancestral arts. Shamans commune with elemental spirits and the earth, while these artifacts reek of raw demonic corruption. Recognizing that understanding the Burning Blade's devices requires someone well-versed in the occult, Margoz sends you to seek out a warlock residing in the capital. Beneath the red cliffs of Orgrimmar lies the Cleft of Shadow, a dimly lit cavern where practitioners of forbidden magics ply their trade under Thrall's wary eye. There dwells Neeru Fireblade, an influential orc warlock who insists his mastery of fel power is aimed entirely at thwarting demonic threats. Handing him the example collar draws his immediate curiosity, bringing Durotar's cult investigation straight into the heart of the warlock enclave.

quest:83.text: Red Linen Goods. Red Linen Goods is an Elwynn Forest task offered by seamstress Sara Timberlain at the Eastvale Logging Camp. In need of fabric, she asks passing adventurers to hunt down local Defias bandits and strip them of their linen bandanas. In exchange, she uses the reclaimed cloth to tailor useful goods for travelers. While the low-level Defias brigands skirmishing in Northshire Valley make do with cheap burlap masks, the organized outlaws prowling greater Elwynn Forest sport finer crimson linen bandanas. To local craftsmen short on raw materials, these gang identifiers represent a surprisingly practical supply of usable cloth. Operating out of the bustling Eastvale Logging Camp near the eastern border of Elwynn, Sara Timberlain is always on the lookout for workable textiles. By encouraging adventurers to thin out the Defias encampments hidden across the woods, she keeps her tailoring trade supplied while helping to curb the Brotherhood's brazen encroachment.

quest:830.text: The Admiral's Orders. Recovered from a locked strongbox atop Tiragarde Keep, these weathered papers bear the personal seal of the late Grand Admiral Daelin Proudmoore. The recovered orders reveal that the Kul Tiran human garrison along Durotar's coast is far more entrenched and organized than simple shipwreck survivors. Delivering them to Gar'Thok in Razor Hill exposes lingering military plans threatening the fledgling Orc nation. Hidden inside a heavy chest on the upper floors of Tiragarde Keep, an aged envelope survives under the watch of Lieutenant Benedict. Sealed with the crest of Grand Admiral Daelin Proudmoore, the parchment outlines direct naval commands issued during Kul Tiras's bloody invasion of Durotar. Even after the Grand Admiral fell at Theramore, his officers maintained their fortifications, clinging tightly to their mission to eradicate the Horde settlement.

quest:832.text: Burning Shadows. Recovered from the Burning Blade cultist Gazz'uz in the depths of Skull Rock, this mysterious glowing pendant whispers urgent warnings into the bearer's mind. The voice specifically threatens Gazz'uz with the wrath of Neeru Fireblade, an orc warlock residing in Orgrimmar. Upon slaying Gazz'uz deep within Skull Rock, an ominous pendant known as the Eye of Burning Shadow is retrieved from his remains. Rather than being an inert magical trinket, the stone vibrates with psychic communication. A demanding voice speaks directly into the mind of anyone holding it, demanding reports from Gazz'uz and warning him that his clandestine operations east of Orgrimmar have been compromised.

quest:835.text: Securing the Lines. Securing the Lines is a task given by Rezlak near Razorwind Canyon to protect vital goblin supply routes running through Durotar. Harpies roosting in Drygulch Ravine continuously intercept and plunder supply caravans, prompting the frustrated goblin to hire muscle to clear them out. The dry valleys of Durotar are harsh enough without aggressive harpies swooping down on unsuspecting travelers. Operating on behalf of his boss Gazlowe, the goblin Rezlak watches over regional supply operations. Unfortunately, the Dustwind harpies inhabiting Drygulch Ravine have turned Razorwind Canyon into a hazard, routinely raiding caravans and seizing incoming shipments before they can reach their destinations. Rezlak lives by the goblin maxim that you can get anything done if the price is right. Rather than personally entering the canyon, he hires adventurers to break the back of the roost by eliminating Dustwind Savages and Dustwind Storm Witches. Clearing these harpies keeps the trade corridors open, secures incoming shipments of engineering gadgets, and points helpful travelers toward greater opportunities in Ratchet.

quest:840.text: Conscript of the Horde. Conscript of the Horde is an introductory transition quest that directs young Horde adventurers out of Durotar and into the vast wilderness of the Barrens. Initiated by the scout Takrin Pathseeker along the western road from Razor Hill, it sends recruits across the Southfury River to Kargal Battlescar's border outpost. Once an aspiring Horde soldier proves their strength around Razor Hill, the needs of the wider nation call them westward. Takrin Pathseeker keeps watch along the dirt highway leaving Durotar, evaluating travelers on behalf of his friend, veteran Kargal Battlescar. Taking Takrin's recruitment letter marks a recruit's first formal assignment beyond the orcs' new homeland of Durotar. The border outpost across the bridge spans the divide between Durotar's red canyons and the arid expanse of the Barrens. Kargal Battlescar is charged with mustering recruits to hold the frontiers, though border guard duty is only the beginning. With centaur, quilboar, and Alliance expeditions probing the frontier, raw manpower is urgently redirected toward the settlement of the Crossroads.

quest:842.text: Crossroads Conscription. Crossroads Conscription directs newly enlisted Horde recruits from the border outpost into the heart of the Barrens. Carrying a signed letter from Kargal Battlescar, adventurers report directly to Sergra Darkthorn at the vital strategic hub known as the Crossroads. After proving their worth to Kargal Battlescar at the Far Watch Post on the border of Durotar, recruits are handed a signed recruitment letter and sent west. The journey follows the packed dirt road through the arid brush of the Barrens until reaching the central junction. At this sun-baked intersection sits the Crossroads, the Horde's vital logistical hub linking northern Kalimdor to the southern wilderness. Awaiting new arrivals is Sergra Darkthorn, a sharp-tongued orc shaman handpicked by Warchief Thrall to oversee operations at the Crossroads. Despite grumbling from seasoned veterans like Kargal Battlescar—who considers her difficult and overly talkative—Thrall holds Sergra in high esteem. Fierce and unyielding, she is quick to remind recruits, particularly arrogant men, that under Thrall's Horde, female warriors and leaders stand on completely equal ground and will tolerate no insolence.

quest:844.text: Plainstrider Menace. Plainstrider Menace is an introductory hunting task assigned by Sergra Darkthorn at the Crossroads. Newly arrived Horde adventurers are directed to cull the native plainstriders scavenging the settlement's supply routes, serving both as pest control and as an initial test of hunting prowess. The Crossroads sits at the logistical heart of Kalimdor, coordinating supply caravans across the harsh savanna. However, the arid terrain leaves local wildlife desperate for sustenance. Flocks of tall, flightless plainstriders roaming just east of the outpost have taken to picking at food crates and disrupting the settlement's lifeline. To protect these vulnerable provisions, the shaman Sergra Darkthorn dispatches travelers to cull the aggressive birds before they inflict serious damage on the outpost's stores. While pest management is an immediate practical goal, Sergra views the plainstriders as a measuring stick for newcomers. She considers the birds simple prey—easy game intended to teach young hunters how to survive the elements and track quarry in the sun-baked plains. Bringing back their sharp beaks proves that a hunter has the patience and basic martial skill required to face the fiercer beasts native to the Barrens.

quest:845.text: The Zhevra. The Zhevra is an early hunting trial issued by Sergra Darkthorn at the Crossroads. As part of a progressing test of martial prowess across the savannas of the Barrens, young hunters are charged with tracking down swift zhevra runners and taking their powerful hooves. Following an initial cull of the Barrens' overgrown plainstriders, Sergra Darkthorn directs fledgling Horde warriors toward slightly more formidable game. The striped zhevras roam in herds across the northern and southern plains. While not the apex predators of the savanna, they are fleet-footed herd beasts known for their stubborn endurance and powerful, bone-cracking kicks. To Sergra, this hunt is less about securing trade goods and more about testing an adventurer's developing edge. She demands four intact hooves as physical proof of the kill, warning that the beast's rear kick has enough force to drop a grown tauren onto its haunches. Proving oneself against these fleet runners earns a hunter entry into even deadlier trials against the predatory prowlers of the plains.

quest:853.text: Apothecary Zamah. This errand sends an adventurer racing from the arid Barrens to Thunder Bluff carrying a volatile, rendered fungal emulsion. Apothecary Helbrim needs the potent mixture delivered swiftly to his colleague, Apothecary Zamah, tucked away in the shadowy depths beneath Spirit Rise. After studying the peculiar fungal blooms thriving across the oases of the Barrens, Apothecary Helbrim cooks down a batch into a delicate emulsion. The unstable brew degrades rapidly once prepared. Lacking the time to travel to Mulgore himself, Helbrim entrusts the flask to a reliable runner to make the climb up the bluffs before the solution loses its chemical potency. Apothecary Zamah maintains her laboratory far from the open plains of Mulgore, sequestered inside the Pools of Vision. This subterranean cavern rests deep beneath the sacred heights of Spirit Rise, shared with Forsaken mages and priests. Here, beneath the floor of the tauren sanctuary, the Royal Apothecary Society quietly conducts its research using raw materials gathered throughout the continent.

quest:854.text: Journey to the Crossroads. Journey to the Crossroads is a pivotal rite of passage for young Horde adventurers leaving the peaceful meadows of Mulgore behind. Directed by the tauren mystic Kirge Sternhorn at Camp Taurajo, travelers are sent north to the Crossroads to aid the orcish overseer Thork. It marks the moment a novice steps onto the wider stage of Kalimdor's frontier. For many tauren leaving their homeland of Mulgore, Camp Taurajo is their first real taste of the harsh, windswept plains of the Barrens. Just past the mountain pass from Mulgore, mystic Kirge Sternhorn watches over travelers making their descent into these dry grasslands. Sensing their growing capability, Sternhorn directs promising champions to journey further north along the dusty trade route rather than lingering on the fringe. The quest underscores the vital bond forged between the tauren of Thunder Bluff and Thrall's new Horde. Kirge notes that the fates of both peoples are now intertwined, and the orcs battling to carve out an outpost at the Crossroads desperately need reinforcements. Upon reaching the outpost, Thork warmly welcomes travelers coming from as far as the high bluffs, eager to put their strength to the test against the perils of the savanna.

quest:855.text: Centaur Bracers. Centaur Bracers is a military bounty offered by Regthar Deathgate west of the Crossroads. It tasks Horde champions with thinning the aggressive Kolkar centaur ranks contesting control of the central Barrens. The fledgling Horde is engaged in a broad struggle to carve out safe territory across Kalimdor, and the Barrens serve as the vital crossroads between Durotar and Mulgore. However, violent nomadic tribes of Kolkar centaur contest every watering hole and plain, attacking supply trains and scouting parties. From his bunker west of the Crossroads, the orc warrior Regthar Deathgate coordinates defensive efforts to stem their relentless advances. Rather than relying on empty reports, Regthar demands tangible proof of action against the horse-tribes. Soldiers venturing into Kolkar territory are tasked with returning with severed bracers taken directly from slain centaur warriors. This grim accounting serves both as verification for Horde bounties and as a calculated message intended to intimidate surviving Kolkar raiders.

quest:8569.text: Past Efforts in Warsong Gulch. Past Efforts in Warsong Gulch is a military commendation turned in to capital city officers in recognition of service on the front lines. Rather than celebrating outright conquest, it honors veterans who offered valiant struggle and sacrifice amidst the contested woods of Ashenvale. City commanders accept these tokens to sustain war morale and reward dedication across both factions. War between the Silverwing Sentinels and the Warsong Outriders rarely yields clean or effortless victories. Across the southern borders of Ashenvale, skirmishes are brutal, bloody, and often end without decisive triumph. Recognizing that morale cannot hinge entirely on unblemished success, commanders in Stormwind, Orgrimmar, and other capitals instituted honors for steadfast service. The Ribbon of Sacrifice commemorates those who threw themselves into the fray regardless of the odds. Capital officials such as the Alliance Brigadier Generals and Horde Warbringers manage mobilization far behind the front lines. While recruiters direct new blood toward battlefields like Warsong Gulch, quartermasters and tacticians must account for returning fighters who endured grueling campaigns. By acknowledging individual courage and sacrifices in stalemate or defeat, leadership ensures that frontline soldiers remain committed to holding Ashenvale.

quest:860.text: Sergra Darkthorn. Having proven their basic tracking and stalking skills in the rolling hills of Mulgore, young tauren are directed outward into the arid wilderness of the Barrens. Melor Stonehoof sends aspiring hunters north of the border to report to Sergra Darkthorn at the Crossroads. This journey marks the hunter's formal transition from local trials to the demanding predatory hierarchy of Kalimdor's broader plains. For a novice tauren hunter, completing initial rites in Mulgore is only the beginning. The lush valleys of their ancestral homeland are protected and familiar, nurturing beasts that test patience rather than sheer survival. Melor Stonehoof recognizes when a hunter's spirit has grown enough to require harsher trials. He instructs his pupils to pack their gear, leave the safety of Bloodhoof Village, and venture east across the mountain pass into the baked scrublands of the Barrens. The path through the red rock canyons leads straight into the wide, sun-scorched savanna where the young Horde stakes its claim. At the intersection of Kalimdor's central trade routes lies the Crossroads, a fortified settlement bustling with orcs, trolls, and tauren. There waits Sergra Darkthorn, an experienced orc shaman renowned for her unforgiving standards. She acts as a mentor to any bold enough to stalk the Barrens' fierce fauna, promising to temper raw eagerness into hardened wilderness discipline.

quest:861.text: The Hunter's Way. The Hunter's Way is a rite of passage offered to aspiring trackers in Mulgore by the elder Skorn Whitecloud. To prove their emerging skill and respect for the wild, wanderers must fell the cunning flatland prowlers and present their claws to Melor Stonehoof atop Thunder Bluff's Hunter Rise. For the tauren, hunting is neither mere sport nor simple subsistence; it is considered one of their people's highest honors. It demands patience, awareness of the Earth Mother's balance, and reverence for the beasts that roam the rolling plains. Elder Skorn Whitecloud, resting in Mulgore after decades of tracking across Kalimdor, recognizes this restlessness in young adventurers. Rather than allowing them to wander aimlessly, he channels their ambition into a traditional trial of maturity and discipline. To demonstrate that their tracking instincts are genuine, candidates are tasked with taking down Mulgore's flatland prowlers. These great cats are swift, stealthy, and cunning ambush predators that blend easily into the high grass of the plains. Gathering four sets of claws proves that a fledgling wanderer can spot a predator before becoming prey, turning the hunter's own ferocity back upon them. Upon securing the trophies, the initiate ascends the soaring wooden towers and bridges leading up to Thunder Bluff. There, upon the Hunter Rise, Melor Stonehoof receives the claws. As a master tracker who values Skorn Whitecloud's ancient wisdom, Stonehoof accepts the offering as proof that the initiate possesses the right spirit to be guided further along the predatory paths of Kalimdor.

quest:867.text: Harpy Raiders. Harpy Raiders is an early offensive task given by Darsok Swiftdagger at the Crossroads to curb the aggressive Witchwing flock. Tasked with hunting down baseline raiders and roguefeathers in the northwestern Barrens, adventurers harvest talons to cripple the flock's supply raids. Caravans crawling across the dusty trails of the Barrens face constant harassment from wild beasts and quilboar, but the Witchwing harpies pose a particularly deadly aerial nuisance. Striking from the rocky crags in the northwest, these feral creatures routinely sweep down upon merchant trains and supply wagons, slaughtering pack animals and pillaging critical goods bound for orcish outposts. Rather than launching a haphazard assault against the mountainous roosts, the orc rogue Darsok Swiftdagger has spent days scouting the flock's habits and hierarchy. He knows that an uncoordinated strike will scatter them into the winds. To decisively break the Witchwing, Darsok intends to systematically butcher the flock from the bottom rank up, beginning with the front-line raiders before moving against their commanders.

quest:86784.text: Sticks and Bones. Sticks and Bones is a local task offered by Deathguard Bartholomew in Tirisfal Glades. He sends travelers to gather dry branches across the blighted woodland to deliver to Eleanor Shackleton, an experienced survivalist camped in the western hills. While Deathguards in Tirisfal Glades are usually consumed by military patrol duty and guarding against the Scourge or Scarlet crusaders, Deathguard Bartholomew takes a moment to look out for an acquaintance. Knowing that Eleanor Shackleton spends her unlife out in the harsh elements, he encourages passing adventurers to collect dry branches for her camp fire. Eleanor Shackleton prides herself on surviving the blighted wilderness of Tirisfal alone. Despite being undead, the Forsaken still feel the damp, bitter chill that rolls off the northern moors. Eleanor's philosophy on wood gathering is simple: whenever you think you have collected enough firewood, collect five times more. Grateful for the extra timber, she lets the courier keep Bartholomew's basket and shares the warmth of her fire.

quest:869.text: Raptor Thieves. When a vital shipment of guard payroll went missing from the Crossroads guard tower, the defenders caught an impossible culprit: a wild raptor. Perplexed and enraged by the heist, Gazrog orders a retaliatory cull to prevent the cunning beasts from striking again. The Crossroads relies heavily on mercenary and grunt guards to keep vital trade arteries open across the Barrens. Keeping those guards paid is essential for morale and discipline. When the silver payroll vanished directly from the guard tower, leadership expected Centaur raiders or Quilboar scavengers. Instead, one thief caught red-handed in the dead of night was a predatory Barrens raptor, leaving the settlement's leadership stunned and out of pocket. Gazrog makes no pretense of understanding why wild beasts would hoard shiny coins, nor does he care to study animal behavior. With the guards growing restless over their missing pay, Gazrog demands blood and deterrence. By sending hunters to harvest a dozen raptor heads across the savannah, he aims to break the predators' boldness before launching a full recovery effort for the silver.

quest:870.text: The Forgotten Pools. Tonga Runetotem at the Crossroads sends Horde adventurers to inspect the Forgotten Pools, an oasis northwest of the settlement. The Cenarion Circle suspects that unseen subterranean energies are causing verdant life to surge through the arid savannah. Long ago, the Barrens flourished as a fertile, vibrant land before ages of war and Sundering shattered the continent, reducing the region to sun-baked scrubland. Yet recently, lush oases have miraculously begun to take root in the dry basin. To the druids of the Cenarion Circle, this sudden bloom is unnatural. Rather than ordinary springs, they sense subterranean powers pressing upward through the earth, coaxing vegetation and wildlife to life in anomalous pockets across the wastes.

quest:871.text: Disrupt the Attacks. Disrupt the Attacks is an early defensive assignment issued by Thork at the Crossroads in the Barrens. The aggressive Razormane quilboar have severed supply routes connecting Durotar to the outpost, threatening the settlement's survival. Horde adventurers are dispatched to thin out the quilboar forces while scouts attempt to locate their warband's leader. The Crossroads serves as the vital junction for all Horde traffic moving through central Kalimdor. Its survival relies entirely on freight wagons and caravans hauling food, iron, and equipment west from Durotar. When the Razormane tribe set up aggressive ambushes along the northeast trails, these essential deliveries ground to an abrupt halt. With resources dwindling and defensive stores running low, Thork cannot afford to wait for peaceable negotiations. Rather than waiting for the quilboar to launch a direct assault against the town walls, Thork orders proactive strikes against their bramble dens northeast of the settlement. Striking at their Water Seekers, Thornweavers, and Hunters weakens their scouting perimeter and deprives their raiding parties of magical and logistical support. These initial skirmishes buy crucial time while Horde trackers comb the brush to discover who is organizing the raids.

quest:88.text: Princess Must Die!. Princess Must Die! is a local bounty offered by Ma Stonefield at the Stonefield Farm in southern Elwynn Forest. She seeks an end to Princess, an enormous prize-winning sow from the nearby Brackwell Pumpkin Patch that continually raids her prized vegetable patches. Putting down the rampaging pig ensures the Stonefields can harvest their crops in peace. The Stonefield Farm relies heavily on its crops, but a voracious threat has jeopardized their harvest. Princess, a celebrated prize-winning sow belonging to the Brackwells, has grown to monstrous proportions by trespassing onto the Stonefield plots and devouring their vegetables. Ma Stonefield has had enough of the brazen pig feasting on her hard work and wants the beast put down before she ruins the entire season's yield. Princess rarely roams without company. Over at the Brackwell Pumpkin Patch, situated to the east beyond the Maclure homestead, she stays surrounded by her loyal entourage of protective boars. Slaying this massive sow requires cutting through her guards and stripping the distinctive brass collar from her neck to prove the gluttonous beast will trouble the Stonefield fields no more.

quest:886.text: The Barrens Oases. High on the Elder Rise of Thunder Bluff, Arch Druid Hamuul Runetotem senses an unsettling surge of power flowing into the arid soils of the Barrens. To uncover the truth, he dispatches promising travelers eastward past Mulgore's gates to rendezvous with his kinsman, Tonga Runetotem, at the Crossroads. This mission marks the beginning of an investigation into the unnatural waters springing up across the sun-baked plains. While the plains of Mulgore flourish under the watchful gaze of the Earth Mother, the vast savannas of the Barrens to the east have remained harsh, scorched, and dry for generations. Recently, however, the tauren druids meditating atop Thunder Bluff's Elder Rise have detected strange currents of energy waking deep beneath the parched plains. Life is stirring where it ought not to be, and the Cenarion Circle fears that whatever force is causing this surge may harbor hidden peril for the land and its creatures. To investigate these strange occurrences, Arch Druid Hamuul Runetotem dispatched Tonga Runetotem into the field. Recognizing that the vast wilderness holds dangers too great for one investigator alone, Hamuul enlists travelers leaving Mulgore to hasten after Tonga. Following the road east past Bloodhoof Village and through the mountain passes leads straight to the Crossroads—the dusty, bustling heart of Horde territory in the Barrens—where Tonga awaits answers.

quest:887.text: Southsea Freebooters. Southsea Freebooters is an introductory bounty task commissioned by Gazlowe in Ratchet to curtail local piracy. Infuriated by pirate raids on goblin trading vessels, the chief engineer hires adventurers to assault a Southsea pirate encampment along the Merchant Coast just south of town. Ratchet operates as the premier neutral trading port in central Kalimdor, built on the steady traffic of merchant vessels traveling between the eastern continents and Kalimdor. However, the Southsea Freebooters have established a fortified beach camp directly south along the Merchant Coast. From this staging ground, the buccaneers target incoming and outgoing goblin cargo ships, bleeding profits and destabilizing the local shipping lanes. Gazlowe's anger stems not only from the pirates themselves, but from the perceived incompetence of the Steamwheedle Cartel's naval leadership. Despite immense sums invested by the Trade Princes into maintaining defensive fleets, Vice Admiral Grezzlik has failed to police the waters effectively. Frustrated by Undermine's sluggish response, Gazlowe bypasses naval channels and resorts to contracting independent mercenaries to thin out pirate brigands and cannoneers.

quest:890.text: The Missing Shipment. Gazlowe is expecting a delayed shipment of goods sent across the Great Sea from Booty Bay. Suspecting either dockside administrative blunders or the Southsea Freebooters, he dispatches couriers down to the Ratchet piers to cross-examine Wharfmaster Dizzywig's logs. Ratchet thrives as the Steamwheedle Cartel's commercial beachhead on Kalimdor. Ships regularly cross the Great Sea from Booty Bay, carrying manufactured commodities, exotic supplies, and heavy freight needed to fuel the port's rapid construction and trade ventures. When inbound inventory goes missing, it disrupts business for Chief Engineer Gazlowe, who meticulously tracks every crate entering the port. While Southsea Freebooters infest the coastline south of the town and routinely intercept merchant vessels, Gazlowe knows better than to act without checking his own ledgers. Before accusing pirates or dispatching mercenaries into a skirmish, he sends his personal inventory records directly to Wharfmaster Dizzywig down on the docks. Dizzywig oversees the actual offloading and storage of ship cargo, making him the only goblin capable of determining whether the shipment was lost at sea or simply misplaced in a warehouse.

quest:892.text: The Missing Shipment. Following an inquiry at the docks, Wharfmaster Dizzywig returns Gazlowe's ledger with clear records, pointing the finger away from harbor graft and toward the local pirates. Delivering the paperwork back to Gazlowe prompts the goblin boss to plan retaliation against the Southsea Freebooters to recover his lost cargo. Ratchet thrives on trade, but running a bustling port alongside the Barrens brings constant logistical headaches. When an expected cargo shipment goes missing, Gazlowe assumes an error in harbor accounting or foul play on the piers. Upon examining the manifest, Wharfmaster Dizzywig insists his books are clean and the intake records fully accounted for, meaning the missing merchandise never even made it onto the dock.

quest:894.text: Samophlange. Commissioned by the goblin engineer Sputtervalve in Ratchet, this task sends adventurers north into a Venture Company research outpost southwest of the Sludge Fen. Their goal is to locate a mysterious contraption known only as a samophlange. Equipped with a pilfered operating manual, the curious investigator must navigate an erratic control console to extract the device. Goblins are notoriously driven by innovation, curiosity, and profit, but even the Tinker Sputtervalve finds himself perplexed by the latest development coming out of the Venture Company's digs in the northern Barrens. Operating southwest of the Sludge Fen, the rival outfit has been tinkering with a device designated as a samophlange. Without knowing its precise mechanical function or lucrative potential, Sputtervalve is eager to lay his hands on the equipment to reverse-engineer its design before his commercial rivals capitalize on it. Securing the device is no simple task. The Venture Company guards their operations fiercely, surrounding the facility with armed overseers, deforesters, and complex machinery. Sputtervalve provides an intercepted operating manual to assist in shutting down the erratic rig safely. Upon reaching the central control station, an investigator finds a chaotic array of levers, lights, and gauges maintaining optimal pressure across three critical control valves, guarded by a locked console.

quest:900.text: Samophlange. This task requires shutting down the intricate machinery powering the Venture Company's digging operations in the northern Barrens. By cutting off three separate control valves, adventurers can safely power down the central apparatus. Turning off these valves halts the volatile flow of fuel and pressure keeping the machine active. The Venture Company's machinery at the Sludge Fen is as dangerous as it is complex. When confronting the central control console, the dials and indicators make it clear that the core mechanism cannot simply be shut down at the flip of a switch. To prevent an explosion or mechanical failure, the feed lines must be handled manually first. Three distinct valves govern the flow into the rig: the Main Control Valve, the Fuel Control Valve, and the Regulator Valve. Each must be manually sealed against high pressure. As each valve closes, the glowing status indicators on the console fade from green to yellow, finally allowing the central shutoff mechanism to be engaged safely.

quest:901.text: Samophlange. This quest is the critical step in shutting down the Venture Company machinery at the Sludge Fen in the northern Barrens. Having already shut down the surrounding valves, an operative must secure the console key from Tinkerer Sniggles to open the main control unit and extract the mysterious samophlange. Before the core component can be physically extracted, the machinery must be completely unpowered and unlocked. With the auxiliary valves turned and the pressure relieved, the terminal's dials and gauges settle into an idle state. However, the housing itself remains locked tight to prevent sabotage, requiring a physical key held by the lead goblin engineer overseeing the drilling site. The Venture Company relies on Tinkerer Sniggles to oversee the delicate balance of their industrial equipment at the Sludge Fen. Sniggles keeps the console key on his person, residing inside a nearby hut just northeast of the primary rig. Overcoming the engineer is the final obstacle standing between the operative and the samophlange nested inside the chassis.

quest:90902.text: Rediscovering the Light. Offered by Aramis Hammerhand in Deathknell, this task challenges newly raised Forsaken paladins to embrace the Holy Light once more. Calling upon holy powers inflicts intense agony upon undead flesh, requiring fledgling paladins to channel healing into injured Deathguards despite the burning torment. For former champions of the Silver Hand and fallen knights of Lordaeron, awakening in undeath means confronting a horrifying reality: the Holy Light still answers their call, but it burns their withered bodies from within. Aramis Hammerhand instructs newly risen Forsaken paladins that abilities once practiced as second nature now bring excruciating pain. Because holy energy naturally conflicts with the foul magic sustaining undeath, channeling the Light requires raw willpower and agonizing perseverance. Rather than allowing this torment to deter them, Forsaken paladins view the pain as an enduring testament of faith. Deathguard throughout Deathknell suffer grievous wounds combating mindless zombies, and it falls upon these undead knights to restore them. Aramis teaches that pushing through the burning pain is like exercising an atrophied muscle—the agony itself is treated as a badge of honor and living proof that the Light has not forsaken them.

quest:91208.text: Coming to Terms. Offered by Aramis Hammerhand in Deathknell, this quest tasks newly risen paladins with reaching out to a fellow knight struggling to accept undeath. Fleeing into the hills in terror, the newly returned warrior faces the agonizing realization of becoming what she once fought against. Awakening from death into the ranks of the Forsaken is jarring for anyone, but for former paladins of the Silver Hand, the shock is visceral. Having dedicated their mortal lives to destroying the undead in service to the Holy Light, these individuals suddenly find their souls tethered back to decomposing flesh. While some adapt under the guidance of Aramis Hammerhand, others are overwhelmed by horror and confusion, fleeing into the Tirisfal wilderness rather than confronting their grim new existence.

quest:91209.text: Continue Your Training. This quest directs newly risen Forsaken paladins to leave Deathknell and travel to Brill for advanced instruction. Entrusted by Aramis Hammerhand, the journey introduces the fledgling holy warrior to the wider perils of Tirisfal Glades. It also serves as a stark warning about the deep suspicion that holy practitioners face among the undead. Once a newly awakened soul has mastered the rudiments of martial combat and channelled holy power within Deathknell's cloistered graveyard, Aramis Hammerhand sends them east into the broader expanse of Tirisfal Glades. Their destination is Brill, a bustling regional outpost serving as the administrative hub for central Tirisfal. There, Shari Stilwell oversees the advancement of those who dare walk the path of the paladin in undeath. Aramis offers parting advice that underlines the fraught reality of being an undead paladin. While Lordaeron still requires defenders against external threats, wielding the Holy Light under Sylvanas Windrunner's banner draws bitter suspicion. Countless Forsaken suffered agony or death at the hands of holy zealots, and the mere presence of the Light breeds distrust among their undead peers.

quest:916.text: Webwood Venom. Webwood Venom is an Alliance quest in Shadowglen, Teldrassil. The scholar Gilshalan Windwalker tasks young night elves with gathering venom sacs from giant webwood spiders to study how the growth of the new World Tree has affected native wildlife. Gilshalan Windwalker has journeyed to Shadowglen to examine the unnatural size and aggression of the local webwood spiders infesting Shadowthread Cave. He notes that these beasts are cousins to much smaller varieties elsewhere. Suspecting that the immense magical energies of Teldrassil are causing rapid and disturbing mutations in local fauna, he requests venom sacs to compare their biological properties against ordinary arachnid species. The webwood spiders dwelling around and inside Shadowthread Cave have become increasingly hazardous to young night elf novices in the glen. Gathering their venom serves a dual purpose: it thins out a dangerous localized infestation while supplying Darnassian researchers with direct biological evidence regarding Teldrassil's volatile influence on the wild.

quest:917.text: Webwood Egg. Gilshalan Windwalker tasks young defenders in Shadowglen with recovering an unhatched spider egg from deep inside Shadowthread Cave. Having gathered samples of their venom, he needs living specimens to study the unnatural aggression afflicting Teldrassil's wildlife. Securing an unhatched clutch allows researchers to study the creatures safely without subduing full-grown arachnids. Having secured raw venom from the aggressive Webwood spiders prowling the perimeter of Shadowglen, Gilshalan Windwalker requires live subjects to better understand their unnatural corruption. Knowing that hauling a thrashing, giant arachnid out of the subterranean depths would prove deadly for any novice, Gilshalan opts for a more practical solution: an unhatched egg taken directly from the brooding clutches within Shadowthread Cave. Shadowthread Cave serves as the subterranean nursery for the forest's increasingly hostile arachnids. Penetrating the cave and recovering an intact egg provides scholars with a controlled subject that can hatch under containment. Gilshalan intends to bundle the egg alongside his venom samples and send them directly to Darnassus for further examination, marking the conclusion of his local field study and directing recruits toward higher duties atop the boughs of Aldrassil.

quest:918.text: Timberling Seeds. Timberling Seeds is an early task given by the botanist Denalan at Lake Al'Ameth in Teldrassil. Concerned by the growing hostility of the local nature elementals, Denalan seeks to harvest their seeds to test whether enriched soil can cultivate calmer, more harmonious growth. The task offers a glimpse into the quiet efforts of night elf herbalists working to understand the subtle afflictions plaguing the World Tree. Timberlings are nature elementals native to the boughs of Teldrassil, intricately linked to the health and vitality of the flora around them. Ordinarily peaceful reflections of the forest's balance, their recent and inexplicable hostility has alarmed the local night elves. Rather than merely culling them, the botanist Denalan hopes to understand the source of their agitation. Suspecting the blemish lies deep within the ground itself, Denalan aims to sprout fresh timberlings in enriched, carefully treated loam. By collecting seeds from the wandering timberlings near Lake Al'Ameth, he hopes to nurture a gentler generation of elementals and discover whether the land's corruption can be countered from the roots up.

quest:920.text: Tenaron's Summons. Tenaron's Summons marks a crucial transition for young night elves in Shadowglen. After assisting Gilshalan Windwalker with local woodland perils, you are called to ascend the massive boughs of Aldrassil to confer with Tenaron Stormgrip. This summons marks the moment a novice leaves minor local chores behind to confront the deeper spiritual afflictions touching Teldrassil. Having proven your capability handling the venomous spiders and corrupted wildlife stirring in the glen, your efforts do not go unnoticed. Gilshalan Windwalker passes word that Tenaron Stormgrip himself has requested your presence. Even among the exceptionally long-lived night elves, keeping an elder waiting atop the great tree Aldrassil is considered poor form. Tenaron waits in the highest chamber of Aldrassil, looking out over the verdant boughs of Shadowglen. Answering this summons leads directly into larger matters of stewardship: the cleansing of Teldrassil's moonwells and the investigation of the unnatural corruption creeping into the World Tree's fledgling ecosystem.

quest:921.text: Crown of the Earth. Crown of the Earth is an introductory rite given by Tenaron Stormgrip high within Aldrassil. As young night elves prepare to venture beyond the Shadowglen, they are sent to draw sacred water from a nearby moonwell and confront the painful history of Mount Hyjal and their people's lost immortality. Before any fledgling adventurer departs the sheltered boughs of Shadowglen, the elders ensure they understand the steep price the kaldorei recently paid. At the Battle of Mount Hyjal, the World Tree Nordrassil was sacrificed to defeat Archimonde and banish the Burning Legion. With that cataclysmic blast, the night elves lost their ageless immortality and their sacred shield. Tenaron Stormgrip acts as both mentor and historian, assigning novices this ritual to instill humility and purpose before they face a changing world. The task requires drawing water from a moonwell north of Aldrassil using a crystal phial. These moonwells are no ordinary springs; their waters are infused with remnants of the ancient Well of Eternity. While the druids channel their restorative powers into the wild and the Sentinels revere them as tranquil shrines to the goddess Elune, the kaldorei remain acutely cautious. Arcane sorcery remains strictly outlawed across night elf society, as the wellspring that sustains their land is also a reminder of the reckless magic that once nearly broke the world.

quest:92124.text: Book Inventory. Book Inventory is an introductory task in Northshire Abbey given by Brother Paxton. Frustrated by misplaced and missing tomes, the abbey's librarian sends young adventurers to find his assistant, Daniel, and take stock of the abbey library's archives. However, Daniel's notorious habit of daydreaming about local tradeskills makes getting a straight answer far more difficult than Paxton would like. Northshire Abbey preserves some of the oldest scholarly works, spiritual writings, and historical records left standing in the Kingdom of Stormwind after the First War. Managing these volumes falls upon Brother Paxton, a meticulous monk who takes great pride in the abbey's collection. Lately, books have gone missing from the shelves, threatening Northshire's archival peace. Paxton needs a clear inventory to understand how widespread the loss really is, but he lacks the patience to chase down his daydreaming helper. Stationed inside the abbey library, Daniel serves as Brother Paxton's assistant, yet the youth's mind rarely stays on parchment and catalog numbers. Instead, Daniel is fascinated by the practical trades of Elwynn Forest—smithing, leatherworking, tailoring, and herbal craft. This preoccupation exasperates Paxton to no end, as every inventory task inevitably leads to the assistant rambling about local crafters rather than locating lost scriptures.

quest:922.text: Rellian Greenspyre. This errand sends you from Denalan's lakeside retreat in Teldrassil into the capital city of Darnassus. Handing over a timberling seed to the druid Rellian Greenspyre reveals disturbing news about the spreading corruption in the boughs of the World Tree. Denalan has spent considerable effort cultivating and understanding the flora and elemental life around Lake Al'Ameth. Having collected seeds from the local timberlings, he dispatches you into Darnassus to present a sample to his colleague, Rellian Greenspyre. Rellian, a fellow druid who walks the tranquil terraces of the Cenarion Enclave, previously voiced curiosity about Denalan's research and hopes to raise a timberling of his own.

quest:923.text: Tumors. Assisting the Cenarion Circle in Darnassus, this task sends adventurers to cull the afflicted timberlings around Wellspring Lake in northern Teldrassil. By collecting mossy tumors from these twisted nature spirits, druids hope to study the spreading poison and safely incinerate the corrupting growths. Teldrassil was raised to be a sanctuary of harmony, but a strange affliction has begun twisting its native flora and fauna. Timberlings—typically placid, bark-skinned nature spirits—have grown hostile and erratic. Upon their living wood, grotesque mossy tumors have sprouted, pulsing with a foul, unnatural poison. While Cenarion scholars like Denalan and Rellian Greenspyre search for the root cause of this sickness, those creatures already lost to the malevolence must be culled to protect the rest of the boughs. Wellspring Lake in northern Teldrassil has become a focal point for the outbreak. The timberlings wandering its shores are among the most heavily tainted on the entire world tree. Rellian Greenspyre charges travelers with cutting down these corrupted guardians and excising their growths. By bringing the tumors directly to the druids in Darnassus to be safely burned, the night elves hope to stem the spread of the contagion while they continue searching for the source of the disease.

quest:924.text: The Demon Seed. Acting on orders funneled through Neeru Fireblade, Ak'Zeloth charges Horde travelers with neutralizing the Demon Seed atop Dreadmist Peak. By deploying an unstable Flawed Power Stone upon an altar of fire, adventurers shatter a potent conduit tied to the Burning Legion before its dark influence spreads further across the Barrens. Perched within a jagged cave high on Dreadmist Peak sits the Demon Seed, suspended over a demonic altar of fire. The artifact acts as a powerful apparatus for the Burning Legion, anchoring demonic frequencies into the dusty heart of the Barrens. To combat this threat, the orc Ak'Zeloth prepares specialized power stones capable of disrupting the artifact's link to the Nether, provided an operative can carry one to the peak before its volatile energy collapses.

quest:92460.text: Coming of Age. Coming of Age marks the initial rite of passage for young Skyborne taking their first steps beyond Thendal Village on Zephras Isle. Guided by Ailee Farheart, novices report to village leader Rorian the Dayseeker to receive an ancestral relic and formally pledge their aid to the shen'dorei. For every young Skyborne coming into adulthood, the journey begins in Thendal Village. Guided forward by Ailee Farheart, fledglings make their way just west to the greatfather tree where the village elder awaits. Passing into maturity among the shen'dorei is not merely a social milestone, but a ceremonial commitment to serve their community amid rising local troubles. At the entrance of the greatfather tree, Rorian the Dayseeker presides over the ceremony. He formally bestows an ancestral relic upon the initiate—an heirloom passed through generations of shen'dorei. Borne by many who came before, the relic serves as a lasting token of the winds of home, destined to return to the people only when its bearer's ashes are scattered to the breeze.

quest:92461.text: Harmony in Balance. Harmony in Balance is an early rite of duty given to fledgling adventurers on Zephras Isle by Rorian the Dayseeker. It tasks the player with culling juvenile vuldren in Thendal Grove to preserve the natural equilibrium of the island. Through this mundane necessity, novices learn how sensitive local beasts are to the shifting magical currents around them. Even in an era defined by uncertain futures and mounting peril, daily survival on Zephras Isle requires humble diligence. In Thendal Grove, the local vuldren population has grown at an unsustainable rate, threatening the delicate environmental harmony that sustains the island's wildlife. Rorian the Dayseeker assigns young protectors the sober task of thinning their numbers to avert widespread ecological strain. While culling wild beasts may appear to be ordinary gamekeeping, the vuldren's surge reflects deeper concerns. Though typically docile creatures, the wildlife of Zephras is attuned to the island's atmosphere and reacts sharply when the magic carried on the winds falls out of balance. Correcting imbalances early prevents docile creatures from degenerating into unpredictable and dangerous pests.

quest:92462.text: Infestation Investigation. Infestation Investigation is an early task given to young adventurers stepping out into Thendal Grove on Zephras Isle. Ranger Elatrell Featherlight orders a cull of pesky cirrusflies that have begun swarming the eastern groves. Left unchecked, the fast-breeding insects threaten to destabilize the peaceful grove and endanger local settlements. Thendal Grove has long maintained a delicate balance, but recent reports by local rangers indicate a sudden population surge of pesky cirrusflies on the eastern edge of the woods. While individual cirrusflies are minor pests, their swarms quickly turn aggressive and destructive when numbers balloon. Ranger Elatrell Featherlight wastes no time dispatching capable youth to cull the flying insects before their presence completely overwhelms the grove. Following their initial coming of age, young defenders are thrust directly into the practical upkeep of Zephras Isle. Clearing out pests might seem like menial labor, but keeping the woodlands safe from creeping wildlife outbreaks is vital to safeguarding the settlements nearby. The sheer abundance of entrails and insects clinging to returning hunters proves that the swarm's scale is far worse than initially feared.

quest:92463.text: The Cirrusfly Queen. The Cirrusfly Queen is a hunt targeting the matriarch of the aggressive insect hive dwelling in Thendal Grove on Zephras Isle. Following early reconnaissance of the infestation, Elatrell Featherlight directs recruits into the heart of the grove to eliminate the queen and cull the swarm at its source. Ending her reign provides immediate relief to the local rangers working to keep the wilderness manageable. Initial efforts against the cirrusflies revealed that simply swatting away stray worker drones would never curb the infestation spreading across Thendal Grove. Elatrell Featherlight tasks capable wanderers with penetrating deeper into the southeastern reaches of the grove where the main hive lies. There, the queen directs the colony under the vigilant protection of heavier soldier drones. While common cirrusflies might seem like petty pests from a distance, their larger breeds pose a serious physical danger to anyone passing beneath the boughs of Zephras. By hunting down the matriarch and withstanding her guards, novices prove their martial mettle, earning high praise and a nod of respect from Featherlight's ranger cadre.

quest:92464.text: Elemental Unrest. Elemental Unrest is an introductory task given by Rorian the Dayseeker on Zephras Isle. Following the departure of the island's sentient elemental benefactors, the lesser wind spirits near the Thendal Standing Stones have grown agitated and unpredictable. You are sent into Thendal Grove to find Rorian's apprentice, Yala Windwatcher, and discover what is unsettling the local breeze. For generations, the people of Zephras lived alongside powerful, sentient wind spirits who guided and protected them. With those elemental benefactors gone, the island has drifted into persistent imbalance. The air is no longer tended by benevolent minds, leaving only simple sprites that reflect the volatile emotions and forces lingering across the landscape. Northeast of Rorian's post, near the ancient Thendal Standing Stones, the air has grown sharply hostile. Because these lesser manifestations lack true self-awareness, their turbulence is not born of malice, but of reaction. Rorian sent his apprentice, Yala Windwatcher, to monitor their erratic behavior from the edge of the grove and deduce what unseen tension is disturbing them.

quest:92465.text: Agitators. Agitators is an early task on Zephras Isle issued by Yala Windwatcher. The aggressive Al'Aketh cult has pushed into Thendal Grove, agitating the peaceful native wind sprites into hostile elementals. Adventurers are sent to disperse the roiling winds and clear out the cultist converts threatening the area. Thendal Grove has fallen under the shadow of the Al'Aketh cult. Known for their unsettling designs on Zephras Isle, the cultists have encroached on the grove and actively riled the delicate wind spirits dwelling there. Once peaceful sprites have turned violent, forming volatile roiling winds that threaten anyone passing through the region. Yala Windwatcher tasks passing champions with subduing both the enraged elementals and the Al'Aketh converts fomenting the unrest. While putting down the wind creatures restores a fragile calm to the grove, dealing with the cultists is a somber duty: Yala laments the shedding of shen'dorei blood among their own people, yet recognizes that the cult leaves little choice.

quest:92469.text: Return to Rorian. Return to Rorian is a mission carrying urgent reports from the field back to Thendal Grove on Zephras Isle. After aiding Yala Windwatcher against encroaching forces, an adventurer is dispatched to inform Rorian the Dayseeker that the Al'Aketh cult has actively escalated their presence by disturbing the local wind spirits. Following the disruption dealt to the agitators harassing Zephras Isle, Yala Windwatcher stays behind to mop up remaining hostiles while tasking you with an essential duty: delivering intelligence. Thendal Grove needs to know that the mysterious Al'Aketh are no longer operating purely in the shadows.

quest:92470.text: Foul Matriarch. Foul Matriarch is a trial of survival assigned by Aetheen of the Gales to budding initiates in Thendal Village. The task demands delving into the southern caves to cull the scavenging ursera and slay their vicious den mother, Urs'anah. Completing the hunt proves that an adventurer possesses the resolve required to face greater perils across Zephras Isle. Aetheen of the Gales maintains a watchful eye on newcomers finding their footing around Thendal Village. Once an initiate demonstrates early competence, Aetheen issues a dangerous rite of passage: a direct assault against the predatory wildlife threatening the perimeter. Rather than simply fighting on the open paths, the initiate is sent directly into the dark caves to the south to thin the local ursera packs and confront their broodmother. The local rangers have long noted the ferocity of the ursera, but none poses a greater threat to the haven than Urs'anah, their formidable matriarch. Sheltered deep within Thendal Cave, she directs her scavengers and aggressively defends her lair. Bringing back her severed head serves as definitive proof that an adventurer is capable of handling ferocious beasts and is ready to push beyond the borders of the starting grove.

quest:92471.text: Aetheen of the Gales. This quest marks a rite of passage for young adventurers on Zephras Isle, directing them to report to one of the island's leading authorities. After completing early trials under Rorian the Dayseeker, promising youths are sent into Thendal Grove to meet Aetheen of the Gales, an elder who reads the winds and evaluates the next generation. The early tasks set before novitiates on Zephras Isle are not merely mundane chores; they serve as informal tests to evaluate whether rising youths possess the grit and spirit needed to defend their homeland. Recognizing that island life faces growing trials, mentors such as Rorian the Dayseeker keep a watchful eye on candidates who prove capable of handling greater responsibility. Deep within Thendal Grove sits Aetheen of the Gales, a respected member of the Council of Elders governing Zephras Isle. Aetheen spends her time reading the currents of the air and assessing young shen'dorei as they come of age. Stepping before her signifies that an initiate has outgrown minor perimeter duties and is ready to tackle direct threats facing the community.

quest:92472.text: The Next Step. Following the resolution of the immediate beast threats near Thendal Village, Elder Aetheen of the Gales directs travelers southward toward Shen'dar Village. The journey marks a shift from clearing wild fauna to confronting the organized zealotry of the Al'Aketh Cult, who revere the Windlord Al'Akir. After proving capable against the local predators and the matriarchs plaguing the northern wilderness of Zephras Isle, adventurers are called to broader duties. Elder Aetheen of the Gales recognizes that simple pest control is secondary to the true peril taking root across the island. To protect the isle's inhabitants, capable defenders must be dispatched to support the outlying settlements. The primary danger facing southern Zephras is the Al'Aketh Cult. Described as ruthless zealots, the cultists dedicate themselves to Al'Akir the Windlord, ruler of the elemental realm of Skywall. Their growing power poses an immediate menace to Shen'dar Village. In response, Aetheen sends travelers southward down the road, past lurking ambushers in the highlands, to reinforce Constable Aonda's local guard.

quest:92473.text: Aggressive Encroachment. Aggressive Encroachment is a task issued by Valreaa Valewind to protect the local settlement from desperate wildlife. Ursera from a nearby den have grown increasingly bold, wandering into the village and threatening its inhabitants. The ursera population nesting southwest of the village has become an urgent safety hazard. Recently, a hungry adolescent beast strayed right up to the base of the village's central elder tree, nearly mauling a young child playing nearby. The settlement's rangers were forced to cut the creature down before tragedy struck. Recognizing that hunger and starvation are driving these predators to attack civilized grounds, the rangers have ordered a cull of the scrawniest ursera in Thendal Grove. By eliminating the desperate and malnourished beasts prowling outside the dens, the Rangers of the Grove hope to halt further encroachment until they can uncover what is disturbing the local wildlife.

quest:92474.text: Falling With Style. "Falling With Style" is an introductory rite of passage for young Skyborne in Thendal Village. Offered atop the local watchtower by the mischievous Myriaal Mistwake, it challenges novices to test their innate slow-fall ability by leaping from the platform toward Rorian the Dayseeker below. Perched high above Thendal Village on Zephras Isle, Myriaal Mistwake invites young Skyborne to test their heritage through a game of daring. Rather than treating their innate magical gifts as sacred relics kept under strict restraint, Myriaal encourages newcomers to leap into the open air from the watchtower ledge. The purpose is practical as well as playful: mastering the instinctive art of walking upon air before life beyond the grove demands it in perilous situations. The exercise serves as a vivid demonstration of two contrasting Skyborne attitudes. While Myriaal delights in sudden descents and startles onlookers for amusement, Rorian the Dayseeker embodies traditional caution. When novices glide down to land squarely before him, Rorian admonishes the reckless display, warning that thoughtlessly exhausting one's magical gifts can leave a traveler helpless when danger strikes. Even so, he concedes that controlled practice within the safety of the village has its place.

quest:92481.text: A Student of the Arcane. A Student of the Arcane is an introductory trial and summons for novice spellcasters on Zephras Isle. Initiated by Rorian the Dayseeker after newcomers prove their basic mettle, it directs budding mages to review a Glowing Recall Crystal and report to the local mentor, Dorii Brightwhisper. After helping manage the troublesome vuldren lurking near Thendal Grove, fledgling mages are entrusted with a curious artifact: a Glowing Recall Crystal. Left behind by Dorii Brightwhisper, the island's resident arcane instructor, the crystal serves as a magically recorded missive designed to test an initiate's aptitude and welcome them into deeper mystical study. According to Dorii Brightwhisper, mastery of the arcane has slowly dwindled among their people during their long millennia spent secluded high in the clouds. Dorii views each new practitioner not merely as a student, but as an essential pioneer meant to recover lost knowledge and restore their people's once-mighty magical heritage.

quest:92482.text: The Way of the Hunter. The Way of the Hunter is an introductory training quest for fledgling hunters in Thendal Grove on Zephras Isle. After proving their mettle against the local vuldren threat, young trackers are directed by Rorian the Dayseeker to present themselves to Tai'ree Farsight to begin their formal tutelage. Upon returning from thinning the disruptive vuldren prowling the outskirts of Thendal Grove, young hunters find that their practical skills have caught local attention. Rorian the Dayseeker passes along a scribbled summons from Tai'ree Farsight, the grove's resident hunter trainer. For novice rangers setting out into the wider wilds of Zephras Isle, this marked the shift from simple island defense to true martial and survival instruction. Found near the center of the village, Tai'ree Farsight welcomes promising pupils with stern realism. Emphasizing that thriving in untamed nature demands sharp senses and lightning reflexes, she offers guidance born of her own long years of experience. Her mentorship marks the foundational steps for any island tracker looking to hone their marksmanship and survival skills.

quest:92483.text: At Home in the Shadows. "At Home in the Shadows" is an introductory rogue quest on Zephras Isle. After aiding Rorian the Dayseeker in Thendal Grove, budding rogues are directed to read a summons and meet their local class mentor, Akeri Duskblade. The quest marks the moment young rogues transition from general village chores to serious stealth and combat training. While handling basic threats around Thendal Grove, young rogues draw the attention of Akeri Duskblade, the grove's resident rogue trainer. Rather than mingling openly in the settlement, Akeri passes a simple note through Rorian the Dayseeker. Rorian recognizes that despite Akeri's suspicious demeanor, the mentor understands the practical skills needed to survive outside the grove's sheltered boundaries. Tucked away inside the village watchtower, Akeri Duskblade wastes no time mincing words. He evaluates every newcomer's footing and awareness immediately upon their arrival, warning that sloppy footwork outside Thendal Grove leads straight to an early grave. By surviving Akeri's scrutiny, a rogue takes their first formal step into mastering stealth, precision, and survival on Zephras Isle.

quest:92484.text: Embracing the Elements. Embracing the Elements is an introductory shaman quest in Thendal Grove on Zephras Isle. Initiated by Rorian the Dayseeker, the task directs young practitioners to Windshaper Boro, the local shaman trainer. It introduces the silent rift between the local people and the elemental spirits of the winds. After helping manage the vuldren pest problem around the village, aspiring shamans are approached by Rorian the Dayseeker. During their time afield, Windshaper Boro left behind a humming recall crystal, signaling that it is time for formal elemental instruction to begin in the center of the grove. Upon meeting Windshaper Boro, he explains the difficult state of local shamanism. The spirits of the four winds abruptly severed communication years ago, abandoning their former communion. Zephras shamans now dedicate themselves to deep study of the natural world, striving through rigorous training to bridge the silence and coax the spirits into dialogue once more.

quest:92485.text: A Student of Nature. A Student of Nature marks a fledgling druid's introduction to formal training on Zephras Isle. After helping restore local harmony, novice druids are summoned by Xyton Silverwind beneath the boughs of Thendal Grove. It serves as the opening gateway into understanding the deeper balance between flora and fauna on the isle. Following the resolution of local disturbances caused by overzealous wildlife, Rorian the Dayseeker delivers a personal summons to young initiates. Left behind by the local mentor Xyton Silverwind, the folded parchment invites aspiring druids to step forward and dedicate themselves to the deeper mysteries of the wild. It signals that an initiate's natural talents have caught the eye of the grove's elders. Meeting Xyton Silverwind on the lower level of the great tree in Thendal Grove anchors a novice to their calling. Silverwind regards the vibrant flora and fauna of Zephras Isle as an intricate living tapestry, one that demands constant preservation and vigilant balance. To walk the path of the fang, claw, feather, and branch requires enduring mentorship, and this meeting marks the true beginning of that lifelong stewardship.

quest:92532.text: The Warrior's Path. The Warrior's Path is an introductory martial quest offered to budding fighters on Zephras Isle. Following instructions delivered through Rorian the Dayseeker, young warriors are directed to Blademaster Ren in the Thendal Village watchtower. Ren stands ready to offer combat instruction and discipline to those prepared to shield their people. Upon returning to Rorian the Dayseeker in Thendal Village after restoring balance nearby, aspiring fighters receive word that the settlement's blademaster has taken notice of them. Rorian delivers a crumpled note penned by Ren herself, asking the novice to seek her out directly. Elevated above the settlement within the village watchtower, Ren keeps an observant eye over both the island's borders and the recruits who may one day defend them. Reaching the watchtower introduces the warrior to Blademaster Ren's philosophy of combat. To Ren, martial mastery is not simply an exercise in brute strength, but a vital duty to lead, endure, and protect in an increasingly uncertain world. She pledges her guidance to the recruit as they hone their skills, offering rigorous training as they grow strong enough to face the greater perils threatening their home.

quest:92544.text: Al'Aketh Thugs. The peaceful roads around Thendal Grove are threatened by a violent band of Al'Aketh cultists occupying the nearby temple ruins. Dispatched from the Shrine of Akir under orders to harass wayfarers and force recruits into their ranks, these zealots pose an immediate danger to local travelers. Hanaa Nightwind tasks adventurers with breaking their hold and slaying their brutish commander. Just southwest of Thendal Grove lie ancient temple ruins that should offer quiet shelter to wanderers. Instead, the grounds have been overtaken by the Al'Aketh, an aggressive cult driven by fanatical ambition. Far from peaceful worshipers, these cultists act as highwaymen and enforcers, preying upon those traveling along the outskirts of the grove. The Rangers stationed nearby suspect these ruffians were sent directly by High Priestess Lorthuna from the Shrine of Akir to bully and coerce the populace into bowing to the cult's influence. Heading the rabble at the temple ruins is Malduko Cloudcrush, a brutal leader who uses violence and fear to keep both his initiates and unsuspecting wayfarers in line. With brutes and newly indoctrinated neophytes answering his commands, Malduko has established an aggressive outpost right on the doorstep of Thendal Grove. By striking down Cloudcrush and scattering his underlings, Hanaa Nightwind hopes to shatter the cult's confidence and send a clear warning that zealotry and coercion will not be tolerated in these lands.

quest:92597.text: Reading the Ley Lines. Reading the Ley Lines is a rite of passage for young Skyborne discovering their Highborne magical heritage. Entrusted by Falorne Fallwind on Zephras Isle, novitiates travel to the standing stones in Thendal Grove to sense and draw upon the raw arcane currents surging through the elemental terrain. Even within the windswept confines of the elemental plane, latent arcane conduits run beneath the earth. While strange elementals and the hostile Al'Aketh drift across Zephras Isle, subterranean ley lines have begun pushing toward the surface. To practitioners of magic, these ruptures provide direct access to untamed arcane reservoirs, offering strength to any who possess the bloodline and knowledge necessary to channel them. Falorne Fallwind urges initiates to embrace their Highborne ancestry rather than supplicate themselves to wind spirits like the local Windshapers or the zealots of the Al'Aketh. In Fallwind's view, survival against the harsh powers of the elemental plane depends not on begging foreign creatures for mercy, but on mastering the intrinsic arcane power running beneath their boots. Northeast of the settlement lies Thendal Grove, where ancient standing stones mark a potent ley line convergence. Surrounded by roiling winds and Al'Aketh converts, this exposed point of magical flux allows initiates to attune their senses, harmonizing with the pulse of the ley line and unleashing the full potential of their natural racial abilities.

quest:92598.text: The Gift of Skysight. The Gift of Skysight is an early rite of passage for young Windshapers learning to harness their innate connection to the spiritual realm. Under the direction of Ventaari Brightwish, initiates travel to an Elemental Convergence to awaken their perception and listen directly to the whispers of the spirits. Windshapers possess an inherent bond with the elemental forces that shape their world, embodied by the sacred faculty known as Skysight. This gift allows mortal senses to attune to spiritual wavelengths, bridging the physical gap between the living and the unseen. While a Windshaper can invoke this inner vision across the wilds, doing so near points of concentrated power deepens the connection, unlocking resonant boons and hidden wisdom whispered on the wind. Northeast of the settlement, amidst ancient standing stones, lies an Elemental Convergence in Thendal Grove. Places such as these act as focal points where raw energies gather and spirit entities linger. Ventaari Brightwish sends novices to this sacred site not simply to complete a task, but to test their spiritual constitution. Like any faculty of body or mind, Skysight requires deliberate exercise to mature, ensuring that a growing Windshaper can interpret the shifting omens of the elements upon which their people's survival depends.

quest:926.text: Flawed Power Stone. Deep within the arid expanse of the Barrens, mysterious stones infused with arcane energy rest atop arcane tables. Intentionally fashioned with fatal defects, these volatile relics consume their own power rapidly once separated from their source. The flawed power stones found scattered in the Barrens are curious magical anomalies. While undeniably charged with arcane essence, their structure was intentionally compromised during their creation. Whatever hands shaped them ensured that they would remain deeply unstable, decaying into inert matter mere moments after being handled. Rather than acting as steady reservoirs or catalysts, these stones immediately begin to burn through their contained power the moment they are taken from the ritual tables where they rest. This self-consuming nature prevents anyone from transporting them far.

quest:9260.text: Investigate the Scourge of Stormwind. The Scourge invasion has brought the horrors of the Lich King directly to the gates of Stormwind. Outside the capital's walls, necropolises shadow the land while undead abominations and cultists conjure dark magic. Lieutenant Orrin enlists capable defenders to cull the invaders, gather Necrotic Stones, and decipher the sinister runic circles pulsing at their encampments. The presence of Scourge forces so close to Stormwind City is an unsettling shock for the kingdom. Floating necropolises loom overhead while shambling undead and sinister cultists establish footholds right on the doorstep of humanity's greatest bastion. Lieutenant Orrin rallies defenders outside the city to push back these invading horrors before they can overwhelm the capital's perimeter. Beyond simply fighting off the walking dead, the mission requires investigating the glowing runic circles etched into the dirt around the enemy encampments. These occult circles crackle with the same fell magic radiating from the necropolises above. Venturing into their glow reveals eerie whispers lingering on the air—unnatural voices that suggest the circles serve as conduits of some kind of dark communication, though Lieutenant Orrin can only guess at whom they contact.

quest:9261.text: Investigate the Scourge of Ironforge. Lieutenant Nevell of the Argent Dawn calls upon brave defenders as the Scourge arrives directly outside the gates of Ironforge. Undead troops and ominous runic circles threaten the snowy passes of Dun Morogh beneath a hovering necropolis. Defenders are tasked with destroying the walking corpses and deciphering the purpose behind these strange glowing sigils. The Scourge invasion does not stop at Lordaeron or the plagued lands of the north. Floating necropolises cast grim shadows across Azeroth, including the frigid heights of Dun Morogh right outside Ironforge's mountain entrance. The Argent Dawn has stationed observers such as Lieutenant Nevell to monitor and counter this creeping blight before it can breach the fortress of the Bronzebeards.

quest:9262.text: Investigate the Scourge of Darnassus. Investigate the Scourge of Darnassus is an emergency mission issued by Lieutenant Beitha on behalf of the Argent Dawn. With a necropolis looming over the Scourge encampment, Alliance defenders are tasked with destroying encroaching undead and deciphering the dark runic circles appearing outside the city gates. The Scourge invasion has reached the sheltered boughs of Teldrassil. Floating necropolises appear in the sky, vomiting forth ghouls, skeletons, and necromantic horrors right outside Darnassus. Lieutenant Beitha of the Argent Dawn has stepped forward to coordinate the capital's defense, enlisting willing volunteers to blunt the vanguard and gather intelligence before the undead can overwhelm the night elven homeland.

quest:9263.text: Investigate the Scourge of Orgrimmar. The Scourge has brazenly established an encampment right outside the gates of Orgrimmar under the shadow of a floating necropolis. Lieutenant Dagel tasks defenders with repelling the undead, recovering necrotic stones, and probing the mysterious runic circles humming with necromantic energy. This sudden intrusion brings the Lich King's reach directly to the heart of Durotar. The threat of the Scourge is no longer confined to the ruined kingdoms of Lordaeron or the icy wastes of the north. Floating necropolises have appeared across Azeroth, casting dark shadows even over Durotar. At Orgrimmar's very threshold, undead forces have gathered, carving out encampments and threatening the capital of the Horde. Lieutenant Dagel and the Argent Dawn are coordinating defensive efforts, calling upon local champions to push the invaders back before they can establish an unbreakable siege.

quest:92742.text: Testing the Wells. Testing the Wells is an investigative task assigned by Alba Fairmoon to determine the source of poison seeping through Westfall's soil. Adventurers are sent with sampling kits to collect groundwater from the wells at the Jansen Stead and Molsen Farm. Westfall's open plains have suffered severe neglect and banditry, but an insidious contamination beneath the earth threatens whatever agriculture remains. To understand how the farmland is being tainted, Alba Fairmoon directs investigators to test the groundwater directly. By drawing water samples from settled farmsteads, investigators hope to identify the nature of the toxins plaguing the region's soil and life. The survey focuses on two vital locations: the Jansen Stead and the Molsen Farm. Both plots lie among the scattered homesteads vulnerable to roaming Defias outlaws and feral wildlife. Drawing samples from their wellheads offers a baseline for whether the blighting agent is naturally emerging, magically induced, or deliberately seeded into the water table feeding the region.

quest:92744.text: Murloc Gills. Murloc Gills is an Alliance task in Westfall given by Alba Fairmoon. Amid concerns that the crop blight could poison coastal fisheries, adventurers are dispatched to the Longshore to collect murloc gills for ecological analysis. Because murloc physiology is acutely sensitive to maritime contaminants, their gills reveal whether toxins have infiltrated the sea. Westfall is already on the verge of ruin due to widespread crop failure, displaced farmers, and banditry. Alba Fairmoon fears an even deadlier development: that the corruption afflicting the inland harvest has begun draining into the Great Sea. If Westfall's coastal waters are tainted, the fish stocks that feed the peasantry and supplement the tables of Stormwind City could vanish entirely, tipping a strained kingdom into outright famine. While murlocs are notoriously stubborn and violent creatures, their amphibious biology makes them keen natural bio-indicators. Murloc respiratory systems constantly filter seawater, making their gill tissue exceptionally receptive to foreign poisons, blights, and unnatural pollutants. By studying freshly harvested gills taken from the tide-dwellers prowling the Longshore, Fairmoon hopes to measure the exact severity of the encroaching contamination.

quest:92745.text: The State of the Mines. The State of the Mines is a task given by Alba Fairmoon to combat environmental contamination across Westfall. After well samples turn up toxic metals, Alba suspects the mines the Defias have seized and warns that the farmland could be ruined for decades. To stop this ecological disaster, adventurers are sent to disrupt Defias-led excavations at both Jangolode Mine and the Gold Coast Quarry. Westfall was once the primary breadbasket of Stormwind, but recent water samples retrieved from local wells reveal dangerous levels of toxic metals. Alba Fairmoon's first suspicion falls on the mines the Defias Brotherhood has seized across the region. If this pollution continues unchecked, the surrounding earth will be rendered barren and unable to sustain crops for decades to come. Rather than relying solely on their own highwaymen, the Defias use local creature populations as labor to strip Westfall of its natural wealth. Riverpaw gnolls are set to backbreaking work digging out stone and mineral veins at the Gold Coast Quarry, while kobold diggers are put to work tunneling into the depths of the Jangolode Mine. Cutting down their workforce strikes directly at their ability to process and distribute contaminated minerals.
