quest:928.text: Crown of the Earth. Crown of the Earth is a transitional journey that takes young night elves out of Shadowglen and into the broader realm of Teldrassil. Carrying sacred moonwell water consecrated atop Aldrassil, travelers are directed south along the forest road to meet Corithras Moonrage in Dolanaar. It marks the graduation from secluded training to the urgent ecological defense of the great World Tree. After proving their dedication by sampling the enchanted waters of Shadowglen's moonwell, initiates are summoned before Tenaron Stormgrip at the crown of Aldrassil. Recognizing their readiness, Tenaron seals the gathered water into a larger vessel and commands them to venture beyond the sheltered grove. The road leading south toward Dolanaar is the primary artery out of Shadowglen, winding through woods that have grown increasingly unpredictable and hostile. Dolanaar serves as the first major village travelers encounter upon exiting the starting glen. Situated along the cobblestone paths curving through central Teldrassil, the settlement bustles around its own pristine moonwell. Here awaits Corithras Moonrage, an elder tasked with overseeing broader preservation efforts across the boughs. The vessel delivered into his keeping ties the fledgling adventurer directly to the wider, troubled fate of the World Tree.

quest:929.text: Crown of the Earth. Crown of the Earth is a sacred task assigned by Corithras Moonrage in Dolanaar to draw sanctified waters from the moonwell near Starbreeze Village. In exchange for replenishing the waters of Darnassus, young night elves learn the tragic history that led their people to cultivate the massive boughs of Teldrassil. The great central moonwell of Darnassus demands constant communion with the lesser fonts scattered across the crown of the World Tree. Druids craft refined jade phials specifically to draw and carry these luminescent waters without disturbing their purity. By sending initiates on foot to Starbreeze Village, the elders ensure both that the civic fountains remain brimming with Elune's grace and that the youth understand the labor required to nourish Teldrassil. Completing this chore rewards the initiate with oral history. Corithras Moonrage recounts the despair that gripped the kaldorei immediately after the Battle of Mount Hyjal. The sacrifice of the ancestral World Tree Nordrassil stripped the night elves of their precious immortality, and amidst the ruin, Illidan Stormrage was unleashed while Shan'do Malfurion Stormrage disappeared. This climate of grief and isolation laid the groundwork for Teldrassil's controversial planting.

quest:933.text: Crown of the Earth. Crown of the Earth is an Alliance quest given by Corithras Moonrage in Dolanaar. He directs you to draw water from the moonwell near the Pools of Arlithrien, an area increasingly threatened by crazed Gnarlpine furbolgs. Completing this task uncovers how Arch Druid Fandral Staghelm rallied the night elves to raise Teldrassil in the wake of Malfurion Stormrage's disappearance. Corithras Moonrage tasks you with taking a tourmaline phial to a moonwell resting southeast of Darnassus's entrance, along the shores of the Pools of Arlithrien. The journey is far from quiet. The once peaceful Gnarlpine furbolgs have succumbed to sudden, violent fury, ambushing travelers and harrying Sentinel patrols throughout the region. What early reports wrote off as isolated skirmishes has escalated into a pervasive threat haunting the new home of the night elves. Upon receiving the filled phial, Corithras shares critical history regarding Teldrassil's creation. Following the Third War, Shan'do Malfurion Stormrage vanished, leaving the Cenarion druids leaderless and fractured. In his absence, Arch Druid Fandral Staghelm seized the mantle of leadership. Staghelm persuaded the Circle of Ancients in Darkshore that the night elves could not afford idle mourning; they needed to reclaim their lost immortality and heal their civilization by planting a massive new World Tree.

quest:934.text: Crown of the Earth. Crown of the Earth is a pivotal step in the Dolanaar quest chain investigating the ailments plaguing Teldrassil. Corithras Moonrage tasks adventurers with gathering water from the sacred moonwell in the Oracle Glade, using the journey to reveal the troubling truth behind the World Tree's creation. Corithras Moonrage directs travelers far to the northwest of Teldrassil, nestled beneath the majestic canopy of the Oracle Glade. Resting directly under the massive boughs of the Oracle Tree lies the first and most potent moonwell raised upon the island. Drawing an Amethyst Phial from its shimmering waters brings seekers face to face with the prime sanctuary from which the druids and the tree itself monitor the health of their new homeland.

quest:935.text: Crown of the Earth. "Crown of the Earth" marks the culmination of the moonwell rites across Teldrassil. Handing over the gathered waters to Arch Druid Fandral Staghelm in Darnassus underscores the growing anxiety over the World Tree's flawed, unblessed existence. Teldrassil was raised in the wake of the Third War to grant the night elves a new home and restore their lost immortality. However, the Great Aspects Alexstrasza and Nozdormu withheld their blessings, refusing to sanction the tree's creation. Without their divine protection, Teldrassil has fallen victim to creeping sickness, causing bizarre creatures to erupt from the boughs and once-peaceful furbolg tribes to descend into madness.

quest:93552.text: Harvesting Windstones. Harvesting Windstones is a task offered by Dalia the Collector in Thendal Grove on Zephras Isle. As the ancient elemental energies sustaining the island slowly fade, raw windstones have become an essential magical fuel source. Adventurers are sent across the grove to harvest crystalline windstone clusters before their power is lost. Zephras Isle relies heavily on lingering wind magic to sustain itself, but its natural defenses are dwindling. Centuries ago, the native wind elementals who shared the island with the local elves vanished entirely. Since their departure, the ambient magic upholding the land and the great anchor pylons has been in a slow, steady decline. For the residents of Thendal Grove, surviving this depletion requires securing every possible reserve of raw energy. Windstones are vibrant blue crystalline formations scattered naturally throughout Thendal Grove. Within their brittle shells lies dense, concentrated wind magic left behind from ages past. While not an endless solution, they provide a reliable and invaluable source of arcane sustenance and utility for the island's elves, making the collection of raw clusters a vital daily endeavor.

quest:937.text: The Enchanted Glade. In the Oracle Glade on northwestern Teldrassil, Sentinel Arynia Cloudsbreak struggles to protect the ancient Oracle Tree from aggressive Bloodfeather harpies. After a dispatched runner bound for Darnassus is slain, defenders are called upon to strike back at the harpies' nests and recover their belts as proof. The Oracle Glade is one of Teldrassil's sacred retreats, centered upon a colossal, ancient specimen known as the Oracle Tree. Sentinel Arynia Cloudsbreak was dispatched with an escort of warriors to keep watch over this venerable bough. Unfortunately, savage Bloodfeather harpies have encroached on the hollows, nesting aggressively throughout the surrounding canopy and threatening anyone who draws near. Tensions peaked when the Oracle Tree attempted to send a courier to the capital city of Darnassus carrying an urgent report. The messenger never cleared the boughs; harpies ambushed and slaughtered the runner before the report could leave the glade. In response, Arynia has tasked local adventurers with culling the flock and retrieving Bloodfeather belts to push back the encroaching flock.

quest:93746.text: A Firm Response. "A Firm Response" is a Horde quest on Zephras Isle issued by Ayessa Dawnsinger. Tensions are boiling over as the mysterious High Order intrudes upon the territory and dealings of the local Windshapers. Ayessa orders a preemptive strike against Belathaan Brightwish on the road to the Shrine of Akir to establish clear boundaries through force. The Windshapers of Zephras Isle do not tolerate uninvited scrutiny, especially from an organization as secretive and calculating as the High Order. Prior warnings have gone unheeded, forcing Ayessa Dawnsinger to escalate the matter. To safeguard their interests, she chooses to intercept Belathaan Brightwish in the isolated stretch of road leading north toward the Shrine of Akir, ensuring the altercation stays away from prying eyes in town.

quest:940.text: Teldrassil. Following the cleansing of the rogue harpies near the Oracle Tree, Sentinel Arynia Cloudsbreak entrusts you with carrying a status report to Darnassus. The inscribed bark is addressed to Arch Druid Fandral Staghelm, bearing news of the state of the boughs and the ongoing corruption plaguing the World Tree. Deep in the boughs of Teldrassil, the Oracle Tree watches over the forest. After clearing the harpies from their nests in the Oracle Glade, Sentinel Arynia Cloudsbreak decides it is finally safe to dispatch word to the kaldorei leadership. Entrusting you with a piece of inscribed bark, she sends you across the wilderness and into Darnassus—the great 'forest of stone'—to deliver the Oracle Tree's report directly to Arch Druid Fandral Staghelm. When presented with the report, Fandral Staghelm receives it with mixed feelings. Though grateful for the news that the harpies were pushed back, the report underlines a deeper truth: as soon as one threat is diminished on Teldrassil, another festers in its place. For Staghelm, who championed the planting of the new World Tree to reclaim the night elves' lost immortality, the ongoing afflictions of the boughs are a bitter reminder that his grand work remains far from finished.

quest:94414.text: The Anchors of Zephras. The Anchors of Zephras is an introductory quest offered by Halaan Hawk-Eye on Zephras Isle. Halaan invites travelers to borrow his far-reaching vision to observe the ancient anchor pylons that tether and preserve the floating island. Though the soaring monoliths appear untouched from a distance, Halaan warns that the wind spirits' stabilizing magic has begun to waver. The anchor pylons of Zephras are ancient, towering monoliths gifted by the spirits of the winds. Deeply woven into the isle's mystical foundation, they serve to bind, steady, and sustain the landmass amidst the churning skies. To look upon one is to witness the fragile balance keeping Zephras aloft, relying continuously on the benevolence of the wind spirits. Despite standing proud and undamaged to the naked eye, the anchor pylons have grown erratic. Halaan Hawk-Eye notes that the magical harmony sustaining them has become unstable and inconsistent in recent times. Without clear signs of physical distress, this subtle decay raises quiet alarm among those who watch over the groves, hinting at deeper imbalances threatening the isle. Lacking the innate skysight that peers across worlds or the arcane prowess to tap Zephras's deep ley lines, Halaan possesses a simpler, sharper natural gift: keen, unclouded vision over immense distances. By lending this perspective, he allows others to observe the distant pylons in fine detail, encouraging newcomers to cultivate gratitude for the present while staying alert to their homeland's shifting fate.

quest:95041.text: Data Hoarders. Data Hoarders is a task given by Jemma Quikswitch, an exiled gnome residing in Ironforge. During the desperate evacuation of Gnomeregan, she copied her family's most prized archives onto punch cards, only to lose several in the freezing drifts outside the city gates. Recovering these lost data cards means salvaging everything from advanced naval engineering schematics to irreplaceable family recipes. When the trogg invasion and subsequent radiation disaster forced the gnomes out of Gnomeregan, thousands fled with whatever belongings they could snatch up in the chaos. Jemma Quikswitch took the prudent step of transcribing generations of family knowledge into physical punch card archives. Tragically, a damaged satchel spilled several key cards into the snowfields surrounding the fallen city. Without these missing punch cards, the remaining data registers as indecipherable gibberish, threatening to erase her family's intellectual legacy. Gnomish data archives reflect the peculiar breadth of their civilization's priorities. The Quikswitch family records include profound arcanotechnical field equations, vital Second War submarine hull blueprints, and Grandma Quikswitch's secret chili recipe. To an outsider, combining military engineering with household cooking might seem odd, but to surviving refugees in Ironforge, preserving domestic comforts matters just as much as preserving technological marvels.

quest:95065.text: Fishin' Time. Fishin' Time is a simple errand for Gilbert Gray, an elderly angler soaking in the scenic coastal views at the harbor in Stormwind. Running out of bait just as the fish begin biting, he relies on passersby to run into the city's canals and resupply his tackle box. Not everyone in Stormwind is consumed by politics, war, or looming conspiracies. Down at the harbor edge, Gilbert Gray spends his quiet days enjoying the ocean breeze and watching his bobber dance on the tides. But an enthusiastic angler can easily lose track of their tackle, and a sudden run of biting fish quickly drains even a well-prepared bait tin. Rather than abandon his prized perch, the old man turns to helpful adventurers to replenish his essentials. Stormwind's local angling needs run through Catherine Leland, who operates a well-known tackle shop nestled along the stone canals just west of the bustling Trade District. Supplying fishermen across the city with lures and bait, Leland ensures that old regulars like Gilbert Gray never have to pack up their lines early for lack of a shiny bauble or a squirming nightcrawler.

quest:952.text: Grove of the Ancients. Grove of the Ancients is an Alliance delivery quest that directs adventurers out of Darnassus and across the sea to Darkshore. Tasked by Arch Druid Fandral Staghelm, the courier carries correspondence to Onu, a venerable Ancient of Lore residing south of Auberdine. Having assisted with matters concerning the Oracle Glade atop Teldrassil, adventurers find themselves brusquely summoned into further service by Arch Druid Fandral Staghelm. Not one to waste idle hands, Staghelm tasks the messenger with carrying an urgent dispatch across the sea to the ancient forests of Darkshore, instructing them to book flight aboard a hippogryph from the city. Upon reaching Darkshore and traveling south of Auberdine to the Grove of the Ancients, the messenger delivers the missive to Onu. The towering Ancient of Lore accepts the correspondence with quiet reflection, subtly noting Staghelm's relentless impatience. To Onu and the ancient keepers of the forest, all things unfold in their proper time—a calm, enduring wisdom that Shan'do Malfurion Stormrage embodied, but which Staghelm distinctly lacks.

quest:953.text: The Fall of Ameth'Aran. Sentinel Tysha Moonblade tasks adventurers with exploring the haunting ruins of Ameth'Aran in Darkshore to decipher ancient stone tablets. These inscriptions record the tragedy and ruin that struck the Highborne city during the Sundering. The gathered knowledge is intended for the Circle of Ancients in Auberdine, recovering history largely lost during the War of the Ancients. Long before the coast fractured into the misty expanse of Darkshore, Ameth'Aran stood as a flourishing settlement where Queen Azshara's elite sorcerers practiced powerful arcane magic. Following the cataclysmic destruction of the Well of Eternity ten thousand years ago, the city was reduced to broken marble and cracked pillars. Today, it remains haunted by the restless, anguished spirits of the Highborne who died when their golden age tore apart. Because the War of the Ancients plunged the night elf civilization into chaotic survival, remarkably few written accounts survived the Great Sundering intact. Sentinel Tysha Moonblade attempted to survey the ruins herself, discovering two large engraved tablets—the Lay of Ameth'Aran and the Fall of Ameth'Aran—before ghostly Highborne specters forced her to retreat. Retrieving these readings ensures that the historical truths of the ancient disaster reach the scholars of the Circle of Ancients in Auberdine.

quest:95314.text: That Shadowvale Green Elixir. Carolai Anise in Brill seeks salvage from the abandoned settlement of Shadowvale, tucked deep within the secluded Whispering Forest. Before the kingdom fell, the village was infamous for distilling Whispering Elixir from strange local herbs—a potent draught that remained prized on the black market even after being outlawed in Lordaeron. Long before the Third War and the arrival of the Scourge, the reclusive inhabitants of Shadowvale brewed a distinct concoction known as Whispering Elixir. Distilled from rare herbs unique to Tirisfal Glades, the draught gained notoriety across northern Lordaeron. Despite being officially outlawed within the Capital City, its unusual properties made it eagerly sought after by mystics, poisoners, and practicing apothecaries willing to skirt royal decrees. Shadowvale sits hidden deep within the Whispering Forest of western Tirisfal. The villagers were historically an insular and distrustful people who rarely welcomed outsiders. Following the Scourge invasion, the settlement fell into ruin, but forgotten stores of the aged green elixir remain among the wreckage. Carolai Anise operates out of Brill, taking advantage of persistent underworld demand to pay adventurers willing to brave the forest's unsettling silence.

quest:954.text: Bashal'Aran. The demonic satyrs and vicious grells that infest the ancient night elven city of Bashal'Aran will not approach one shrine, bathed in an unearthly blue aura. Thundris Windweaver, the elder of Auberdine, sends adventurers to investigate the source of this untouched sanctuary. Bashal'Aran once stood as a glorious settlement of the ancient Kaldorei Empire, but its broken marble and overgrown arches now teem with demonic taint. Twisted satyrs and corrupt grells feed greedily upon the lingering magical energies of the ruins, their malice swelling with every passing day. Yet despite their predatory dominion, Thundris Windweaver in Auberdine spotted a curiosity: atop a western bluff in the ruins, an ethereal blue aura burns over a shrine that no demon will approach.

quest:955.text: Bashal'Aran. Asterion, a sorrowful highborne ghost haunting the ancient ruins of Bashal'Aran, seeks a way to undo the binding magic that tethers his spectral form. Believing the mischievous local grells have touched the seal holding him, he tasks travelers with gathering their earrings to trace its lingering magical resonance. Amid the shattered marble of Bashal'Aran lingers Asterion, an ancient night elf spirit who has endured centuries of confinement. Trapped between life and true death, his existence has dwindled into an agonizing wait under the canopy of Darkshore. Bound directly to the ruined settlement by arcane craft, Asterion lacks the means to dispel his shackles alone, his mind worn thin by uncounted years of solitude and despair. Asterion suspects that the key to his release is an ancient seal hidden somewhere in the ruins. While he cannot physically scour the brush and collapsed stones himself, the feral grells infesting Bashal'Aran constantly forage and steal small baubles. Asterion asks travelers to collect the earrings worn by these creatures, intending to read the residual magical impressions on the trinkets and locate the seal that holds his soul in torment.

quest:956.text: Bashal'Aran. Asterion, a night elf spirit trapped amidst the ruined pillars of Bashal'Aran, seeks the relic holding him bound to this world. Having sensed the corruption of his prison among the local grells, he directs travelers to hunt the satyrs who command them and recover the Ancient Moonstone Seal. For well over a thousand years, the spirit Asterion has remained tethered to the fallen ruins of Bashal'Aran. The surrounding marble pillars serve as an unyielding cage that neither his fading spiritual strength nor his ancient magic can crack. Bound by a cursed relic, he has spent centuries staring out at Darkshore's mist-shrouded canopy, wondering whether even the erosion of the stone around him would grant him release. After discovering that nearby grells bore traces of the magic maintaining his captivity, Asterion deduced that the source of the enchantment had fallen into the hands of the satyrs who direct the chaotic creatures. Wandering through the ancient groves, these demonic night elves keep a watchful grip on the Ancient Moonstone Seal. Reclaiming this talisman is the critical step toward shattering the invisible bars that anchor Asterion to his shrine.

quest:960.text: Onu is meditating. While investigating the Master's Glaive in southern Darkshore, the ancient of lore Onu enters a deep trance to contemplate the growing threat. Players who lose their mystical scrying phial can speak to the meditating ancient to receive a replacement. His thoughts center on the sinister alliance and motivations of the Twilight's Hammer cult and the serpentine naga. Onu is an Ancient of Lore rooted in Darkshore's Grove of the Ancients, standing as a living repository of Kalimdor's history. When ominous reports surface concerning dark excavations at the Master's Glaive, Onu turns his immense consciousness inward. He meditates heavily on what could draw both the fanatic Twilight's Hammer cultists and the insidious naga to the petrified remains of an ancient behemoth. For adventurers carrying out his reconnaissance, he remains an accessible anchor, offering replacement scrying phials should theirs be misplaced in the wild. To monitor the ruins without risking the ancient's physical presence, Onu relies on nature-attuned divination. Adventurers are entrusted with a phial of scrying, meant to conjure a scrying bowl directly within the excavation site so Onu can commune from afar. Because the journey south through Darkshore is perilous and fraught with hostile wildlife and cultist patrols, Onu anticipates mishaps. His trance is not unbroken slumber, but an attentive vigil; he readily provides another vial of sacred waters to ensure the investigation of the Master's Glaive continues without delay.

quest:96047.text: Camping 101: First Aid. This task directs novice medics in Dun Morogh to expand their survival craft beyond simple bandages. By seeking out Thamner Pol in Kharanos, adventurers learn how to assemble a dedicated First Aid Kit to keep campers alive in the field. Adventurers braving the frozen reaches of Dun Morogh quickly discover that linen scraps and hasty stitches are only the beginning of survival medicine. True wilderness survival often depends on having established supplies at a resting site. Those who show aptitude in basic treatment are steered toward local craft instructors in Kharanos who can teach them how to turn raw medical supplies into complete kits tailored for camp survival. In the bustling hamlet of Kharanos, Thamner Pol passes along practical techniques for outfitting expedition sites with emergency supplies. Knowing how to construct a proper field kit ensures that an entire party can bandage lacerations and recover their stamina together around the hearth fire before venturing back into the biting cold.

quest:96390.text: Nip 'Em in the Bud. Nip 'Em in the Bud is a mission directed by Earthseer Farsen to eliminate Dark Iron spies infiltrating Dun Morogh. The clandestine operatives have been spotted lurking near Ironband's Compound, threatening the security of the Bronzebeard homeland. Dun Morogh has long been a fortified sanctuary for the Ironforge dwarves, but the ancient enmity between the dwarven clans never truly sleeps. Dark Iron infiltrators have slipped through the high passes and snowy crags, skulking suspiciously close to vital excavations and settlements. Earthseer Farsen recognizes that even a few hidden observers can presage a devastating strike, calling on stalwart defenders of the Alliance to root them out before their schemes take hold.

quest:96392.text: Farsen's Watch. Farsen's Watch is an observational task given by Earthseer Farsen, a visiting Wildhammer shaman stationed high above Gol'Bolar Quarry. Using the earthseer's shamanic far sight, adventurers witness firsthand the growing infiltration of Dark Iron dwarves into the heart of Dun Morogh. This crucial survey marks an early step along the path toward the Hall of Thanes. Perched above the snowblown excavation of Gol'Bolar Quarry, Earthseer Farsen keeps a vigilant watch over the lower reaches of Dun Morogh. Having journeyed south from the crags of Aerie Peak, the Wildhammer visitor brings a keen spiritual awareness to lands usually patrolled by Ironforge mountaineers. Rather than relying on simple scouts, Farsen uses the traditional arts of his clan to monitor subterranean rumblings and unexpected movement along the hillsides. To convince travelers of the imminent danger, Farsen lends them his farsight—a shamanic gift that projects one's awareness across vast distances. Looking through the spiritual lens, it becomes obvious that Dun Morogh's troubles extend far beyond unruly troggs and wild beasts. Dark Iron dwarves have slipped close to Ironforge's industrial center, entrenching themselves for an operation that demands immediate confrontation before it takes root.

quest:96408.text: A Visitor to Dun Morogh. A Visitor to Dun Morogh is an investigative task offered by Beldin Steelgrill outside Kharanos. Mountaineers reported an unfamiliar campfire high on the cliffs overlooking Gol'Bolar Quarry, prompting a scout to check whether the stranger poses a threat to the local dwarves. Dun Morogh's mountaineers keep a diligent watch over the crags and snowy valleys surrounding Ironforge. When a campfire suddenly appeared high above Gol'Bolar Quarry, it raised eyebrows in Kharanos. Beldin Steelgrill, concerned by the unusual encampment situated directly above a vital dwarven excavation, recruits travelers to scale the ridges and determine whether the mysterious stranger is a benign traveler or an intruder.

quest:96607.text: The Great Outdoors. The Great Outdoors is an introductory survival lesson offered by seasoned travelers to newly minted wanderers across Azeroth. By taking a moment to rest by a warm campfire, fledglings learn how staying well-rested and prepared keeps an adventurer alive beyond city walls. It marks the first step into mastering wilderness survival and specialized field camps. No matter how sharp your blade or potent your magic, the wilds of Azeroth quickly whittle down anyone who neglects the basics of survival. Seasoned wanderers stationed near roadside clearings offer this simple lesson to travelers setting out from their home valleys. Taking time to rest by a campfire does more than ease sore boots—it settles the mind and readies the spirit for the harsh road ahead. Only those who master the discipline of regular rest and preparation stand a chance of surviving long enough to claim fortune and glory. Once an adventurer grasps the value of a crackling fire and proper rest, the instructors point them directly toward town tradesfolk. A camp in the field is rarely complete with just an ember and a bedroll; survival requires practical crafts. Whether forging replacement rivets, cooking trail rations, or stitching torn gear under the stars, every profession provides unique camp fixtures to turn a barren hillside into a self-sufficient outpost.

quest:96627.text: The Adventurer. The Adventurer is a breadcrumb assignment given by Marshal McBride in Northshire Valley. Recognising your early competence, McBride directs you beyond the cloistered abbey grounds toward Goldshire to look into a newcomer named Sam Sarsaparilla. Once recruits clear Northshire Valley of immediate threats like the local Defias and vermin, Marshal McBride begins looking down the road. With Stormwind's regular military presence stretched thin across the kingdom, the local garrison must rely on promising fighters to keep tabs on travelers and wanderers roaming the surrounding woods. Rather than a military order or a bounty hunt, McBride tasks you with an unusual errand: checking up on a specific new adventurer spotted near Goldshire named Sam Sarsaparilla. The request serves as a transition out of Northshire's secluded valley into the wider, more perilous expanse of Elwynn Forest.

quest:96628.text: The Adventurer. The Adventurer is a local errand given by Mountaineer Thalos at the southern gate of Dun Morogh. Before sending travelers through the mountain tunnel toward Kharanos, Thalos asks them to carry a bundle of supplies to Eric Brighthammer, a newcomer camped just outside the village. Guarding the high passes and tunnels between Coldridge Valley and the broader snowy expanses of Dun Morogh is demanding work for the Ironforge Mountaineers. Stationed at the border gate, Mountaineer Thalos keeps an eye out for both local dangers and travelers passing along the beaten trail. When word reaches the post about a lone adventurer arriving near Kharanos, Thalos uses trusted passersby to haul necessary supplies onward to support newcomers venturing into the frozen crags. The road descending from the southern pass winds into the settlement of Kharanos, the primary hub for dwarven craft and travel in central Dun Morogh. Eric Brighthammer has recently established himself just on the outskirts of the village. By delivering the Mountaineers' bundle of provisions to him, travelers help establish a vital link between the outlying ridge sentries and those actively wandering the wilderness.

quest:96630.text: The Adventurer. The Adventurer is a brief quest set in Teldrassil involving the discovery of a discarded journal in the wilds. The plain notebook recounts the humble travels and camping outings of an unknown traveler, intended for delivery to Lyreena Duskblade near Dolanaar. Amid the dense boughs and tangled roots of Teldrassil, travelers occasionally stumble across abandoned personal items. This simple journal recounts the unremarkable yet earnest wanderings of a nameless adventurer. Instead of grand heroics or perilous monster hunts, the bulk of its pages enthusiastically document the simple joys of making camp beneath the twilight canopy. Rather than leaving the personal keepsake to weather in the damp wilderness, the finder is drawn to carry it toward Dolanaar. Lyreena Duskblade, stationed near the night elf settlement, serves as the recipient for the displaced pages, perhaps offering closure or insight into whose travels were left behind.

quest:96638.text: The Adventurer. "The Adventurer" is an introductory journey quest on Zephras Isle. Given by Aetheen of the Gales in Thendal Grove, it directs newly seasoned wanderers southwest toward Shen'dar Village to meet Raan Wildwind, a veteran camper who knows the wilds. While Thendal Grove provides shelter and quiet refuge, the wider expanses of Zephras Isle remain wild and perilous. Aetheen of the Gales watches over the initiates and sees when an aspiring traveler is ready to step beyond familiar borders. For those seeking fame, fortune, or purpose, remaining behind the grove's sheltered perimeter is no longer enough. Southwest of the grove along the road toward Shen'dar Village, another traveler has already made his camp. Raan Wildwind has spent time navigating the perils outside the safe haven. Seeking him out provides burgeoning wanderers a pragmatic introduction to survival beyond Thendal Grove, learning from someone who has already braved the open paths.

quest:96652.text: The Adventurer. While exploring the rugged wastes of Durotar, travelers stumble across a plain, discarded journal chronicling the quiet travels of an unfamiliar figure. Its pages speak warmly of outdoor life and camping out under the stars, awaiting delivery to Brakk near Razor Hill. Durotar is a harsh land where survival usually takes precedence over leisurely travel, making the discovery of a wandering chronicler's book an unusual sight. Found lying unattended in the red dirt, the modest journal contains the musings and exploits of someone completely unknown to the common heroes of the Horde. Rather than detailing bloody battles or grand campaigns, its pages dwell on the humble joys of sleeping under the open sky and making camp in the wild. Whoever penned the entries left enough of an impression—or connection—to point toward Brakk, an adventurer camped near the settlement of Razor Hill. Carrying the personal effects of lost travelers to those who know the road is often the only way scattered wanderers are ever reunited with their belongings, or at least remembered by those watching the dusty roads.

quest:96656.text: The Adventurer. The Adventurer is an introductory task given by Executor Arren to seasoned young Forsaken champions outside Deathknell. Having proven reliable in strikes against the Scarlet Crusade, you are dispatched up the road toward Brill to investigate a stranger lingering near the settlement. Rather than uncovering another zealot spy, the task introduces you to Eleanor Shackleton, an independent traveler eager to teach the practical survival skills of the wild. Executor Arren maintains a vigilant watch over Deathknell and the surrounding approaches. With Scarlet Crusaders actively spying on the region and infiltrating northern Lordaeron, any newcomer spotted wandering near Brill warrants immediate scrutiny. Having demonstrated your dedication by eliminating crusader threats along the border, Arren turns to you to investigate the unknown figure quietly, determining whether she poses a hidden danger to the Forsaken. Upon tracking down Eleanor Shackleton along the roadside near Brill, her intentions prove far removed from Crusade fanatical plots or Scourge necromancy. A fellow Forsaken pausing before her next journey into the wilds, Eleanor is simply an adventurer. Instead, she recognizes the spark of an adventurer in those sent to check on her, offering to share the practical essentials of surviving open wilderness and making camp.

quest:96658.text: Camping 101: Cooking. Camping 101: Cooking teaches fledgling adventurers the essential art of starting a fire and preparing sustenance in the wild. Found across the starting settlements of both the Alliance and Horde, this lesson introduces the campfire as the core anchor for any makeshift outdoor campsite. To survive outside fortified walls, every traveler must know how to build a fire. Beyond boiling water and roasting meat, a basic campfire serves as the vital foundation for pitching a camp in uncharted terrain. A basic campfire anchors the campsite this lesson introduces. While apprentice cooks can only sustain a modest fire with minimal surroundings, mastering culinary arts unlocks the ability to kindle larger blazes capable of supporting more elaborate campsites. Furthermore, adventurers who branch out into other practical tradeskills discover ways to craft useful furnishings to complement their camps.

quest:96659.text: The Adventurer. As young tauren prepare to depart their ancestral training grounds on Red Cloud Mesa, Chief Hawkwind asks them to perform a final favor. He entrusts them with a bundle of essential supplies meant for Kaga Wildhoof, a seasoned wanderer camped near Bloodhoof Village who once aided the chief in his own past. Before travelers descend the mesa path toward the broader plains of Mulgore, Chief Hawkwind pauses to address unfinished personal debts. Long before guiding new generations of hunters and shamans on Camp Narache, Hawkwind crossed paths with Kaga Wildhoof. Described by the chief as an accomplished adventurer, Wildhoof provided vital aid when he needed it most. Hearing that she has pitched camp just outside Bloodhoof Village, Hawkwind uses the departure of newly proven novices to send provisions to his old benefactor. This errand marks a pivotal rite of passage for young Horde champions leaving Red Cloud Mesa. The trail down the plateau leads directly toward Bloodhoof Village, the cultural and logistical heart of central Mulgore. Carrying the supply bundle across the plains bridges the sheltered training life of the mesa with the wider, wilder struggles of the United Tauren Tribes.

quest:968.text: Tools of the Highborne. Tools of the Highborne is an Alliance quest offered by Thundris Windweaver in Auberdine. Travelers are dispatched south into the shattered ruins of Ameth'Aran to pry lingering magical relics from the hands of restless Highborne apparitions. The goal is simple: recover these ancient artifacts before their latent sorcery can unleash further harm upon Kalimdor. South of Auberdine, east of the coastal highway, lie the overgrown stone foundations of Ameth'Aran. Ten thousand years ago, this settlement served as a bastion for the Highborne—the privileged aristocracy of the ancient night elven empire. When their unchecked arcane dabbling culminated in the Sundering of the world, Ameth'Aran was shattered. Yet its inhabitants never truly departed. Sentinels patrolling Darkshore report that the ghosts of these aristocrats still haunt the sunken plazas, clutching the enchanted tools and trinkets they possessed in life. For modern kaldorei society, the arcane is not merely forbidden knowledge; it is an existential danger that nearly obliterated life on Azeroth. Thundris Windweaver recognizes that leaving these Highborne implements in ghostly hands leaves the doorway open to corruption. By dispatching adventurers to wrench these relics away from the restless spirits, Thundris intends to see them thoroughly destroyed, ensuring the dormant, tainted sorcery can never again fuel another disaster.

quest:97279.text: Wayward Weapons. Wayward Weapons is an early training task in the Valley of Trials, issued by the overseer Gornek. With young warriors arriving in droves to serve the Horde, armaments are running thin. To prove their discipline and support the encampment, recruits scour the scrubland to salvage gear abandoned by less capable predecessors. The Valley of Trials is the forge where raw recruits are tested against the harsh red wastes of Durotar. With countless aspirants stepping forward to pledge their blades to the warchief, the encampment's weapon stocks are strained to their limit. Weaponsmith Kzan Thornslash struggles to keep pace with demand, especially when early lessons prove fatal or humiliating for the unready. Overseer Gornek turns this shortage into a practical trial. Rather than wasting new metal, he directs fresh arrivals to recover the abandoned blades and blunt training weapons left behind by failed recruits who fell or fled in the dust. Delivering these recovered arms to Kzan allows the smith to repair and temper them for the next wave, teaching novitiates that survival in the Horde demands scavenging as well as swinging steel.

quest:97558.text: Hides for the Forsaken. A grim necessity of undead existence in Tirisfal Glades, where the Forsaken must scavenge animal hides to replace their decaying flesh. Shelene Rhobart tasks adventurers with gathering darkhound hides, duskbat wing membranes, and murloc skin to patch damaged bodies. Forsaken flesh does not heal naturally. Sustaining physical wounds leaves rotting gaps that cannot regenerate through normal biological means. To maintain their forms and keep their corpses functional, the Forsaken must source organic material from the living world and stitch replacement pieces over their injuries. Not every hide serves the same anatomical purpose. Thick darkhound hide offers durability for broad, sturdy repairs. Delicate duskbat wing membranes are light and pliable enough to cover faces and fingers without creating stiff, clumsy layers. Meanwhile, the pliable skin of Vile Fin murlocs is gathered to line internal membranes and sensitive areas such as inner cheeks and mouths.

quest:97919.text: Camping 101: First Aid. Camping 101: First Aid introduces fledgling adventurers in Elwynn Forest to the practical survival art of field medicine. It directs travelers to Michelle Belle in Goldshire to learn how to prepare a First Aid Kit for wilderness campsites. Adventurers traveling across Elwynn Forest quickly discover that combat and harsh wilderness survival take a heavy toll. While town healers and inns offer respite, journeying through dangerous territory often requires immediate, self-reliant care. Learning First Aid provides a practical remedy for bleeding and trauma, allowing travelers to mend wounds without relying on arcane rituals or holy supplication. A durable camp is more than a fire and a bedroll; it is a temporary haven against the dangers of the wilds. Through instruction from Michelle Belle at Goldshire's Lion's Pride Inn, skilled practitioners learn to assemble dedicated first aid kits. Having medical supplies on hand at camp ensures that a weary party can treat injuries and recover their strength before facing the perils ahead.

quest:97920.text: Camping 101: Fishing. Camping 101: Fishing introduces novice anglers in Elwynn Forest to the practical craft of wilderness survival and camp amenities. By seeking out local fishing expert Lee Brown near Goldshire, travelers can learn to apply their angling knowledge toward crafting cozy additions for a campsite, such as a decorative fish bowl that bolsters adventurers' spirits. While fishing is often considered a solitary pastime meant for quiet lakeshores and riverbanks, seasoned survivalists understand that camp life requires more than just food and shelter. Crafting comforting fixtures such as a fish bowl brings levity and morale to weary travelers resting between excursions, reinforcing the belief that a sound mind and high spirits foster formidable fighters. Stationed along the waters outside Goldshire, the seasoned angler Lee Brown assists novice fishermen who seek to expand their craft. Those who display sufficient proficiency with rod and line are directed to him to learn how simple catches and basic materials can be turned into functional campsite enhancements.

quest:97957.text: Camping 101: Herbalism. Camping 101: Herbalism directs budding herbalists to local profession trainers across Azeroth, such as Faruza in Brill, to master the craft of Incense Candles. These aromatic creations provide vital restorative aid to spellcasters resting in wilderness camps. While herbalism is commonly seen as the groundwork for alchemy, practical field survival relies just as heavily on gathered roots and blossoms. Experienced travelers point aspiring foragers toward regional master herbalists to learn how to prepare Incense Candles. In the Tirisfal Glades, Eleanor Shackleton directs promising foragers to visit Faruza in Brill once they demonstrate fundamental skill. Life on the road takes a heavy mental toll on spellcasters and spiritualists. Incense Candles release restorative fragrances meant to lift spirits and soothe weary minds. By infusing dried plants into candles, gatherers provide crucial aid to the healers and mages whose magical reserves falter during extended travel.

quest:97960.text: Camping 101: Skinning. Camping 101: Skinning is an introductory wilderness instruction given to novice gatherers in Tirisfal Glades and across Azeroth. It directs skinners who have practiced their trade to regional craftsmen to learn how to fashion a durable camp chair out of harvested hides. Survival in the wilds demands more than a sharp blade; it requires knowing how to husband your strength between trials. Adventurers like Eleanor Shackleton emphasize that harvesting beast pelts provides more than raw trade goods. By developing basic field proficiency, skinners can fashion essential camp comforts like chairs out of treated skins, allowing weary wanderers to rest and recover properly before their next perilous encounter. In Tirisfal Glades, young Forsaken skinners who reach initial competency are pointed toward Rand Rhobart, who plies his trade along the road linking Brill to the Capital ruins of the Undercity. Rhobart shares practical techniques for turning rough leather into functional campsite seating, an art mirrored by skinning masters throughout the lands of both the Horde and the Alliance.

quest:983.text: Buzzbox 827. Buzzbox 827 is the first in an experimental communication relay built by the gnome Wizbang Cranktoggle along the coastline of Darkshore. Plagued by breakdowns, these curious mechanical contraptions rely on an eccentric design that uses local wildlife parts for field repairs. Restoring the silent machine allows Wizbang to test his long-distance voice network directly from Auberdine. While visiting Auberdine, the eccentric gnomish engineer Wizbang Cranktoggle sought to bridge the long distances of the wild coast with a series of long-range acoustic relays called Buzzboxes. Designed to transmit voice over great distances, these lever-laden devices stand out starkly against the ancient ruins and somber forests of Darkshore. However, like many ambitious gnomish inventions, they suffer from chronic instability and require near-constant upkeep to keep their internal gears churning. Rather than hauling refined iron gears and copper pins across the wilderness, Wizbang adopted an unconventional solution: he built each Buzzbox to be serviced using components harvested from nearby native fauna. Buzzbox 827, stationed just south of Auberdine along the misty shoreline, was engineered to function with the sturdy, jointed legs of local tide and reef crawlers. Depositing the legs into the receiver hopper prompts the machine to self-assemble and jump back to life, broadcasting Wizbang's distant voice through its speakers.

quest:98389.text: A Light in the Darkness. Offered by Aramis Hammerhand in Deathknell, this quest tasks Forsaken adventurers with rescuing newly raised undead trapped in Night's Web Hollow. It highlights the delicate relationship between undead wielders of the Holy Light and a populace that deeply distrusts them. By aiding their fallen kin, these holy practitioners hope to prove their loyalty to Sylvanas and the Forsaken cause. The Holy Light is notoriously agonizing and hazardous to the undead, yet some Forsaken retain their connection to the sacred magic they wielded in life. In Deathknell, figures like Aramis Hammerhand strive to demonstrate that their faith has not turned them against their people. To combat the suspicion that holy practitioners will turn on other undead as monstrosities, they actively use their abilities and compassion to safeguard their kin. Northwest of Deathknell lies Night's Web Hollow, a dank cavern crawling with vicious spiders. Freshly raised undead, still disoriented by their awakening and lacking the wits to defend themselves, frequently stumble into the hollow and end up cocooned in sticky webbing. Rescuing these unfortunate Forsaken serves a dual purpose: saving new recruits for the Dark Lady and proving to leaders like Executor Arren that practitioners of the Light are devoted servants of the Forsaken.

quest:984.text: How Big a Threat?. How Big a Threat? is an Alliance quest given by Terenthis in Auberdine. Having witnessed furbolg madness taking root across Teldrassil, the night elf druid directs scouts to investigate local furbolg settlements in Darkshore to confirm whether the same dark taint has crossed the sea. The night elves of northern Kalimdor have long maintained cordial or peaceful relations with indigenous furbolg tribes. However, following the Third War, strange corruptions began unhinging furbolg minds in Teldrassil, resulting in violent kidnappings and feral attacks against their former allies. Stationed in Auberdine, the druid Terenthis fears that this sinister affliction is not isolated to the World Tree, but is actively spreading among the mainland tribes along the misty coasts of Darkshore.

quest:985.text: How Big a Threat?. How Big a Threat? is an Alliance quest offered by the night elf Terenthis in Auberdine. Having already scouted the hostile Blackwood furbolg camp south of town, adventurers are sent to cull the corrupted pathfinders and windtalkers before their frenzy threatens the settlement. Following initial scouting south of Auberdine, the Sentinels have determined that the Blackwood furbolgs pose an immediate danger to Darkshore's refugees and defenders. Terenthis tasks combat-capable travelers with striking directly at their camp, eliminating Blackwood Pathfinders and Windtalkers to break their offensive momentum. Night elves traditionally view furbolgs as spiritual kin and historic allies of the wilderness. However, the malignant spread of fel moss and demonic taint across northern Kalimdor has driven the Blackwood tribe mad. With no known remedy to restore the furbolgs' minds, the defenders of Auberdine view violence as a grim necessity to prevent innocent deaths.

quest:98576.text: Glyphic Parchment. Glyphic Parchment is an introductory summons directed to aspiring mages in the Valley of Trials. Delivered via Gornek, the written missive guides fledglings toward Mai'ah, a troll mage trainer stationed near the Den, to begin their arcane discipline. While new recruits prove their physical mettle against the local pests of Durotar, those possessing an affinity for the arcane cannot rely purely on brute force. Gornek passes along a written notice scribed with runes, instructing novice spellcasters to seek out Mai'ah, who oversees the early magical instruction of the Horde's newest recruits. Stationed just outside the entrance to the Den, Mai'ah tempers the ambitions of young spellweavers. Rather than recklessly hurling raw sorcery, she emphasizes patience, timing, and calculated intellect. Under her guidance, novices learn to view the cosmos as delicate strands to weave rather than an unruly tempest to unleash.

quest:98601.text: A Difficult Path. A Difficult Path marks the formal beginning of a Forsaken paladin's training in Deathknell. After dealing with the mindless undead rising from the crypts, newly awakened champions of the Light are directed to Aramis Hammerhand within the village church to confront the agonizing reality of wielding holy energy in undeath. When a freshly awakened Forsaken paladin finishes culling the feral undead outside the crypt, Shadow Priest Sarvis hands over an unexpected delivery. The Consecrated Scroll radiates holy energy so intensely that the shadow priest visibly recoils, bluntly asking the bearer to step aside. To a practitioner of shadow and decay, the very aura of the Holy Light feels like an open flame. Inside the desecrated church of Deathknell awaits Aramis Hammerhand, the Forsaken paladin trainer. Where other races wield the Light naturally and joyfully, undead who call upon it endure searing, visceral agony. Aramis makes no attempt to soften the blow: channeling holy power through a rotting vessel is sheer torment, but he demands his disciples embrace the pain rather than flinch away, using it as a crucible to temper their newfound resolve.

quest:99.text: Arugal's Folly. Arugal's Folly culminates in a dangerous investigation into the curse gripping Pyrewood Village. Dalar Dawnweaver tasks Horde operatives with obtaining enchanted shackles from the villagers to decode Archmage Arugal's twisted handiwork. Unraveling these bindings exposes the tragic magic holding the settlement under the shadow of the worgen. South of the Sepulcher lies Pyrewood Village, a settlement caught in an uncanny state of existence. Under the daylight sun, its residents go about their lives as ordinary human peasants, fearful and insular. Yet as twilight falls over the forest, their human forms tear apart into savage Moonrage worgen, roaming the streets under Arugal's sway. Dalar Dawnweaver seeks to unravel the exact arcane bindings causing this diurnal horror.

quest:99134.text: Discipline. Discipline is a task issued by Executor Zygand in Tirisfal Glades. Unimpressed by the competence of the local Deathguard garrison, Zygand commissions outside adventurers to administer physical punishment to slackening undead sentries. The Deathguard form the military spine of the Forsaken across Lordaeron, but freedom from the Lich King's iron will brings its own complications: apathy, fatigue, and negligence. Taskmasters like Executor Zygand have little patience for slackening discipline, especially with threats from the Scarlet Crusade and Scourge prowling Tirisfal's borders. To keep the troops sharp, officers rely on blunt instruments and aggressive oversight to maintain military readiness. Executor Zygand deliberately employs independent operators rather than ranks from within the garrison to administer his punishments. Using the Executor's Motivator, outsiders remind negligent Deathguards that survival in service to the Dark Lady requires absolute vigilance. Those who fail in their duties quickly learn that unlife offers no shelter from consequence.

quest:99141.text: Patience. Patience is a task assigned by Executor Zygand in Tirisfal Glades, demanding strict military accountability for the Dark Lady. With routine field reports overdue, Zygand dispatches an adventurer to collect updates from nearby Deathguards and an unusual sentry. The assignment highlights the rigorous, uncompromising discipline enforced across Forsaken holdings. Executor Zygand holds command over local security in Tirisfal Glades and tolerates no lapses in vigilance. To Zygand, serving Lady Sylvanas requires nothing less than absolute efficiency. When regular field dispatches fail to arrive at his post on schedule, he sees it as an unacceptable breach of duty rather than a minor delay. Rather than abandon his post to investigate, he sends incoming Forsaken agents to rein in delinquent subordinates and ensure that the borders remain secure. The dispatches involve sentries stationed at critical vantage points surrounding Brill. Deathguard Dillinger keeps watch over the graveyard to the west, where rogue undead and Scourge remnants often stir. To the east, Deathguard Kristof oversees a waystation guarding the approaches to the Capital City and the eastern roads. Most unusual among them is Gordo, a hulking abomination wandering near Stillwater Pond whose simple mind makes military record-keeping a deeply dubious expectation.

quest:99142.text: Tomb Weed. Tomb Weed is an alchemical quest assigned by Junior Apothecary Holland in Tirisfal Glades. Holland has been modifying wild doom weed and replanting it at the haunted Balnir Farmstead, cultivating a potent new specimen that unexpectedly attracts the local Scourge. Junior Apothecary Holland is not content simply harvesting native herbs for the Royal Apothecary Society; he harbors grand ambitions of his own. By gathering doom weed and subjecting it to minor alchemical alterations, he replanted the strains across the soil of the Balnir Farmstead to cultivate an evolved specimen he christened tomb weed. Holland views this hybrid flora as the centerpiece of his work and a herald of his personal destiny. While Holland anticipated alchemical potency, the transplanting of tomb weed into the Balnir Farmstead yielded an unforeseen side effect. The wandering Scourge remnants infesting the blighted fields have shown an uncanny, pervasive attraction to the burgeoning flora. Holland relies on passing travelers to push past these encroaching undead and harvest the matured crop so he can continue his experiments.

quest:99156.text: Rear Guard Patrol. Rear Guard Patrol is a critical defense assignment given by Deathguard Linnea in Tirisfal Glades. Rather than fighting off mere wandering ghouls, patrollers are tasked with hunting down Riptear, an abomination roaming near Venomweb Vale that should never have made it past the Bulwark. The Bulwark stands as the sole fortified barrier separating Tirisfal Glades from the horrors of the Western Plaguelands. The strategy of the Forsaken military hinges upon a strictly one-front war. If mindless undead slip behind the lines, the supply routes feeding the front can be strangled in an instant. While stray spirits or ghouls occasionally bypass the barricades, reports of an abomination roaming the glades signal a severe failure of containment.
